mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this is a decisive debate for the future of europe, both in the economic and social fields, with political consequences. the compromise solution between the main parliamentary groups seems to me to be balanced. it is important to exclude the application of the country of origin principle, as is the exclusion of temporary work in the health and other social fields, the services of general interest and the exclusion of lotteries. it is also essential that the criteria for economic services of general interest which are either completely excluded or included with the intervention of each member state are made very clear. as it is in the compromise, i naturally stress the importance of not interfering with the directive on the posting of workers. ladies and gentlemen, if progress is to be made towards the completion of the internal market in services, it is equally important to ensure conditions of fair competition in the various member states. breaking down bureaucratic or technically unjustifiable barriers but not facilitating social imbalances, in particular by not distorting labour markets or labour relations. this process of building the internal market in services, although very important for the economic development of europe, must respect the standards which guarantee european social cohesion. and if that was not the case with the initial version of the directive, we in the european parliament can now adopt a text which will contribute in a balanced and clear-cut way to the creation of a genuine european market in services, while at the same time ensuring european social cohesion. that takes both lucidity and courage.
the directive establishing the internal market in services was proposed by the european commission, chaired by the social democrat romano prodi, and maintained by the current commission, led by mr barroso. this is a proposal which plays a central role in the context of the offensive of capitalism in the european union. a proposal tailored to the interests of the large multinationals, which would obtain better conditions for exploiting workers and dominating new economic sectors. it advocates the total liberalization of services, including public services, with profound negative consequences for workers and for the sovereignty of states. if adopted, this proposal would act as a real 'trojan horse' against wages, collective labour agreements and labour rights and against the ability of a state to effectively protect public services and, in general, how services are provided. it is not possible to 'reform' this proposal, as the pse and the ppe want to do, by trying to safeguard the essential and negative elements of the directive while at the same time saving face. as the workers have demanded and we have advocated from the outset, it is necessary to reject it.
i voted in favour of this resolution because i defend freedom of expression as a european and universal value and i condemn violence as an expression of indignation against anyone, including embassies and european interests. i voted in favour because the condemnation of incitement to religious hatred and the dissemination of racist and xenophobic attitudes is contained in the second paragraph of the resolution. however, i think that this resolution as a whole is unbalanced, because it focuses on freedom of expression and not on the islamophobic intention behind the cartoons published by a racist and xenophobic far-right newspaper in denmark. the defence of freedom of expression and the most fundamental human rights requires that this parliament explicitly distance itself from islamophobia and condemn any attempts to conflate the islamic religion and its followers as a whole with terrorism. in voting in favour of this resolution i also wanted to express my solidarity with the danish people, but i do not support the dismissive and arrogant attitude of the government of prime minister andreas fogh rassmussen, which i consider to be partly responsible for the exploitation of this incident by the extremist reactionary forces which, both in the west and in the islamic world, are inciting the 'clash of civilizations'.
i would like to say that i am very pleased that the european parliament has been able to take part in the debate on the report. it is an ignorant and arrogant regime, as evidenced by the statements of its president on the holocaust. not even le pen would do better. it is still a reactionary and fundamentalist regime, which violates human rights on a daily basis. and finally, it is a dangerous and adventurous regime. he's betting his survival on enriching uranium that puts him on the doorstep of the club of countries with nuclear weapons. we agree: europe must do everything but war to prevent tehran from acquiring nuclear weapons. that is why we do not agree with the proposed resolution, particularly paragraph 7. the passage of the iranian issue to the un security council is a wrong and irresponsible step as it brings the world closer to a new preventive war, now in the form of surgical military intervention. europe has an alternative to escalation: it can and must turn what is today a problem into an extraordinary opportunity for humanity and the iranian people. i remind you and read article 6 of the nuclear non-proliferation treaty: each of the parties to the treaty assumes responsibility for the continuation of negotiations for an end to the nuclear arms race and for a treaty aiming at total and complete disarmament under international control. it is here, not in war, that we must begin. the union states which have signed the treaty have in their hands an opportunity to reverse the hidden logic of arms in the negotiations with iran. the european union must not be allowed to continue to be a mere spectator, but a spectator of the world.
mr president, despite international efforts it is increasingly clear that either iran is raising its bargain, or it is not sincerely interested in stopping the process of enriching uranium and its subsequent military use. iran is now a state that does not respect the rules of the international community, that does not appear to intend to respect them, and that presents itself as a threat to regional and world security. today's iran is a potential danger. tomorrow's iran with nuclear weapons is a certain danger. in this context, citizens expect the european union to be a guarantee of their security and a factor of stability in the world. the answer to the citizens' aspirations must be given, first and foremost, by those who have taken on the task of leading the negotiations with iran in the face of the risk, certainly calculated, that iran will not want to comply with the legitimate demands of the international community. mr president, simply referring the matter back to the united nations and the security council is not, in my view, sufficient. in our view, the first task of the european union must be to help keep the international community united and firm in the face of the threat posed by iran, both to the region and to the world. indeed, we cannot allow the difficulties and the politically sensitive moment we face to generate divisions when our own global security is at stake. iran must know that the diplomatic path is not closed, but that it is up to it to restore confidence through concrete, verifiable acts of total suspension of its uranium enrichment and reprocessing activities. it must also abandon provocative discourse on israel and the holocaust and commit itself to a policy of respect for human rights and opposition acceptable to the international community. but what are the right and effective measures to achieve these objectives? this is the fundamental question we must answer. mr president, the relevance and international role of the european union depend increasingly and above all on its action. we hope that this moment, which is a particularly grave moment, will enable the european union to demonstrate that it is in a position to play its role on a world scale, a role which has been called for many times in this parliament. we want you to succeed.
in writing. the title of this resolution, which was approved by a majority of meps, is clear as to its real purpose: to support the recent escalation and worsening of the situation with regard to iran's nuclear programme. the european parliament has voted in favour of the amendments tabled by the committee on foreign affairs, security and defence policy, which call for a peaceful political settlement of the dispute over iran's nuclear programmes and reaffirm its opposition to any military action or threat of use of force, stressing that an escalation of the dispute would lead to a deepening of the crisis in the region. the same applies to other amendments calling on 'all countries to refrain from any threat to the territorial integrity of iran and to distance themselves unequivocally from any pre-emptive attack'. the majority of meps, instead of supporting measures that would promote the de-escalation of international relations, support the un security council monitoring the situation. this is a longstanding demand of the united states, which is seeking to use this measure to isolate iran internationally and to pseudo-legitimize new interventions and dangerous military adventures in order to impose its dominance in the region and defend its economic interests. that is why we are voting against it.
the report by mr friedrich-wilhelm graefe zu baringdorf, on behalf of the committee on agriculture and rural development, on the management of risks and crises in the agricultural sector [2005/2053 (ini) ] (a6-0014/2006) follows.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, it is well known that agriculture is subject to serious risks and crises, which have actually intensified in recent years, both for climatic reasons and natural disasters such as floods, droughts and fires, and also because of epizootic diseases and their international spread. although the commission presents various options for managing risks and crises, its proposals do not take account of the difficult situation facing small and mediumsized farmers and family farming today, who are threatened by an unfair common agricultural policy and by the negotiations within the world trade organisation, which are contributing to the destruction of thousands of small farms, the strangulation of the rural world and the desertification of vast areas of the interior of countries such as portugal, which is also reflected in the increase in forest fires. in its proposal, the european commission, in addition to insisting on the co-financing of natural disaster insurance premiums paid by farmers, proposes funding on the basis of only 1% of the modulation, which is clearly insufficient. what is needed is, as we have proposed, the creation of a public insurance funded by the european union so that there are better framework conditions for risk management and crisis prevention, which is fundamental for family farming. the commission's proposals do not sufficiently take account of the risks and possibilities of crisis, as the rapporteur points out, and it is therefore essential that the commission should make a more precise assessment of the instruments and measures which are likely to prevent price falls, market crises and loss of income for farmers and which are capable of ensuring the continuation of their activity. i note the willingness expressed here by the commissioner to take account of the positions taken in this debate, and i look forward to seeing them translated into practice in the work that will follow, both in relation to the management of risks and crises in agriculture and in the creation of a safety net with regard to the forthcoming reforms of the common market organisations, particularly for wine, fruit and vegetables. however, it should also provide for the possibility of granting aid for the purchase of fuel by farmers when fuel prices are excessively high.
mr president, commissioner, the last few years, and the last year in particular, have been a vivid illustration of the variety of risks and crises facing european farmers. in 2005, while thousands of hectares of forest were destroyed by fire, with loss of human life, and drought was severely affecting several areas of southern europe, several countries in central europe were hit hard by devastating floods. in either case, of equivalent historically unprecedented dimensions. on the other hand, both animal diseases and the inevitable liberalization of trade expose farmers in particular to new risks and uncertainties. the commission's initiative which is the basis of this report is therefore welcome. it is, however, far behind the real needs. i therefore support the rapporteur in most of his comments and suggestions, particularly as regards agricultural insurance and mutual funds, but i regret the timidity - and i use this term to be rather delicate - of his approach to covering income crises, especially when some of our most important commercial competitors have security devices to deal with them. i also see this report as an important part of the broader approach that the subject deserves, particularly in the debate that is taking place on the solidarity fund, as well as the forestry strategy that we will certainly be discussing, and the own-initiative reports on natural disasters that are being drawn up by various committees of this parliament. i hope that parliament will adopt coherent positions on this set of instruments. this will be the best contribution that can be made to the union's urgent need to provide itself with the appropriate instruments for protecting its farmers, first of all to prevent crises and risks from occurring, but also to remedy them if they cannot be avoided.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on thursday at 10 a.m.
the report by mr heinz kindermann, on behalf of the committee on agriculture and rural development, on the implementation of the european union forestry strategy [2005/2054 (ini) ] (a6-0015/2006) is reproduced below.
on behalf of the pse group. commissioner, we all know that it is commonplace to talk about the economic, social and environmental importance of european forests. however, it is never too much to remember that they occupy 35% of the territory, represent almost 3.5 jobs, 15 million owners and the value of production of more than 350 billion euros. these are therefore indicators which illustrate the importance of the subject and the importance which the community institutions must attach to it, especially at a time when various factors, whether arising from natural causes or human action, are threatening the forest, in a particularly complex international context which calls for a new and urgent approach from the european union to the energy question, where biomass can and must play a relevant role, as the commission and the austrian presidency have recognized in giving priority to this issue. i therefore welcome the commission's communication on the implementation of the strategy and welcome the report by mr kindermann, with whom i largely identify, which is an excellent contribution by parliament to the formulation of the european forestry strategy, as well as some amendments which i think can improve and complete the report. the recognition of the vulnerabilities of the forest, which the report identifies well, is a good contribution to the debate we are having at the moment on natural disasters and therefore the integrated approach to this very important subject, which i hope the commission will welcome and, like us, see the problem as a whole, so that the contributions of these various instruments now on the political agenda can help to improve the situation of european forests.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, the unquestionable need for forest maintenance and the preservation of its multifunctional character require effective management and support measures that take into account the different forests and their specific problems. i do not think it is necessary to insist on a uniform interpretation of the concept of forest when we know that there are already internationally agreed and negotiated definitions which are the basis for the production of periodic reports and assessments of the state of forests in europe and the world. while we are certainly in favour of a european union action plan for sustainable forest management, we have not followed up on several of the proposals in the report now under discussion. we regret that several of the proposals we made in the committee on agriculture to draw attention to the situation of forests in the southern european countries, which are faced annually with fires, sometimes accompanied by drought, as happened in portugal last year, where some 300 000 hectares of forest were burned at very high cost and with serious consequences for forests, biodiversity, farmers and the populations of vast areas. we therefore insist on the need for a real medium- and long-term forest fire prevention strategy and for a specific regulation and a specific budget line in the community budget to protect forests against fires, taking into account resolutions already adopted by the european parliament and the experience of the specific community regulation that already existed and which, unfortunately, has been abolished by the commission. we also believe that the next action plan should cover seven years to correspond to the period of the next financial perspective and include a programme for the protection of the horse breed which recognises its multi-functionality and its contribution to livestock rearing and cork production, which is of fundamental importance for the development of large areas in the southern countries. we hope that the executive committee will take account of these proposals, which we are once again advocating here and which the report does not contain, so that the action plan can be a positive instrument in the defence and promotion of the various forests, including those in the southern countries with climatic conditions conducive to forest fires.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the european commission report we are examining here today sets out the main conclusions of the analysis of the implementation of the european forestry strategy and the emerging problems affecting the forestry sector, and outlines possible actions for the future. experience has shown that the forestry sector can contribute to the lisbon strategy objectives of sustainable economic growth and competitiveness and also to the gothenburg objectives of safeguarding the quantity and quality of europe's natural resources. the commission proposes the development of a european action plan for forest management which could provide a coherent framework for the implementation of forestry measures and thus allow the many potential resources of this sector in europe to be further developed. however, the treaty establishing the european union does not provide a legal basis for a common forestry policy and the effects of the community's sectoral forestry policies, as well as the lisbon and gothenburg strategies, are still not sufficiently effective in combating forest degradation. i would remind you of the tragedy of the forest fires and drought that have plagued southern europe in recent years, of which portugal is unfortunately a particular example. i understand that this situation may not be a remote problem for many of you, but i would like to draw your attention to the great difficulties facing the forestry sector in this southern part of europe and all the citizens who depend on it. this problem, given its seriousness, must be tackled as a matter of priority and a serious and thorough approach must be taken. a common forestry policy is more important than ever. i therefore believe that the member states should start to reflect in depth on the environmental, social and economic advantages of introducing a common policy in the context of the future constitution. that is why i ask for support for amendments nos 7, 8 and 9, which have been signed by myself and by my colleague mr herranz garcia, among others.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on thursday at 10 a.m. the competent authority shall inform the applicant of the reasons for the refusal.
the following is the report by mrs mairead mcguinness, on behalf of the committee on agriculture and rural development, on the proposal for a council decision on community strategic guidelines for rural development (programming period 2007-2013) (com (2005) 0304 - c6-0349/2005 - 2005/0129 (cns)) (a6-0023/2006).
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on thursday at 10 a.m.
in writing. the former bolkenstein directive was radically transformed and made clear progress in the construction of an internal market for services. we therefore voted in favour of this proposal, in its revised form, because we believe that it guarantees a balanced progress towards the creation of a european internal market in services and that the exclusion of services of general interest, lotteries and essential health areas will lead to a better balance in the directive. in its present formulation, the directive is positive for the portuguese economy, in particular by no longer applying the principle of the country of origin. the opening up of the european services market will create many jobs. with this text the so-called "social dumping" will be definitively removed. the directive reduces unjustifiable bureaucratic barriers in various member states by making the provision of services subject to the rules of the country in which the service is provided. the exclusion of temporary work and non-interference with the posting of workers directive are also important to ensure social balance and cohesion. all these arguments helped to consolidate our vote.
in writing. we regret that our proposal to reject the bolkestein directive, the central point of the lisbon strategy and the cornerstone of neoliberalism in the service sector, which is designed to serve the interests of the economic and financial groups in the european union, has not been adopted, as is shown by the positions of their representative organisations, in particular unice. it is true that the struggles of the workers and the people have forced some concessions and adjustments, which, when they were positive, had our support, but the regrettable agreement of the pse with the ppe has frustrated the expectations of all those who hoped that the european parliament would be able to reject such a serious proposal for the workers and the peoples of the various member states. we therefore voted against the overall proposal and many of its sub-aspects, which we regarded as negative, in particular the following aspects: - the liberalization of services in general, including in sensitive areas of public services and sectors such as water services, social housing, energy services, postal services, research, education and training, cultural services and security services, where our proposals to remove them from the scope of the directive were rejected; - the fragility of the situation for the recruitment of workers, including self-employed workers; - the worsening of the difficulties in defending the rights of consumers, users of public services and the environment.
in writing. the majority of the ep approved the compromise of the pse/epp, which sought to save essential aspects of the proposal for a directive on the liberalisation of services, rather than reject it, as had been proposed by us. as a result of the firm denunciation of the most negative aspects of this proposal and the struggle of workers to reject the directive, the majority of the european parliament excluded some services from its scope by referring them to a later decision and concealed, in an exercise of legal juggling, the rule of application of the law of the country of origin of the service provider. however, while not all of the ambitious goals of the large economic and financial groups have been achieved, a step forward has been made in the deepening of competition in numerous service sectors, including public services, which will have negative consequences for workers' rights and the services provided to the population. the same is true of further limitations on the sovereignty of states, by strengthening the role of the european court of justice. but the directive on the liberalization of services has not yet been adopted. the council, on which the portuguese government is seated, will have to assume its responsibilities. we will continue to fight for the rejection of this proposal for a directive, which, if adopted, will call into question the interests of workers and the country.
in writing. the decision that a service provider is free to offer its services in any other member state without unusual barriers being imposed on it is in the interests of consumers, workers, service providers and the interests of europe. the services market has the greatest potential for growth and development in the european economy, and our aim is to promote reforms that stimulate the economy by defending the rights of workers, consumers and entrepreneurs, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises, which are traditionally more vulnerable to administrative, political and economic barriers. i have approved this report because it is in favour of genuine freedom of establishment and freedom to provide services in the eu. if it is possible to acquire goods and services freely in another member state, there is no justification for preventing the service provider from moving, provided that a set of principles, which are of a public and social nature, are respected, and that these principles are safeguarded in the adopted version. despite the commitment - necessary in a political group with the responsibilities of the epp - the result is balanced and, above all, a clear sign that the majority of the european parliament wants an economy with more jobs, more efficient, fair and competitive.
in writing. the proposal for a directive on the liberalization of services is the culmination of an intention that has been in place for nearly 50 years, since it is one of the european union's overriding aims that freedom of services is at the heart of the european project. the solution adopted is a victory for european democracy and resolves a stalemate which until recently was thought to be insurmountable. without this understanding, we would be in a situation where in the coming years nobody would dare to intervene in this matter, with the consequent damage to economic growth and job creation. the fact that a whole series of administrative and bureaucratic barriers to the free movement of persons and service-providing enterprises have been removed makes the adoption of this directive worthwhile. the small and mediumsized enterprises will therefore be the main beneficiaries, since the frustration they felt when they wanted to operate in a neighbouring country will be over. often they had to be resident in the country of destination, or have an open office or a branch, or have previously registered with any administrative authority, or had to prove that they had mastered the language of that country, etc. now, with this directive, all that ends.
in writing. we have voted in favour of this report because we consider its content to be generally positive, although we disagree with some of the particular aspects. however, as a whole, it seeks to respond to problems felt in the rural world, in particular by pointing out that rural areas are disadvantaged and require particular attention, emphasising the great diversity of situations and the specificities prevailing in each member state. thus, special attention is needed in remote rural areas, in mountainous and disadvantaged areas, with problems of depopulation and decline, but also in peri-urban areas, which are subject to increasing pressures from urban centres. it also stresses the inclusion of proposals to encourage existing initiatives at local level, such as farmers' markets and local supply programmes for quality food products, and the need for effective support for young farmers to ensure a generational renewal. specific treatment should be given to the outermost regions, where agricultural holdings are characterised by isolation, small size and low production diversification, and are sometimes affected by severe climatic conditions.
in writing. the community strategic guidelines for rural development will serve as the basis for future national rural development programmes, harmonising the objectives and measures to be implemented in this important european sector. it is of the utmost importance that strategies are fully and rigorously defined to promote the development of european rural areas, the improvement of the living conditions of their populations and the improvement of the rural environment. i think the european commission's proposal is very positive because it presents a very diverse range of objectives and measures, as does the report by mrs mcguinness, which improves the strategic guidelines in several specific areas such as the protection of rural culture and the preservation of the rural landscape.
in writing. under the new rural development regulation, it is planned to adopt community strategic guidelines for the next financial period 2007-13. the importance of rural development policy should be stressed, given that rural areas account for 90% of the eu's territory and are home to 50% of its population. these strategic guidelines aim to define the areas where community funding can create the greatest added value at eu level, translate the eu's main priorities into rural development, ensure coherence of programming with other eu policies and support the implementation of the new cap and the necessary restructuring in the new and old member states. like the rapporteur, i support this proposal for a decision which responds to the need to give the member states clearer guidance on the application of the regulation. however, special emphasis should still be placed on the need to modernise the agricultural and forestry sectors and to encourage young farmers and their families to remain in rural areas.
in writing. despite the inclusion in this resolution of aspects which raise serious questions for us, we have supported the resolution in its most positive sense. however, it is not with palliative measures of limited and more than doubtful reach that the millennium development goals will be met: eradicating extreme poverty and hunger, achieving universal primary education, promoting gender equality and empowering women, reducing child mortality, improving maternal health, combating hiv/aids, malaria and other diseases, ensuring environmental sustainability and creating a partnership for development. the achievement of these just and urgent objectives requires a profound change in the current policies promoted by the major capitalist powers and the world forums they dominate, such as the world bank or the imf. it demands an end to capitalist competition, trade liberalisation, privatisation, the reduction of workers' rights and wages, the control of state policies by the big economic and financial groups and the concentration of wealth in the hands of the few at the expense of the exploitation and oppression of the people. the achievement of these aims requires, after all, the overcoming of the system - capitalism - which engenders exploitation, inequality, poverty, violence and oppression.
in writing. we note with deep concern the alignment of the majority of the european parliament on the increase in international tension and the concealment of the deeply provocative character of the publication of the cartoons, as the dangerous development of events has shown. it is unacceptable to try to justify the escalation of us intervention in the middle east by creating a false environment of clash of civilizations. how worrying it is to see the major powers of the eu converging on the us ambitions for this region. it should be stressed that it is germany, france and the united kingdom which are taking the initiative in trying to block a negotiated solution by the international atomic energy agency on iran, a goal long sought by the united states. contrary to what some would have you believe, the threat to peace, the war, the aggression and the occupation have been carried out by the us and its allies, namely israel. these are the ones who are militarily occupying afghanistan, iraq or palestine. as is the us which has numerous bases and thousands of troops stationed in the region. action is therefore urgently needed to break the current escalation of incitement to violence and to promote the de-escalation of international relations and the defence of peace.
in writing. the society we are proud to live in has made freedoms its essence. our first definition is to be free and therefore responsible. in these recent events, what was at issue was not the exercise of freedom of expression, but an unacceptable reaction on the part of those who claimed to be offended. if all indignation is legitimate, not all means of expressing it are. it is against these excesses, against the attacks on the member states of the european union, that we must first speak out. we reject violence, we stand in solidarity with denmark and the other member states. having said that, it is necessary to add that we know very well that these demonstrations were orchestrated, but we also know that their impact on relations between the west and the islamic world was great. apart from our freedoms, including freedom of expression, all displays of hatred, all promotion of racism and xenophobia are reprehensible and all freedom must be exercised responsibly, at this time or any other. we will not relent in defending our right to be free, but we will not seek confrontation, on the contrary, we will avoid it because we know that the peace and security of the world depend, in large measure, on our sense of responsibility.

madam president, mr vice-president frattini, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by congratulating commissioner frattini on his attention to human trafficking. it is indeed one of the most revolting expressions of international crime. it constitutes a serious abuse of human rights and of immigration and labour laws and is a crime that seriously affects both national and international security. this type of crime has been growing at an alarming rate, and according to un figures it has even become the third most lucrative activity for organised crime. this is a transnational phenomenon and has become a major concern for many countries, whether they are countries of origin, transit or destination. a global and coordinated response is therefore needed, which should involve stepping up efforts at both legislative and operational levels. the adoption in 2002 of the framework decision approximating the criminal laws and penalties of the member states and allowing a judge in a member state to issue a european arrest warrant for criminals involved in trafficking in human beings was important in the legislative field. this framework decision should have been transposed by the beginning of august 2004. we are still waiting for a report on the evaluation of the measures taken by the member states and whether or not they have been implemented by all the member states. as regards the operational plan, i believe that it is particularly important to strengthen the role of europol, which is underused, that we need a global and rapid response capacity to support victims, which can protect them through immediate assistance, and that we need to improve the exchange of information and statistical data, to which the commissioner referred in his initial speech.
madam president, mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, human trafficking is a scourge that must be fought by all means. every year more than 700,000 women and children are caught in trafficking networks. in europe alone, 100 000 women are trafficked annually and subjected to practices that undermine their physical integrity and mental health. trafficking in women and children is the fastest growing criminal activity and is known to increase during major sporting events. trafficking in women is associated with illegal immigration. thousands of poor women are lured by the promise of decent, well-paying employment and then are thrown into prostitution. in view of all the above, the commission has a good opportunity, on the pretext of the world cup, to wage an exemplary fight against the trafficking and sexual exploitation of women and to put in place rapid and effective measures to support victims, in particular programmes for the social inclusion and rehabilitation of women, as well as legal, medical, psychological and translation assistance.

on behalf of the gue/ngl group, exactly three years ago, following protracted struggles by workers in defence of jobs and the viability of companies such as cg & clark in portugal, parliament adopted on 13 march 2003 a resolution with a set of recommendations on the closure of companies which have benefited from community funding. after three years, what has the european commission done to put these recommendations into practice? what steps have you taken to make community aid conditional on long-term agreements on employment and local development? has the commission made available the record of contractual breaches by companies which have relocated and which have benefited directly or indirectly from public incentives? how many times has the commission refused to grant or demanded the reimbursement of community funding to undertakings which have not fully complied with contracts? what concrete measures has the commission taken to support workers and the economic recovery of regions affected by relocations? has the commission drawn up the proposed code of conduct to prevent the relocation of companies? the answer to these questions is clearly given in this report, which, after three years, again lists the same recommendations to the european commission. in general, companies that relocate are characterized by an investment which, by ensuring that they obtain the most varied public incentives and support and the exploitation of cheap and unqualified labour, seeks to obtain high profits in a short period of time until, finding a more profitable alternative, they relocate, sometimes without even fulfilling the commitments they have made and ignoring the extremely serious social and economic damage they cause. the relocation of companies actually works as a permanent blackmail on workers, as pressure to reduce wages, to increase working hours, to increase labour flexibility, basically to reduce their rights. we therefore propose the adoption of an appropriate legal and regulatory framework to combat the relocation of companies so that in three years' time we will not have to have the same debate.
mr president, commissioner dimas, ladies and gentlemen, i too would like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur on his excellent work. in recent years, as has already been mentioned, there has been an increase in natural disasters as a result of climate change, environmental damage, land use change, etc. to respond quickly and effectively to major emergencies, the european union has a set of instruments, such as this regulation, among others, which it has been perfecting. the serious natural disasters that occurred in the summer of 2005, with major floods in central europe, severe droughts in southern europe and fires that destroyed thousands of hectares of forest in my country, portugal, and also in spain, call for appropriate and rapid prevention and civil protection measures. in the working meetings with the local, regional and national authorities of the six countries affected by natural disasters which i visited as rapporteur for the committee on the environment's own-initiative report on natural disasters, it was emphasized that, in order to serve the people, the community's emergency response instruments must be simplified and the rules for applying the regulations more flexible, that is to say simplified and flexible, and in addition, it was recommended that coordination at european level be strengthened and, of course, that financial appropriations be increased.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, this report tackles one of the main problems facing the european union today, with serious repercussions in the worsening of unemployment, economic and social inequalities and the abandonment of vast regions, blocking their development. we believe it is essential that business restructuring should only take place when it is necessary to save jobs and ensure the development of businesses and never just to increase profits at the expense of redundancies or for purely financial and speculative reasons, as is increasingly the case. we therefore insist on the need for strict regulations against such restructuring, which leads to unemployed investment and is accompanied by the dismissal of thousands of workers. the commission has also proposed that the new regulations should ensure that the granting of aid is accompanied by the obligation to maintain employment with rights and regional development in the medium term, without which they cannot receive any support. we therefore insist on the need to ensure that workers, through their representatives, in particular the european works councils, have the right to intervene in the whole process, including the right of veto, and we therefore call for this directive on european works councils to be revised.
in writing. we voted in favour because we think it is important to set up a european institute for gender equality, but we stress that it is essential that it should not be limited to studies, analyses and statistics, as important as all of this is. it must develop cooperation and dialogue with ngos and bodies specialised in the field of equal opportunities, both at national and european level and with third countries, and support measures and actions aimed at ending discrimination. it is also necessary to analyse and monitor the development of the integration of the gender equality dimension into all the policies and the budgetary process of the european union, in particular with regard to the evaluation of the impact of relevant national community policies on men and women, as we proposed and which, unfortunately, was not adopted. finally, we hope that adequate community funding will be secured and that there will be good sense in the appointment of its future administrative board.
in writing. the quasi-police of opinions and the quasi-establishment of single thoughts have turned serious and relevant debates addressing issues of concern into exercises of faith-confirmation in certain policies. this is clearly the case with so-called gender policies. the recognition of the need for a more balanced society, with a more modern division of labour between men and women and greater freedom of choice, is too often replaced by the imposition of policies which are supposed to achieve these aims. as if there were areas of policy where disagreement on method and models was impossible. in summary, this is the basis of my first objection to the idea of an institute for equality between men and women within the european union. the fact that i advocate, as i said above, the need for greater balance in the organization of our societies does not lead me to advocate the creation of such an institute. bureaucratizing freedom doesn't seem like a good way to go. not all methods are good for the realization of a just design. the proliferation of agencies and institutes does not seem to me to be a suitable model for the organization of the community institutions.
in writing. the recent natural disasters, such as floods, extreme drought and forest fires, which have affected not only countries in the european union but also outside it (tsunamis in asia, cyclones in the usa), demonstrate the importance of effective civil protection mechanisms. the commission's proposed high-urgency preparedness and response instrument is designed to strengthen the eu's response capacity in the context of the civil protection mechanism and to maximise assistance in terms of preparedness and rapid response to major emergencies. however, it does not deal with the question of prevention. we therefore consider it important that this report be adopted, which emphasizes this issue by proposing that it be included in the scope of the application of this instrument. we also stress the proposals for integrated management of natural and environmental resources, including the management of forests, areas most prone to flooding, wetlands and other fragile ecosystems and risk assessment in urban areas, the call for special attention to be paid to isolated and outermost regions, greater information and awareness-raising among the population and greater and better training of professionals.
in writing. the text proposed by the commission offers good prospects for civil protection at european level. the measures and actions for which this instrument can be activated will bring great benefits in preparing for and responding to crisis situations. with the amendments tabled by parliament, the prevention of these phenomena is also given a place in the instrument, which seems to be essential in the fight against such important objectives as the protection of people, the environment and property. in a country like portugal, which is plagued every year by forest fires and droughts that leave irreparable marks, this proposal will allow the training of specialised staff, preparation mechanisms and the sharing of equipment and best practices with more developed countries in this field. i therefore agree with mr papadimoulis' report and the amendments to the commission's text.
in writing. we naturally follow the proposals made in the report to introduce and enhance the prevention dimension within this instrument as a key factor in reducing disaster risks, or to enhance the international role of the un in managing relief and aid to the population, or to introduce the protection of public health and cultural heritage, among other aspects. but the debate on solidarity between countries in the event of a catastrophe also helps to highlight (if not to denounce) the unacceptable waste of resources in the arms race and the militarization of international relations by the major capitalist powers, with the united states as their main promoter. what could not be done with the colossal financial resources of militarization and war in the context of prevention, relief and immediate response, as well as the recovery of regions affected by disasters? how many lives, how much suffering, how much destruction of economic, social and environmental resources could be avoided if a policy of de-escalation of international relations, peaceful settlement of conflicts, disarmament and effective mutually beneficial cooperation between the different countries and peoples were pursued?
in writing. the european union has responded positively and in a spirit of solidarity to requests for assistance sent by member states in cases of serious emergencies. however, recent major disasters such as the extreme droughts and fires in portugal and spain have shown that strengthening the community civil protection mechanism should be an immediate objective before new emergencies occur. the text clearly improves on the commission proposal in extending the scope of the regulation and increasing the funding for prevention, preparedness and assistance in the event of disasters. the question of marine pollution is added, because we have to recognize that a coastal state alone cannot deal with an environmental emergency caused by a large-scale oil spill that hits its coast. we are also an open union with policies of international solidarity. we must do what we can when other peoples are affected by serious emergencies, but we must not forget that the main objective is to strengthen mutual aid between the member states of the union. in short, these measures will enable us to respond more adequately to requests for aid, and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the imf is one of the bretton woods institutions which, along with the world bank and gatt/wto, helped to settle the development inequalities between the capitalist centre and the capitalist periphery, not only by facilitating and promoting the liberalization of trade in goods and services, but also by promoting the prevailing liberal ideology, in particular with recommendations on the reduction of the role of the state, privatisations, labour flexibility, among others, which we can now find in the so-called 'lisbon strategy'. through structural adjustment plans they are trying to adapt the economies of the southern countries to the so-called market and competitive economy, by opening up to foreign investment and opening the door to models of economic specialization that favour the centre. the disastrous economic and social consequences of these plans are well known. even the famous stabilization they claim to be aiming for is not only not happening, but today the international monetary system is more unstable and the occurrence of financial crises is increasing. we need another monetary system, based on the un, based on mutual benefit and the promotion of development. the reform of the imf, even if it is based on a greater participation of developing countries, which is not the case, does not change its nature. that is why we abstained.
in writing. the resolution which the european parliament adopted on the relocation of companies was the resolution that was possible because the compromise between the dominant political forces in the ep - social democracy and the right - refused a more consequential resolution by rejecting the amendments which we have tabled to:- denounce that companies that relocate generally aim at maximum profit, ensuring that they obtain tax incentives and financial support, exploiting a cheap and unrighteous labour force; - denounce the fact that relocations are part of the liberalisation of trade and the deregulation of the labour market worldwide, in particular in the wto; - to create a legal and regulatory framework which, inter alia, includes: the contractual definition of a period of at least seven years guaranteeing the creation of stable and lasting employment and the economic development of the regions, provides for penalties to be applied in the event of non-compliance with contractual obligations (refund of the aid granted and prohibition of new community aid) and guarantees the protection of workers by ensuring their information and decisive intervention, including the right of veto; - to draw up an annual communication on relocations and their consequences. in the meantime, we hope that what has been agreed will at least be implemented.
in writing. i agree with the report mainly in the diagnosis chapter, because in the therapeutics chapter it seems to me that the paths already taken have proved to be unsuccessful. i therefore share the view expressed in the report that, despite these disagreements, too often relocation is looked at after it has already taken place, and that this is not only unhelpful but also a sign of a serious inability to anticipate reality. i therefore believe that some legislative measures should be promoted to prevent the waste of public funds and the use of public benefits without a consequent concern for responsibility in the management of private entities. but i don't think certain relocation moves are avoidable. just as i don't think this debate can be had without doing all the accounting, without looking at the profit and loss. in other words, the jobs lost as a result of the opening up of markets must be added to the jobs created by this opening up - not to mention the advantages for consumers. avoid the "law of the jungle" but do not try to prevent a reality from imposing itself. rather, our ambition should be to make the most of it.
in writing. the commission proposal seeks to fill in gaps and propose a european strategy for the next few years for the production and use of mercury in europe. the end of mercury exports, the end of its use in measuring equipment, dental amalgams, the control of emissions and the study of the effect of mercury use in vaccines are important points in this proposal which can bring clear benefits to public health. the authorization provided for in amendment no 2 protects small producers when controlled conditions exist, museum pieces, barometers and items of historical value. in amendment no 6, the advance of the deadline for the restriction of exports could be rushed and harm europe by favouring mercury-exporting third countries only. i agree with the commission proposal and with the report by marios matsakis in general.

in writing. there are two ideas in this report which i consider to be fundamental and which justify my vote in favour, despite my disagreement with other aspects of the report. on the one hand, it seems to me that it is of the utmost importance to realize that in the matter of new technologies almost everything that is said is looking backwards. we don't know what the future will be, we just know it's going to be fast and different. for this reason, the main objective of regulation should be to ensure, on the one hand, openness to competition and, on the other, incentives for investment in innovation. the european economy will only be competitive if it is an innovation economy, an economy for the future and not for this time. on the other hand, i share the concern about the issues of privacy and information security. the society that is developing has, among other things, the risk of being a surveillance society, and that will be the greatest tragedy of modernity in terms of public freedoms. finally, let us recognize that innovation, particularly new technologies, has brought about a democratic revolution in modern societies which must be welcomed, preserved and encouraged.
one year after the last restrictions on imports of footwear from china were lifted, we are now in a position to assess objectively the consequences of trade liberalization in this sector, which is characterized by a sharp increase in imports with the inherent consequences for the european fabric of production. this new reality underlines the need for close monitoring of the restructuring process under way in the footwear sector, encouraging the efforts of the business community to adapt, reorganizing the economic fabric of the regions most directly affected and taking account of the social consequences of the changes. but at the same time it is essential that the european commission should take steps to detect and counteract situations of manifest unfair competition which dramatically aggravate an already problematic situation. unfair competition is the greatest ally of protectionist impulses. the european union must be particularly demanding in this area. in this context, we should welcome the commission's decision to adopt anti-dumping measures after it was found that both china and vietnam have resorted to reprehensible practices in order to artificially lower the prices of their exports in this sector. such practices are particularly unacceptable, given that these countries already enjoy extraordinary comparative advantages. so there can be no room for any kind of calculating contemplation. the measures taken, while commendable on the whole, raise some concerns. the option of gradually implementing the anti-dumping duties, starting with a low amount, may immediately lead to an increase in imports from china and vietnam in advance, thus aggravating the existing situation. this is a serious concern. on the other hand, the option of excluding certain categories of products from the scope of the measures also deserves clear criticism, since there is a fear of abuse which can only be properly counteracted if, as we hope, a rigorous monitoring of these imports is developed.
i would like to begin by supporting the proposal for anti-dumping measures in the footwear sector. it was the minimum we had to demand because dumping destroys the essence and the raison d'être of free trade and european industry cannot die from apathy and complicity in such practices. in the absence of time, i shall confine myself to two comments. once dumping is confirmed, it makes no sense to continue to tolerate it. this is what will happen in practice with the gradual approach envisaged for the application of anti-dumping measures. this gradualism is not justified. second comment: the exclusion of children's footwear is absolutely unacceptable. it has no justification, no legal basis and no technical support. the credibility of these measures is totally compromised by maintaining this and other unjustified exclusions. i therefore urge that these aspects be re-examined. finally, it is vital that the commission should move away from a permanent reactive position and start to show concrete results in its policy priority of opening up third markets for european footwear exports, namely, and in particular, the markets of japan, the market access mechanisms of russia and the opening up of china itself.
the situation in the footwear sector is worrying, particularly in portugal. as an example, dozens of companies in the aveiro district closed down or reduced the number of employees during 2005, as is the case with ecco and rhode. unemployment and the risk of poverty are increasing, as can be seen from the closure of the c&j clarks company in castelo de paiva and the promises of support, training and subsidies to workers, who two years later find themselves abandoned to their fate. once again it is necessary to point out that:- with the rapid increase in footwear imports from third countries, it was not the so-called consumers who were left to their own devices, but the large retailers and distributors who made fabulous profits; - the responsibility for the closure of businesses and the loss of jobs lies not with third countries but with the european union, which is the first to promote competition and the liberalisation of international trade and which maintains a value of the euro that is detrimental to productive and exporting sectors such as footwear. with this policy they lose workers, they lose small, medium and micro enterprises, they lose countries like portugal - as studies and, more importantly, reality prove.

on behalf of the gue/ngl group, the interventions already carried out here demonstrate that the levels of poverty and social exclusion are very high and affect more than 70 million people in the european union. as the report states, it is known that in 14 of the 17 member states for which data are available, child poverty increased in the 1990s. but the current situation is likely to be aggravated by high levels of unemployment, the increase in precarious and low-paid work, flexibility, privatisation of basic sectors and services. the fact that poverty is a violation of human rights calls for greater attention to its causes and the necessary measures to promote social inclusion from a multidisciplinary perspective. hence the proposals we make in defence of changing macroeconomic policies to put social inclusion, employment with rights, public health services, education, access to justice, culture, decent housing at the centre of political priorities. we therefore advocate replacing the stability pact with a genuine development and progress pact and the lisbon strategy with a genuine strategy of economic and social cohesion, which implies that the draft directive on the creation of the internal market in services should not be insisted upon either. experience has already shown that the open method of coordination provided for in the lisbon strategy has not reduced poverty. based on the lisbon strategy, what has advanced are the liberalisations and privatisations of public sectors and services, which have aggravated poverty and made social inclusion more difficult. because these measures were mandatory, the open method of coordination did not oblige any member state to reduce poverty, and that is the difference in this process, two weights and two measures. public policies are essential to alleviating poverty and guaranteeing human rights, hence the need for a universal and supportive public social security policy and the rejection of the challenge we are making here so that this debate is no longer a debate without consequences.

that fishing methods are used to increase selectivity and therefore to enable fish to be caught at the correct sizes, taking into account the biology and life cycle of each species. ensuring satisfactory reproduction of fish and consequently the increase of stocks requires appropriate management measures such as temporary closure of certain fisheries, reduction of by-catches to in writing. as we stressed in 2001, under the pretext of the fight against terrorism, the european commission has put forward proposals which, going far beyond the necessary cooperation between states and existing legal instruments such as extradition, have advanced the supra-nationalisation of key aspects of justice, undermining the sovereignty of states and their duty to safeguard the rights of their citizens. we said then that the european arrest warrant, which is intended inter alia to abolish the principle of double incrimination, even if only to a limited extent, would be a trojan horse designed to lay the foundations for further supranational advances. this report confirms our criticisms. it considers judicial sovereignty to be an obstacle, as is interference by the existing political power in the extradition process, even if it is for reasons of respect for fundamental rights. it is significant that the german constitutional court annulled the legislation transposing the european arrest warrant and that, following this decision, several member states have resumed the application of extradition instruments, decisions which the report criticises, advocating the activation of the so-called passerelle provided for in article 42 of the treaty on european union, thus integrating the european arrest warrant into the first pillar.
in writing. the evaluation of the european arrest warrant has the advantage of focusing on one of the most important mechanisms of judicial cooperation within the european union, when, as is well known, such cooperation is both increasingly necessary and always difficult. traditionally, national authorities have not shared information easily in the security sector, just as they have had difficulty in cooperating in the judicial field. the european arrest warrant therefore responds to these inclinations, seeking to impose cooperation which is fundamental both in terms of greater security - it is the efficient way to prevent criminals from benefiting from the advantages of free movement - but also of greater legal certainty, an equally fundamental good. that said, it is regrettable that it is still necessary to remind member states that they must take 'appropriate measures to avoid any constitutional or legal obstacle to the application of the european arrest warrant to their nationals'. on the other hand, we cannot but mention and congratulate portugal for being one of the first member states to transpose the framework decision in question.

in writing. the commission proposal aims to replace regulation (eec) no 2082/92 on certificates of specifications for agricultural products and foodstuffs by a new text, introducing various simplifications and clarifications and bringing it into line with wto provisions. i understand the need to amend community legislation in this area. i therefore agree with the substance of the commission's proposal and i am voting in favour of the graefe zu baringdorf report. in this report i would stress and vote in favour of amendments 6 (the possibility for a member state to require other types of information provided that this need is duly justified) and 13 (setting a deadline for existing private control bodies if they believe it).
in writing. since 1993, the specific character of agricultural products and foodstuffs has been protected at community level. this has allowed the development of traditional products with specific characteristics linked to the method of their production and preparation. the report we voted on contains many simplifications and clarifications, not only in terms of procedures but also in terms of clarifying the responsibilities of the various authorities involved in examining applications. the importance of this instrument is clearly to enable the products to be valued, but also to ensure the protection of consumers against abusive practices, thus ensuring the fair practice of commercial transactions. the objective of the pilot project is to develop a european tourism strategy to promote the development of tourism in the union. finally, i would like to stress that it is essential that our traditional products are valued, recovered when necessary and protected, because we are the custodians of the heritage we pass on today to future generations.
in writing. protected geographical indications and designations of origin for agricultural products and foodstuffs make a significant contribution to improving the living conditions of the population in rural areas of the european union, including in portugal. the pressure from the usa and australia to make it appear that the existing regulations are incompatible with international trade agreements, particularly the infamous trips, is therefore unacceptable. the wto arbitration court itself has not found them, in general, to be compatible with wto obligations. however, the european union was nevertheless obliged to improve access for third countries. the commission is now trying to make adjustments, which the european parliament has decided to improve in most cases, in order to protect farmers and the rural world. in general, we are following these improvements and have therefore voted in favour, although we consider it essential to defend protected designations of origin, protected geographical indications and protected traditional specialities.

in writing. the protection of geographical indications and designations of origin for agricultural products and foodstuffs allows the producers concerned to preserve the production, processing and preparation of a product of a given origin by means of its registration. in the context of the need for regulatory changes in the light of the wto arbitration ruling, this report improves these instruments, which have significant results in access to higher priced markets and impact on job creation in rural areas of europe. in addition, the socioeconomic effects have been shown to be very positive for activities linked to tourism services. europe is the heir to millenary traditions which are a major tourist attraction. port wine or roquefort are world references for european products. it seems to me that it is important to clearly define the information to be provided to the consumer, not only for the protection of these products but also to enable the application and the rights of opposition. the clarification of the division of powers between the member states and the commission should be emphasized, since it only proves that the need for union activities must always be guided by respect for subsidiarity, so that the full potential effects of the planned actions can be achieved.

on behalf of the pse group. other the situation in the democratic republic of congo presents tremendous challenges to all of us in the european union who take seriously the 'responsibility to protect' enshrined in the last un high level summit in september 2005. the conflict that has ravaged the democratic republic of congo and the entire great lakes region is the bloodiest since world war ii. it has already caused 4 million deaths, the overwhelming majority of them civilians. real and lasting stability in this country is a fundamental condition for peace in the great lakes and in central africa in general and it is in this context that the united nations, which has the largest peacekeeping mission in its history in congo, has called on the european union to contribute to the peaceful conduct of the elections on 18 june, which will be observed by a mission headed by our colleague, mr philipe morillon, a mission which we will all support in this parliament. from the perspective of the european socialists, these elections represent the 'h' hour for the congo. either the transitional institutions born in the context of civil war are replaced by democratically elected institutions or, most likely, congo will continue to be at the mercy of bloody militias. but these elections and the challenge posed by the united nations are also a moment of truth for the european union. does european security and defence policy deserve credibility? can the member states be counted on to implement the european security strategy? i would like to stress three points in the joint resolution we tabled. this intervention must be seen as part of a temporary solution to the problem of internal instability in the country, which will only be resolved when the congolese army becomes a factor of stability. as has been clear from recent congolese army operations in catanga, the population still has reason to doubt the ability of the central government to protect them from the militias. the international community must invest more in consolidating the integrated brigades that already exist and accelerate the creation of new ones. without rapid improvements in the security sector, the union and the un may unfortunately be called upon to intervene in the congo many more times. secondly, it is important that the political legitimacy of this mission is a decisive factor in its success. in this respect it is essential that it be a genuine european mission - and in this respect we welcome the news of the solid participation of several member states led by germany and including also my country, portugal - and that it be a mission backed by the united nations security council. it is also essential that it is clear to all actors, both internal and external, that this mission is welcomed by the current congolese government and, finally, it is essential that the design of this mission reflects a genuine willingness on the part of the european union to support the electoral process with the inherent risks. the priority and objective of the presence of the european forces is clearly to contribute in a visible and credible way to the stability of the congolese electoral process. this is what the people of the congo and africa expect from us.

when the european parliament gave the signal for a second debate on the european constitution in its resolution of january on the reflection period, it made it clear that europe is waiting for the parties. the challenge is understandable. europe must become more and more political and must not do without a strong, active and responsible party structure. parties have a key role to play in achieving europe's ambition and improving the quality of european democracy. bridging citizens and power; boosting european public opinion; supporting civic engagement and participation. the role of european political parties is indeed, and should be, far from being merely parliamentary and representative. incomprehensibly, the european political parties have not strengthened themselves in the same proportion and at the same pace as the european parliament. the european parliament has a duty to ensure that the european parliament is not left behind. and yet, never in its evolution has europe called so much on the dynamic nature of parties. the question of the european constitution, for example, is a case of the dramatic absence of parties in a debate which has so far been confined to purely institutional matters. because europe is waiting for the role of political parties, it is urgent to strengthen party structures as soon as possible by creating a single european statute for european political parties. a statute which strengthens democratic control, which encourages political competition within the european parliament but which also frees european parties from a strictly parliamentary function so that they can be conceived in connection with the various dynamics of the european public sphere. and, of course, the strengthening of political parties requires a single statute, legal personality based on european law, capacity for autonomous responsibility, strengthening of the structures for party reflection, adequate funding and real power to define political priorities. that is why the leinen report aims at much more than an accounting reform of the life of european political parties. the report points to a new way of understanding the strategic role of political parties and their importance in structural solutions to a persistent european democratic deficit. a structural solution means streamlining the political market, greater links between european and national political parties, and attractiveness of european politics, including the european electoral system. the report also contributes to a certain european-level party consciousness so that we who have organized ourselves by taking responsibility for the world realise that these organizations have now also acquired a new scale. this responsibility is growing in these new founding moments of europe, such as the constitution and enlargement, and they require a new political practice, they require a reinterpretation of the role of the institutions, of the citizens and of the parties.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment. i would first like to congratulate mr bushill-matthews on the excellent work he has done and the good cooperation we have established in the drafting of our respective reports. in 2003, the natural growth rate of the european population was 0.04%. between 2005 and 2030, it is projected to lose more than 20 million people. by 2025, the population of the european union is expected to grow slightly due to immigration, but is then expected to decline again. immigration is only a partial solution. europeans do not have the number of children they want. studies reveal that on average they would like to have 2.3 children, but they only have 1.5. this number is insufficient to replenish the population. some causes of low birth rates are late or unstable access to employment, expensive housing, late age at which parents have their first child, lack of tax incentives and family benefits, insufficient parental leave, lack of childcare and other dependent care facilities, gender pay gap, difficulty in reconciling family and working life. demographer phillip longman reveals that in europe it is conservative christians and muslims who are having more children, which will lead to a change in the composition of society. what can be done to change the situation? phillipe logman suggests: sweden has managed to increase its birth rates by strengthening social benefits and building day care centres and nurseries; in italy, where it is very difficult to get a loan, it might help if home loans were made easier. one thing is certain, there is in most member states a strong correlation between high female employment rates and high birth rates and the reverse is also true.

social security systems are most threatened with their sustainability. immigration from outside europe has apparently brought about a balance in the employment rates of some member states, but there emergence of the current scandinavian realizations of the european social model. combining productivity gains and competitiveness gains with strong female participation in the labour market is very important. at the same time, fertility rates have increased and, in the meantime, there are greater facilities for paternity leave and better maternity supports. in the european context, every effort or of another type, for example mutualist. this is very important for workers who are covered by social security in a particular member state, who should find their lives made easier when they return known as active ageing. all this was discussed by the rapporteurs bushill-matthews, edite estrela and all the members of the committees who have worked seriously in this field. i would conclude by saying that, in short, the demographic challenges facing europe today are serious, but there are answers to these challenges. we are also able to contribute to ensuring more effective solidarity between generations.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, the demographic changes in the european union are, in general, a civilizational gain and not a problem. it is thanks to improved living conditions and health care that there is a longer life expectancy which naturally creates new challenges that must be taken into account. some of these challenges - and which are not adequately addressed by the commission in the green paper - are the importance of sexual and reproductive health, the inclusion of a gender perspective in all analyses and policies aimed at promoting the dignity of women in all areas, the improvement of the living conditions of the population and greater economic and social inclusion and cohesion. the proposals put forward by our group therefore stress the need for job stability, safety at the workplace and shorter working hours to allow for greater integration of both young and older workers into well-paid work, giving workers time to devote more attention to their families, more support for their children and their own lifelong learning. what is really important for managing demographic change is therefore employment with rights, a more equal distribution of income, strong public social security based on solidarity between generations, quality public services, particularly in areas such as health, education, housing and social protection. in other words, what we are proposing is the opposite of the path being followed, from priority to competition and liberalism, from increasingly precarious and poorly paid work, to unemployment, to the privatisation of public services and the trampling on labour rights. we therefore insist that a clear change in these policies is required.
