for the gue/ngl group as regards the content of the fisheries agreement between the european community and the kingdom of morocco as regards the waters under its effective sovereignty, i would only underline, in general terms, the positions expressed by representatives of the fisheries sector who consider the conditions of this new agreement to be extremely harmful, as they bring more restrictions, more burdens and less benefits for fishermen. but this agreement raises an earlier and more important question, namely respect for international law and the legitimate rights of the people of western sahara. morocco has illegally occupied western sahara. moreover, as stated in united nations resolutions, morocco has no sovereignty over this territory and, consequently, over its natural resources, nor any right as its administering power, de facto or de jure, under the charter of the united nations. morocco is merely the de facto illegal occupying power of western sahara, that is to say, its illegal colonizer. any agreement with morocco which, ambiguously or not, includes the exploitation of the natural resources of western sahara is therefore a clear violation of international law. the question, therefore, as the polisario front points out, is whether the european union countries will respect international law and contribute to a just and lasting solution to the conflict, respecting the inalienable right of self-determination of the saharawi people, or whether they will encourage injustice, aggression and the violation of human rights. the inclusion in the agreement of clauses which, in a mitigated form, state that the financial contribution from the european community should also be used for the development of the coastal populations of morocco and western sahara who live from fishing, as has been demonstrated in previous agreements, is insufficient and does not safeguard the rights of the sarawi people. if it were really to be ensured that the sarawak people would enjoy the dividends due to the exploitation of their fishery resources, the necessary conditions would have been provided for, for example, by the creation of a united nations fund in order to guarantee their interests and rights effectively. for these reasons we have tabled two amendments which, while reaffirming international legality, explicitly exclude the waters of western sahara from this fisheries agreement by granting fishing opportunities only to community fishermen in the waters under the sovereignty or jurisdiction of the kingdom of morocco, that is to say, in the waters situated exclusively north of the 27°40' parallel. finally, it is important to stress that, although on its own initiative it informed the european council and the european commission of its serious concerns about this agreement, the polisario front, the legitimate representative of the sarawi people, was not consulted throughout this process, which we consider regrettable.
mr commissioner, mr president of the committee on fisheries, we are faced with a very lively and very important debate because, on the one hand, we have the legitimate interests and rights of fishermen and of morocco, but it is also true that we must not forget that this agreement cannot legitimise the occupation of western sahara, which is not recognised by international law. this is a very strategic and fundamental question and i cannot therefore give my consent to a proposal which ignores this problem, which is of the utmost importance to the international community, although i understand those who take other options in this debate.
the debate is closed.
the report by mr reinhard rack, on behalf of the committee on transport and tourism, on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation establishing the second marco polo programme on the granting of community financial support to improve the environmental performance of the freight transport system (marco polo ii) (com (2004) 0478 - c6-0088/2004 - 2004/0157 (cod)) (a6-0408/2005) follows.
mr president, commissioner, i would first of all like to congratulate our colleague and rapporteur, reinhard rack, on the excellent work he has done on this report. i believe that your aim and that of most of the colleagues who have been involved in the debate in committee is above all that we must first of all rebalance the distribution of transport in a sustainable way and develop intermodality by tackling the problem of congestion effectively. otherwise, the expected increase in road freight transport, which is forecast to reach more than 60% in the european union alone by 2013, cannot be tackled. but the excessive traffic of goods on our roads is only the most visible problem. the economic, safety and environmental costs are enormous. consistent measures must therefore be taken to reduce these negative effects. reducing road freight transport and making intermodality a competitive and economically viable reality are the right responses to reverse the current trend. in this context and building on the work already undertaken, the marco polo ii programme contains a wide-ranging and comprehensive set of positive and necessary incentives and actions applicable not only to the territory of the european union but also to the neighbouring regions, which is to be welcomed. it will make it possible to stimulate investment in rail transport, in inland waterways and in the use of motorways of the sea more effectively, while also making use of the european maritime islands and the outermost regions as ports of passage and intermediate links between those roads, motorways of the sea and inland waterways, as i said. but it is also essential to promote the development of technical innovations that can provide competitive advantages for alternative modes of transport, in particular for towed material. the aim of reducing international road traffic, especially that of goods, also implies giving priority to projects in sensitive areas, in particular urban areas where traffic is highly concentrated. finally, mr president, the question of funding. as is well known, this programme was the subject of difficult negotiations in the context of the financial perspective, which resulted in a total amount of eur 400 million, well below the amount proposed by the commission, which regrets the lower strategic ambition it shows. since no more funds can be obtained, as the commission has proposed, it is the use and distribution of this amount that will determine the success of this programme. i cannot therefore fail to congratulate my colleague and rapporteur on the wise reduction of the eligibility ceiling for some projects, which will make this programme more accessible to small and mediumsized enterprises, which represent a very important part of the business fabric and which employ a significant part of the european workforce. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the objectives pursued in this report and the solutions it proposes will certainly have a decisive impact on the future of european freight transport, both in terms of its fluidity and its sustainability, and our support and the favourable vote of this parliament are therefore essential.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on wednesday at 11.30 a.m.
in writing. the text of council regulation (ec) no 1785/2003 should be amended to incorporate the amendments to the provisions applicable to imports of rice resulting from the agreements concluded between the commission and india (council decision 2004/617/ec of 11 august 2004), pakistan (council decision 2004/618/ec of 11 august 2004), the united states of america (council decision 2005/476/ec of 21 june 2005) and thailand (council decision 2005/953/ec of 20 december 2005). these agreements laid down the customs conditions for imports taking into account the nature of the product and the quantities imported, and authorised the commission to derogate from regulation (ec) no 1785/2003 for a transitional period. since this derogation was limited to 30 june 2006, it is urgent to amend the text of the current regulation. i therefore support the commission's proposal and approve the report by mr joseph daul.
in writing. i am in favour of the adoption of this document in its essence. the discharge of the eu-angola fisheries agreement was inevitable given the obligations created in the meantime by the new angolan legislative framework, which are not in line with eu principles on partnership agreements with third countries. i agree with the flexibility of the current fifg and the derogating measures which are presented in this proposal, but i believe that the eu should, in the name of reciprocity, be attentive to the exercise of fishing activity by community shipowners who benefit from these measures.
in writing. the termination of the agreement, in addition to the loss of fishing opportunities, jobs and value added associated with the activities carried out, implies the conversion of vessels dependent on fishing in angolan waters. the commission regrets this complaint and the feasibility of the vessels concerned operating in other areas or under other fisheries agreements, negotiating new fishing opportunities or existing opportunities which are not being used, should be examined. or the fact that the ships remain in angola through the creation of joint ventures. by maintaining jobs and countering the culling of vessels through demolition. measures are therefore needed to facilitate the conversion of these fishing vessels, such as exempting them from the obligation to reimburse aid for construction or modernisation obtained in the previous 10 years and aid for temporary immobilisation granted under the fifg. as for joint ventures or other types of joint ventures with a third country, they must be based on genuine mutually beneficial cooperation projects and not promote the relocation of the community fleet and fishing industry with the resulting loss of jobs and economic activities upstream and downstream.
in writing. the decision by the majority of parliament to waive the parliamentary immunity of mr tobias pflüger, a member of the european united left/nordic green left group in this parliament, elected on the lists of the german social democratic party, is of particular significance. this is an unprecedented decision, obviously of a political nature, which sets a serious precedent, since it follows the participation of this member of parliament in a protest demonstration against the so-called 'munich security conference' held annually in this german city. this is the fourth time that tobias pflüger has faced charges related to his participation in this demonstration. in 1999 the munich court withdrew the allegations. in 2003, the proceedings were closed. in 2004, the police department even issued a formal apology. the present case refers to 2005, when tobias pflüger participated in this demonstration for the first time as an mep. the request for waiver of immunity was made by the ministry of justice of the federal republic of germany. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect, and i am sure that the commission will be able to support them. the report by the committee on legal affairs of the european parliament makes the decision now taken incomprehensible and serious. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. the report adopted today represents an improvement on the text adopted at first reading, making the conditions for the use of nutrition and health claims more restrictive, given that a varied and balanced diet is an indispensable condition for maintaining health and that products considered individually are less important than the diet as a whole. on the other hand, health and nutritional claims must be scientifically substantiated, taking into account all the available scientific data and weighted against the evidence, as is now the case in the proposals which have been adopted and which our group has endorsed. we regret, however, the adoption of an exceptional amendment concerning the nutritional profiles. although the agreed compromise falls short of expectations in certain respects, it provides a certain level of protection and information for consumers and seeks to safeguard the rights of smes.
in writing. the commission proposal seeks to fill in gaps and propose a european strategy for the next few years in relation to consumer information on the food products they consume. increased consumer awareness, with accurate and concise information, can help reduce problems such as cardiovascular disease and obesity. the compromise amendments voted on substantially improve an initial proposal which i consider to be insufficient and ill-founded. the inclusion of imported products, special attention to products for children, easier access for smes, the exclusion of fresh and unpackaged products and the prohibition of health claims on alcoholic beverages (above 1.2%), will provide a stronger and more comprehensive directive. i therefore agree with the commission proposal and with the report by mrs adriana poli bortone.
in writing. we voted in favour of the compromise proposals at second reading because we believe it is important to have a high level of consumer protection in the addition of vitamins, minerals and other substances to food, preventing them from being a danger to public health. however, since the council, in its common position adopted in december 2005, did not take account of some important amendments which the european parliament had approved in may last year, we believe it is important to re-emphasise the bioavailability of vitamins and minerals, that is to say, that they are bioavailable, otherwise consumers will be misled and may even put their health at risk. similarly, maximum safe levels for vitamins and minerals should be established and information for consumers should be made comprehensible and useful. we regret that no other positive amendments have been adopted, but we hope that at least these will be taken into account by the council.
in writing. i should like to thank the rapporteur for his report, which is a very good report. as a fundamental point, i would like to emphasize the fact that the situation in the water catchment areas of the various member states where this species exists is quite different, which means that different strategies and measures must be adopted to ensure that these stocks are recovered effectively. i therefore think it is right that the member states should propose their recovery plans. i also think it is important that the eu should support the measures that each member state considers to be the best for the repopulation of the different river basins. this includes, for example, the construction and/or adaptation of obstacle-crossing mechanisms along the course of rivers.
in writing. the commission's main objective in presenting this proposal for a regulation to restore eel stocks is to establish national eel management plans. the proposal aims to ensure a 40% leakage rate for adult silver eels in each river basin, a difficult-to-achieve objective which applies equally to all member states, regardless of their specific characteristics. it was also proposed to prohibit fishing for eels during the first 15 days of each month, which would be excessive and have serious socioeconomic repercussions. these measures would have to be implemented within a relatively short timeframe, i.e. by july 2007. in this respect, the european parliament's proposals are more balanced and correct the most serious points of the commission's proposal, thereby contributing to the recovery of eel stocks. the report replaces the fishing ban in the first half of each month with a fishing ban that halves the fishing effort. it replaces the 40% leakage target with a high percentage. it allows member states to act only in the relevant river basins. and it increases the implementation deadline to 2008. all this gives the member states greater scope for action.
in writing. the ec-morocco fisheries partnership agreement lays down the principles, rules and procedures governing economic, financial, technical and scientific cooperation in the 'moroccan fishing zones' (article 1). article 2 (a) defines 'moroccan fishing zone' as 'the waters under the sovereignty or jurisdiction of the kingdom of morocco'. the vote in favour of the report in question by the undersigned is obviously based on the assumption contained in rule 2.
in writing. i am in favour of the adoption of this document in its essence. the new agreement provides for a significant reduction in the number of fishing licences allocated to member states. it went from 500 to about 100, and some important fisheries categories were lost: crustaceans and cephalopods. in any case, i think it is important for the community fleet, and for the national fleet in particular, to continue to be able to fish in morocco under a partnership agreement. this also safeguards the cfp's overriding interests in international fisheries, and ensures that some important commitments are made in the field of fisheries management and the fight against illegal fishing.
in writing. i would like to vote in favour of a fisheries agreement between the ec and morocco. but i have to vote against this agreement because no amendments have been adopted to exclude from the scope of the agreement the waters and fisheries resources corresponding to western sahara, a non-self-governing territory, in accordance with un general assembly resolutions 1514 and 1541, illegally occupied by morocco since 1974. so in my view the agreement - and the european commission's legislative proposal for it - is in breach of international law.
in writing. we regret the rejection of our amendments which, while reaffirming international legality, explicitly excluded the waters of western sahara from this fisheries agreement, limiting it to the waters exclusively north of the 27° 40' n parallel.' we consider it all the more serious when the positions of officials of the european commission and of members of this parliament are made public, who regard morocco, in defiance of international law, as the de facto administering power of western sahara. or when it is found that, in the course of previous agreements, there has been fishing and use of western sahara ports without safeguarding the rights and interests of the sarawi people. it is necessary to stress, as the polisario front does, that the united nations, through a legal opinion on western sahara and its natural resources - of 29 january 2002 - reaffirms the condemnation of the exploitation and plundering of natural resources and of all economic activity carried out to the detriment of the interests of the peoples of colonized or non-self-governing territories, depriving them of their legitimate rights over their natural resources, considering such exploitation and plundering illegal and a threat to the integrity and prosperity of these territories. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. following the report on the eu-morocco partnership agreement on marine resources, i would like to state that my vote seeks to follow the regulation most appropriate for the environmental sustainability of the area. in that sense, the agreement is crucial. however, for the eu, as for myself, the issue of human rights is also crucial. we must therefore always enforce the united nations resolutions on this matter. it is clear to me that the understanding of this agreement is about the maritime zones and territories over which there is no conflict and over which the question of sovereignty is not raised, and not about any other, because no state can dispose of what is not under its sovereignty or jurisdiction to the detriment of the self-determination of other peoples.
in writing. the vote on this agreement requires two brief explanations. first of all, the question of western sahara. given that this agreement deals with the subject in the same way as it has been used to, that is, without introducing any change in the european position, and that the commission's legal services have considered it to be in line with international rules, i do not think that the objections to the situation in that territory are being defended effectively here. as regards the substance of the matter, it is welcome that it has finally been possible to reach an agreement on this matter, although it cannot but regret that the final result is not very favourable to portuguese interests. however, given the considerations here, all indications are that this is the best solution, because it is a possible solution. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. the european commission (ec) is responsible for monitoring the application of community law in its capacity as 'guardian of the treaties'. the ec informs, warns and sanctions member states in the event of non-compliance with the community treaties. the annual reports of the ec on the application of community law indicate the state of transposition of directives by the member states in order to ensure effective monitoring of the application of legislation. this control does not consist only in an assessment of the transposition in quantitative terms, but also in an assessment of the quality of the transposition. as part of the objectives of improving european policies, particularly through their transparency, the ec has stated that its aim is to reduce the volume of legislation and to eliminate ineffective legislative acts, which does not mean deregulation. i agree with the rapporteur that more human and financial resources should be made available to the ec services to increase the capacity to respond to infringements. i also support the creation of coordination points in each member state for issues relating to the transposition and application of community law and coordination with national ministries and regional and local authorities.
in writing. despite the extraordinary amount of community legislation in force and in preparation - sometimes of questionable necessity or reason for being - the truth is that all this legislation is amenable to monitoring, particularly as regards the transposition and entry into force phase of the new legislation. as the report says, it is therefore regrettable that the community institutions - in particular the commission - take so long to assess the application of european legislation. this is doubly serious, since it reduces the effectiveness of this mechanism and at the same time deprives it of such important virtues as allowing it to act in such a way as to lead the states to comply with the obligations they have assumed in time. another important aspect of this procedure is that a careful assessment of the difficulties of transposition/application of legislation should be an opportunity for a real improvement in the quality of community legislation, especially when, as mentioned in this report, a process is under way precisely for this purpose.
in writing. the number of cases of failure and delay in transposing community law into national legal systems should, in addition to the need for adequate control of its application, give the legislator a desire for simplification and respect for the principle of subsidiarity. i believe that the application of community law will continue to be insufficient as long as community legislation is not clear and perceptible and the community acquis as a whole remains poorly understood. without good community legislation, it is difficult to ensure that community law is properly applied. i welcome the view of the president of the european commission that the community institutions should make a serious effort to ensure that legislation is contained and that it is effective. sometimes less can mean more.
in writing. of all the issues raised in this report, the one which deserves the most attention is that concerning the impact assessment of community legislation. as i have already said, despite constant and possibly excessive legislative production, it is possible to keep a close watch on the legislative production of the community institutions and, more importantly, on its effects. and that concern should be a constant. in parallel, subsidiarity is invoked, which is quite appropriate in this context. this principle - understood in a non-reductive way - must be a key element of legislation within the european union, where the scale is best, the adaptation to the needs of each country, the maintenance of close ties between power and citizens. that said, there is no doubt that this principle is ineffective for a large number of situations where the community scale is most appropriate. but that is also a key element of this principle. finally, there is concern about the recognition of the role of national parliaments, which is essential for a good legislative outcome. without prejudice to others, these are essential elements for better legislative production.
in writing. as i have already said, respect for subsidiarity - in addition to being a fundamental requirement that has been in place for a long time and which needs to be emphasized more - is the touchstone that distinguishes the true europeanists, faithful not only in speech but actually in practice to the idea and the motto that the draft constitutional treaty has summarized: 'united in diversity'. it is essential that the european union gives priority to decision-making at the level closest to the citizen, evaluates the new legislation it adopts and promotes the simplification of existing legislation on the basis of criteria of intelligibility, adequacy and proportionality. i believe that the european union will gain if it focuses on legislating with quality rather than quantity and on seriously involving national parliaments in this process, in addition to the parties directly concerned, so that they can make their positions known in good time and present counterproposals.
in writing. the european commission's better regulation initiative is key to ensuring the trust of citizens, consumers and businesses in the eu. this confidence is based on their experience or perception of european legislation and its impact on their daily lives. in the context of the internal market, it should therefore be translated into the guarantee of effective and high-quality legislation that does not hinder innovation or create unnecessary distortions and unnecessary costs, in particular for smes, public authorities or voluntary groups. our legislation must therefore help to open up opportunities for trade and business, to increase the choice available to consumers and citizens, while protecting environmental, social and consumer rights. if it does not, we will be going against the tide, against the progress of the lisbon strategy, against growth and employment and against the internal market. i have therefore voted in favour of the mccarthy report.
in writing. we agree with the repeal of irrelevant and obsolete acts in community legislation with a view to simplifying the regulatory framework so that decisions are appropriate, simple, effective and do not call into question the principle of subsidiarity, which should be further emphasised in this report so that there is no doubt about its defence throughout this process. however, we hope that this objective will not be used to call into question certain principles which defend the fundamental rights of citizens, including social rights and workers' rights. we also think that an amendment to the existing interinstitutional agreements governing the quality of union legislation could be a positive thing. we therefore voted in favour of the report, although we have reservations about some aspects and even disagree with others, given its ambiguous wording, as you have already mentioned.
in writing. the report we are debating and voting on, as well as the commission communication on which it is based, deserve my wholehearted support. the effort to analyse and revise the community legislative framework is a goal which must be promoted with a view to simplifying the legislative environment, which is essential for greater legal certainty for both citizens and judicial operators. on the other hand, it is an opportunity to simplify the regulatory environment, which is essential for the development of economic activity. there is, however, one aspect of the report and the commission communication with which i do not entirely agree. the argument put forward in both texts that legislation through regulations tends to be more virtuous than legislation through directives does not merit my agreement. on the contrary, although i am aware of the difficulties involved in transposing directives, i believe that they correspond to a method of legislative production which respects an idea of community which is dear to me. this is without rejecting the regulations or failing to recognise their obvious usefulness.
in writing. the question raised by the communication in question deserves wider attention than that which is confined to the question of the legal basis and limits of the commission's withdrawal of legislative proposals. in my view, the main issue is the finding that the situation in force allowed a set of legislative procedures to exist in limbo, which no longer had any reason to exist, but which were also not closed. this reality, more than a debate on the powers of the various institutions, requires an analysis of the routine and bureaucratic aspects of the community legislative procedure. the fact that there is a package of more than 500 documents between parliament and the council awaiting the attention of the legislators is also a matter which should be of concern to us. the european union does not need to legislate a lot to be relevant, it needs to legislate well to be useful.
the debate is closed. the competent authority shall inform the applicant of the reasons for the refusal.

on behalf of the gue/ngl group, as this report and the recent spring economic forecasts show, weak economic growth in the european union as a whole and high unemployment, with over 70 million people living in poverty, remain, and are generally ignored by the commission. this should require a review of the continued priority given to the monetary and liberal policies of the lisbon strategy and the guidelines of the european central bank. however much one tries to hide the reality, it cannot be denied that monetary and fiscal policy based on the stability pact, and giving priority to price stability, has a negative impact on economic growth and employment growth - and portugal is an example of this - so a monetary and fiscal policy is needed that helps to strengthen economic recovery and combat employment, requiring the repeal of the stability pact and its replacement by a real pact for development and social progress. we insist on the need for a combined and coordinated expansionary policy between the european union and its member states, aimed at strengthening domestic demand, public investment, research and education, quality public services, including in the areas of health and housing and infrastructure and equipment, promoting high rates of employment with rights, ensuring economic and social cohesion and balanced environmental development. we believe that these are some of the essential proposals to win the confidence of the citizens of the european union. without this, we are in fact still living in this climate of pessimism that results from policies that do not address the problems that people are experiencing in the european union at the moment.
madam president, commissioner, i should like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur on the quality of his work. the report begins by stressing that the european union's main problem is weak economic growth, persistently high unemployment and insufficient use of installed production capacity - and this is, in my view, a key message. the first signs of recovery that the commissioner mentioned in his speech are not enough to ensure the union's international competitiveness, nor to compensate for the years of stagnation we have been experiencing. it is important that the balance of public finances should not be seen as an end in itself. moreover, neither the interpretation of the stability pact nor the opening of excessive deficit procedures have been effective in preventing persistent public finances imbalances in the main european economies. two main recommendations, in my view, follow from this report: the first concerns the need to make the balance of public finances fully compatible with the revival of european competitiveness, placing this revival at the centre of europe's political concerns. the incipient growth that is beginning to be noticed has occurred more despite the covenant than because of it. public and private investment needs to be strengthened in the areas of innovation, education, development of new skills and technologies, in line with the lisbon strategy. intergovernmental cooperation and the coordination of economic policies at european union level are fundamental instruments and are still not sufficiently taken up. it also regrets that this priority for growth has not been sufficiently reflected either in the interpretation, as stated in the pact, or, above all, in the financial perspective which we are going to approve in principle tomorrow. the second note concerns the need to further clarify the accounting concepts and practices of the statistical bodies of the member states, i.e. to disseminate good practice, to harmonise concepts, timetables and methodologies. the soundness of public finances is only relevant if it is sustainable in the medium term, which often requires measures of a structural nature. we must stop short-term operations based on extraordinary measures or creative accounting because they destroy credibility and undermine investor and consumer confidence. in short, consolidating public finances is essential, but only if it is sustainable and fully linked to strengthening the european economy and the capacities of its citizens. i think these are two key messages to be taken from the report we are discussing today.

give its opinion on the compatibility of the interinstitutional agreement with the treaties in force, and there are no legal obstacles to its adoption. although it is not for this committee to assess development for better public scrutiny and democratic control of the union's budgetary options. the compromise reached between the parties will not correspond to the vision and ambition for europe and in a difficult political context, marked by a crisis of confidence in the european project, deep divergences between the member states and the institutions and a certain confusion about the the agreement reached for the financial framework for 2007-13 included in the interinstitutional agreement is a bad agreement, because it is insufficient from the financial point of view, inadequate in terms of its priorities and its instruments to meet the challenges facing an enlarged union. it is an agreement which does not respond to the increased need for cohesion, nor does it take as a priority the fight against the growing asymmetries and inequalities, unemployment and poverty, which are occurring in the european union. it is a bad agreement for economic and social cohesion and for the cohesion countries, by undermining the redistributive role of the community budget. the structural funds are reduced by eur 28 billion in the light of the european commission's proposal and their share is reduced from 0.41% of community gni under the current framework to 0.37% in the future financial framework and in a european union of 27. the agreement means €100 billion less than the european parliament's original proposal, which negotiated a commitment of only €12 billion to accept only €4, forcing wrong priorities and at the cost of cuts in other budget lines. it is also a bad agreement for countries like portugal, which, in a context of increased competition and faced with the deep crisis it is in, due, among other things, to the restrictions on monetary and budgetary policy that have led to the increase in unemployment and to a divergence since 2000 with the european union, is suffering cuts of more than eur 1 million a day and 15% of community transfers in relation to the current financial framework, not to mention the injustice of the cuts in the algarve region, the victim of the so-called statistical effect. for all these reasons, we can only reject this agreement.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment from harmful substances. it also defends the stability pact, in particular its 1997 version, in a restricted way, arguing that the 2005 reform has weakened the pact. this blind monetarist and liberal stance, which serves the profits of the large multinational companies operating in the european union and which puts workers (in particular their jobs, their rights and their wages) as a variable of adjustment to crises, is in line with their role in the creation of the single currency and the stability pact. in addition, it is once again apparent that the replacements on the executive board of the ecb are made between the large countries (one german for another german), which, if we add to this the rotation of votes in the council, relegates the small countries to a peripheral and secondary position with regard to monetary decisions in economic and monetary union. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. we support the rejection of the interinstitutional agreement put forward by our group - and voted for by 120 members of this parliament - because, among other reasons, we reject: - a logic that, with each setback, turns every defeat into a mystified "victory", on the pretext that it can always be worse. - the real blackmail of the economically more developed countries of the european union, the so-called 'rich', who imposed the relative reduction of the community budget - and we shall see in the future, if only in absolute terms - when enlargement took place to ten more countries with an average level of economic development below the community average, and preparations are being made for enlargement to two more countries. - a process which increasingly strengthens decision-making at supranational level on monetary, budgetary, economic and social policies - responding to the interests of the economically more developed countries and the large economic and financial groups, which are increasingly out of step with the rights, needs and aspirations of workers and peoples in the various eu countries - and which at the same time, and in the end in a consistent way, reduces the financial means which could help to minimise the consequences of (unacceptable) capitalist competition between countries with a very different level of economic development.
in writing. the european parliament's negotiating position on the financial perspective for 2007-2013, as expressed in its resolution of 8 june 2005, contained quantitative, structural and qualitative elements intended to supplement it and considered to be 'non-negotiable points'. in its resolution of 18 january 2006, rejecting the european council's agreement of december 2005, the european parliament declared its 'determination to defend' these elements by expressing its 'readiness to enter into constructive negotiations with the council'. it was worth it! while recognising that the final outcome of the negotiations, particularly in terms of the quantitative elements, falls short of the position adopted in june, overall this was a success. in view of the need and urgency to reach an agreement, it was the only compromise possible. the ep also called for the commission to be given the power to adopt legislative proposals for the future. most of the qualitative elements are reflected in the new interinstitutional agreement. of these, parliament's full participation in the 2009 revision is noteworthy, as it will enable it to find solutions to the remaining deficits and improve the next financial perspective, in pursuit of the objective of the negotiating position, which remains. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the proposals for the financial perspective (2007-2013) which we have put forward since the start of the negotiations are as follows: - to ensure that the community budget is at a level which, on the basis of national contributions in accordance with the relative wealth of each country (based on its gnp), plays a redistributive role and gives priority to the real approximation of the levels of economic development of the various countries and to an effective improvement in the living conditions of their workers and populations. - a fundamental change in the common agricultural policy aimed at safeguarding the right of each country to ensure its food sovereignty and security by introducing modulation and capping of agricultural aid and ensuring a fair redistribution of agricultural aid between farmers, production and countries. - the end of the conditionality of the cohesion fund to the stability pact and the non-application of the n+2 (or 3) rule to this fund and the structural funds. - full compensation for regions which will suffer the so-called statistical effect, such as the algarve. - portugal should not lose community funding and a specific programme should be set up to modernise the portuguese economy in the context of enlargement. the community framework adopted is contrary to these objectives and needs. hence our rejection.
in writing. i voted in favour of the böge report on the interinstitutional agreement because i consider it to be the greatest common denominator after lengthy negotiations at trilogue level. i cannot, however, fail to express my deep concern at the apparent divergence between the provisions of the agreement reached in december and their practical application. in particular, there seems to be a discrepancy in the allocation of funds to the algarve region at the moment, in the context of the exceptional measures approved for the statistical regions. the algarve region will be seriously affected by the european commission's interpretation of the december agreement, which could lead to it being treated much worse than any other objective 2 region, and even less so than being phased out. in the interests of transparency and good interinstitutional cooperation, i consider it of the utmost importance to clarify the interpretative assumptions of the contents of the financial package 2007-2013.

in writing. if politics is the art of the possible, the search for an agreement on the financial framework of the european union for 2007-13 has proved to be the art of the possible minimum, which is not a reason for satisfaction. the european union has been undergoing a process of enlargement to new countries and political integration in recent years, which should necessarily be matched by an increase in its financial dimension. the project of prosperity and security which the eu represents for its citizens needs, in order to be real, a corresponding financial framework, sufficient for its new dimensions. the idea of solidarity, which has always been part of the design of the european union's financial instruments, is justified both by its objective of fairness and by its objective of promoting a balanced and effective internal market. in view of these considerations, and in particular the impossibility of exceeding the limited budgetary result, i join my vote in favour to this regret and to the wish that the whole budgetary structure be reviewed in good time, in particular with a view to promoting, through the revision of the expenditure chapter, a more development-friendly economy.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a financial perspective for 2007-13. however, i still believe that the proposal initially approved by the european parliament was much more advantageous for the european union, not only in terms of quantity but also in terms of methodology. the proposal adopted by parliament is the consequence of the definition of policies and priorities and, in this sense, is the true expression of a policy, whereas the council decision is more the sum of the member states' demands and therefore loses in quality. i voted in favour of the proposal because, despite this fact, it would be very unfortunate if the european institutions did not have a medium-term financial framework, which is a fundamental instrument for preparing projects linked to development. another important reason for voting in favour of the proposal has to do with the commitment to review both revenue and expenditure. i attach the utmost importance to this point, since i have repeatedly expressed the idea that the current way of financing the european union has run out. for the first time it has become clear that this reform will be of major importance and will involve the european parliament.
in writing. i voted in favour of the interinstitutional agreement on budgetary discipline and improvement of the budgetary procedure because i believe that the outcome of the negotiations on the financial perspective for 2007-2013 is overall positive for the 450 million european citizens. there are no ideal budgets. in the current economic and political context of the european union this is a good deal for europe and for portugal, which will receive 22.5 billion euros over these seven years. in addition to the quantitative gains over the previous council proposal, there are qualitative advantages which portugal will also benefit from. on the other hand, any delay in the decision would mean delays in the use of community funds to solve people's problems. european citizens (and portuguese in particular) would not understand any more delays.

in writing. this report follows the commission's initial proposal of december 2004, which had two objectives: to extend the period of validity of the transitional measures and to lay down rules for the prevention, control and eradication of certain transmissible spongiform encephalopathies, one of the central issues of which is the prohibition on feeding processed animal protein to farmed animals. the undertaking adopted today lays down a set of rules on breeding programmes for the selection of resistance to tse or for the export and import of feed. however, and despite the food and veterinary crises which have occurred in recent years with consequences for public and animal health, it is in the interests of feed business operators to allow derogations from the general ban in force, in particular by allowing the use of fishmeal and by giving the commission the possibility of partial derogations such as for young ruminants. we disagree with this position, which, in addition to the problems already mentioned, raises questions about the model of intensive and vertical development of production, which is now clearly evident in agriculture and fisheries. that is why we abstained.

in writing. the situation of european public finances remains precarious and largely unchanged. european growth remains worryingly slow. the decline in deficits we are witnessing reflects only economic adjustments arising from expectations of higher economic growth and not the structural reforms needed and vital to the future of the european economy. the report thus recalls the implications for growth, employment and macroeconomic stability of public finances and calls on the commission and the member states to work together and take measures to counteract the slow growth of the european economy and provide a positive environment for the smooth functioning of the single currency. these are key measures for a strong and stable european economy capable of providing new business and employment opportunities for its citizens. we cannot, however, forget the difficulties that several member states have had in recent years in keeping public deficits within the levels of the stability and growth pact. this is another reason why we should be following this matter with concern and call on the commission and the member states to take structural measures and to propose a real coordination of economic policies. i therefore voted in favour of mr rosati's report.

the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner, i would like to begin by thanking the many positive contributions from colleagues in the various political groups, as well as the competent support of the staff of the committee on agriculture who worked with me on the preparation of this report. the enormous scale of some of the disasters that have occurred in recent years, and particularly in the last year, has led the european parliament to devote its due attention to this subject. three committees were appointed to present, each from its own perspective, solutions to prevent disasters or to minimize their consequences when they cannot be avoided. it has been a very motivating job that i have been engaged in for the last six or seven months listening to many colleagues, experts, economic agents, local, regional and national authorities and affected populations. i have also had the opportunity to visit the six member states most affected last year, spain, portugal, germany, austria, france and italy. i am very pleased to note the welcome we have received in all the places we have been to and i am sure that our action has been useful to our institution, bringing the european parliament closer to the citizens. i have also tried to ensure that there is as broad a consensus as possible on the proposals i am presenting to you. i was pleased to accept almost all of the amendments tabled, 53 out of 60, and of the few that were excluded, most were excluded for formal reasons of redundancy or duplication and not precisely because of their content. the report under discussion is based on the following three main assumptions: first, agriculture and forestry are activities in symbiosis with nature and are therefore particularly exposed to the effects of climate change, which is exacerbated by the climate change context in which we live, and to the bio-health risks arising from air, water and soil pollution and which are exacerbated by increasing globalisation. secondly, rural exodus is one of the main causes of the increase in forest fires in southern europe, a situation that is particularly acute during times of drought, as the year 2005 unfortunately proved. the budgetary limits of the european union must also be respected, which is why the proposals put forward are compatible with the financial perspective which we adopted here yesterday. i therefore propose, in essence, that existing policy instruments such as the solidarity fund, the european agricultural fund and rural development fund, the veterinary fund, regional policy instruments and the future life+ regulation be optimized by improving them and adapting them to the context of genuine disaster and risk management systems, and in the latter case by the communityisation of an insurance and reinsurance system to be co-financed by farmers, the member states and the european union through the eafrd. the solidarity fund will have to be broader and more flexible, and will have to cover catastrophes of slow development, such as drought, which is not included at the moment, for example. to make it more effective, it should be accompanied by a flexibility clause which, from the appropriations not currently used by the common agricultural policy, can guarantee it adequate financial means when necessary. the eafrd, for its part, should give priority to financing, with the greatest possible co-financing through national rural development programmes, actions aimed at afforestation and reforestation of burnt trees, as well as all preventive measures such as clearing of forests, combining it with the use of biomass to produce energy, in addition, of course, to training and information for the economic operators involved and raising the awareness of the population of this type of problem. these are just a few aspects, very briefly summarized, which illustrate the importance of the agricultural approach to disasters from the point of view of the european parliament and which i hope can count on the widest possible support from this house. i hope that the commission and the council will give due consideration to these proposals in accordance with the requirements of the circumstances.
the commission is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: the methodology used to draw up these three reports, in particular the visits we made to the six countries affected by natural disasters and the public hearing held in brussels, has already been mentioned here. in our countries too, at least in portugal, we have held public hearings to gather suggestions, information and proposals from the various parties involved. i would also like to thank the members for their support, their suggestions, their amendments and the technicians who have helped to improve my report. the climate is changing, the year is no longer compartmented into the traditional four seasons. successive days of drought alternate with days of torrential rains and these with heat waves. climate change is at the root of natural disasters, such as floods, extreme droughts and fires, which have occurred worldwide with great frequency and caused severe damage in terms of human losses, environmental degradation and reduced economic activity. this is one of the great problems of our time. the year 2005 began with the world in a state of shock at the scale of the tragedy caused by the asian tsunami. the identification of the dead and the search for survivors went on for several months. in the summer, several fires destroyed hundreds of thousands of acres of forest in portugal, france, and spain, and violent floods spread devastation and death in countries such as germany and austria. outside europe, hurricane katrina caused unprecedented destruction in some u.s. states, and before the year was out, afghanistan was rocked by a violent earthquake. in addition to earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions, floods and fires, other phenomena associated with climate change and global warming are causing sea level rise in coastal areas and the disappearance of beaches. studies published in the journal science reveal that sea levels could rise 20 feet by 2100 because the arctic and antarctic ice sheets are melting faster and faster. to avoid the worst, serious and immediate measures are needed to curb greenhouse gas emissions and to comply with the kyoto protocol. the commissioner mentioned the water shortage. it is also necessary to ensure a more sustainable, rational and efficient use of water. more than a billion people struggle daily for survival because they lack access to safe drinking water. four hundred million are children. waterborne diseases kill a child every 15 seconds and are associated with many diseases and malnutrition. the allocation of resources between the different domestic, industrial and agricultural users must be studied and discussed, and waste must be combated. it is essential to raise awareness among citizens so that they can take part in preventing these disasters, in particular by reducing greenhouse gas emissions, as i have already said, by protecting the forest and by not building in risk areas. natural disasters have no borders and their environmental consequences affect neighbouring countries as well. given that community action must complement that of national authorities, whether in prevention, planning and intervention, or rehabilitation and follow-up, it is also necessary to strengthen coordination at all levels, improve the existing system and develop early warning systems. despite the specificity of each region and the diversity of the situations encountered, there are common needs to be addressed, such as the definition of risk assessment mechanisms and the drawing up of drought, forest fire and flood maps. the definition of prevention systems to combat the causes of natural disasters and to improve urban planning, especially in coastal and risk areas, such as the preservation of natural ecosystems, the strengthening of cooperation in civil protection between member states and within the european union to ensure that additional means of rapid mobilisation are available to deal with emergency situations, the flexibility and simplification of the rules for the application of instruments such as the solidarity fund and the forest focus programme, are many other proposals in my report and which i hope will naturally be supported, first and foremost, by parliament, the commission and the council.
i would like to begin by congratulating the rapporteurs, my colleagues edite estrela, capoulas santos and galeote quecedo, on the excellent work they have done, which may have in some way contributed to a solution that could have been more interesting, which was also proposed in this parliament and which was not adopted. the natural disasters which have struck europe in recent years (drought, forest fires and floods) deserve special attention from the european parliament as regards their impact on agricultural activity. as the rapporteur, mr capoulas santos, has rightly pointed out, agricultural and forestry production, unlike other economic activities, is closely linked to nature and is therefore more vulnerable to natural disasters. i therefore believe that, after recent experience, european agriculture should be the subject of a new approach to the prevention and response to natural disasters. the current national mechanisms are often inadequate and the supranational response mechanisms of one-off application end up being inefficient. the solidarity fund, which we have already discussed here today and will certainly continue to discuss, is currently under review and it is hoped that it will include drought in its scope. at a time when climate change is already making itself felt and when the vulnerability of farmers to these dangers is becoming increasingly relevant, i consider it of the utmost importance to draw up a community strategy against natural disasters. it is therefore essential that a community programme on forest protection and fire prevention be set up in the next financial framework, with a view to encouraging action to raise awareness, prevent and manage fire risks and with adequate funding. this community programme could be financed by a specific regulation with its own financing or by the individual allocation of a budget line at the level of the eafrd or leader+, as an oral amendment will be presented. the european parliament must therefore give a clear answer to the people it represents, who have suffered directly from natural disasters and who naturally expect our support.
on behalf of the pse group. dear commission, dear members, in recent years europe has been affected by natural disasters which have caused hundreds of deaths and considerable economic and environmental damage to the affected regions. portugal in particular, together with other mediterranean regions, experienced the driest year in the last 105 years in 2005. in december, about 87% of the portuguese territory was in a state of extreme drought. this situation was particularly severe in the algarve region, where the climatic conditions were exceptional, with the combination of high temperatures and dry air. in the algarve, the natural disaster of the drought in 2005, preceded in 2003 by the devastation caused by forest fires, had serious repercussions on local infrastructure, natural and cultural heritage, the environment and agricultural and tourist activities. the water supply to the population has been clearly affected, both in terms of scarcity and compliance with the required quality standards. it is well known that natural disasters occur when extreme weather conditions affect a vulnerable area. it is therefore urgent to reduce the fragility of these regions. european cooperation in civil protection is needed to provide a rapid response to affected areas and to increase prevention and rapid response preparedness in emergency situations. this is what these owninitiative reports are intended to do and to articulate. the european union has a long history of supporting the development of the social dimension in the european union. with this in mind, it is important to recognise that almost all the affected areas are classified areas by the european union and that after the devastation we cannot simply consider that our civil responsibility has been fulfilled. the restoration of lost ecosystems is crucial to the balance of these areas and this also requires solidarity. it is also crucial to increase information and awareness among people and regions vulnerable to natural disasters, to reduce the risks and consequences of natural disasters and to make them aware of what they can do to preserve the natural resources in the region. solidarity has been a keyword in the european union since the treaty of rome. let us not, however, let it become just another empty word in the community jargon.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, we have tabled amendments to the report on the solidarity fund because we consider that in its current version it does not cover aspects which we consider to be of the utmost importance, in particular the maintenance of the criterion of regional disasters. the new proposal for the solidarity fund should address the difficulties encountered in applying it since its creation in 2002. we believe that the fund should be adapted to the specificities and real needs of the various countries facing disasters of a very different and particular nature, such as those on the mediterranean coast. we have therefore put forward a proposal which aims precisely at reintroducing the consideration of extraordinary regional disasters, as provided for in the current fund regulation. it should be stressed that this position is shared by the opinion of the economic and social council which considers it necessary to continue to take account of disasters with a serious regional impact and that, in the same vein, the report on natural disasters by the committee on regional development under discussion today considers that the fund should be considered when the majority of the population of a region is the victim of a disaster with serious and lasting repercussions on their living conditions. the portuguese parliament also adopted a resolution which considers that the possibility of supporting regional disasters with a significant socioeconomic and environmental impact in disadvantaged regions of the european union should be maintained. we have also put forward proposals to make the promotion of support for the restoration of productive activity in areas affected by disasters and the emergency provision of ground and airborne forest firefighting equipment expressly eligible for support. finally, we proposed that, as is the case with the structural and cohesion fund regulations, the allocation of the amount of financial assistance under the solidarity fund should take account of the level of economic and social development of a region or a member state. among other things, the new proposal for a regulation only stresses that we consider it a negative step to extend the scope of the fund without increasing its financial ceiling. we also believe that priority should be given to natural disasters. we consider it a bad thing that the mobilization threshold is being lowered in such a way that the countries of the european union with the highest gross domestic product are clearly the most beneficiaries.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, energy saving is indeed a factor that reduces europe's dependence on an essential commodity, contributes to sustainable development and, by avoiding waste, increases competitiveness. these are therefore objectives of great importance and timeliness, as was stressed by the rapporteur and the commissioner. there seems to be convergence of objectives, the biggest problem we face is how to move from objectives to practice, how to change habits and practices of waste. the text we are about to adopt is an important contribution in this respect too. as rapporteur, i would like to thank the rapporteur for the quality of his report and his cooperation in accepting a substantial number of proposed amendments, and i would point out only three points: first, the liberalisation of energy markets must be accompanied by the quality of regulation. secondly, the harmonization of standards must also be done at international level. thirdly, fiscal differentiation is needed in favour of more efficient practices and, finally, i think that in policy coherence there should be a place for the structural and cohesion funds to sponsor energy-saving measures and actions, especially in cities, in conjunction with the upgrading and rationalisation of transport systems. there are four suggestions i would like to highlight.
