the following is the report by mr boguslaw sonik, on behalf of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, on the prohibitions resulting from convictions for sexual offences against children [14207/2004 - c6-0244/2004 - 2004/0818 (cns)) [a6-0068/2006]:
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on thursday at 11 a.m.
mr president, i would first like to congratulate mrs niebler on her work and also mrs vergnaud, my group's shadow rapporteur. i welcome this initiative by the commission to modernise and simplify community law in the field of equal treatment between women and men in the labour market. there is still a lot of discrimination linked to women's work: wage inequality, difficulty in accessing the labour market itself, especially to well-paid and socially prestigious jobs. and yet the lisbon strategy calls for greater participation of women in the labour market and also more and better jobs for women. thirdly, i would like to reiterate the proposals i made in my reports on the lisbon strategy in the gender perspective and on demographic change. it is urgent that member states adopt measures to enable women to better balance their personal and professional lives. the review of the parental leave directive should help to combat the economic, social and cultural prejudices associated with the right to paternity leave. the member states should introduce paid maternity and paternity leave at the birth or adoption of a child and should naturally follow best practice in terms of the length of maternity leave, which ranges from 14 to 28 weeks, the mandatory period, the amount of pay received during leave and these measures will certainly help to ensure that women are not discriminated against and can have the children they want.
it is essential, mr president, that the principle of equal opportunities and equal treatment for men and women in access to employment and in professional activities should be applied in the various fields, as provided for in the directive we are voting on today, which brings together a number of existing community provisions, including the case law of the european court of justice. the political will to implement the legislative proposals envisaged here is needed in all member states to combat discrimination still existing, in particular in pay, access to employment, vocational training and promotion, including harassment and the sexual harassment that often arises in connection with it, as well as any unfavourable treatment of a woman in connection with pregnancy or maternity. equally important is the recognition that equal treatment in employment and occupation cannot be limited to the adoption of legislative measures and effective legal protection, and also requires awareness campaigns and the creation of child, maternity and paternity support infrastructures and equipment.
in writing. i congratulate my colleague, mr jorgo chatzimarkakis, on his excellent and timely report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council establishing a framework programme for competitiveness and innovation (2007-2013), which i support, particularly as regards the concern to orient the framework programme towards potential applicants, and thus towards its direct beneficiaries. the potential applicant should be given the opportunity, before the application procedure is introduced, to be clearly informed of the forms of support proposed by the framework programme. i also agree with the rapporteur that it is necessary to find a one-stop shop for the framework programme, which will facilitate contact with the partners. i also agree with the rapporteur that the application process must be simplified. finally, i would like to mention the importance of this framework programme for smes in the various regions of the european union and, in particular, for smes in the outermost regions of the eu, which should benefit from this important framework programme in order to help them overcome the heavy constraints affecting them, as set out in article 299 (2) of the ec treaty.
in writing. the commission proposal fills a long-standing gap in public health in the european union, the practical consequences of which have in some cases resulted in dependence on the american or asian pharmaceutical industry. the development of specific medicines for children, rather than the usual dose reduction, provides a better fit to their metabolism and a faster and more effective treatment. the requirement to submit a 'risk management system' for these types of medicines before they are placed on the market creates a very important measure which should allow the avoidance/minimisation of risks and ensure the effectiveness of treatments in such a vulnerable group as the paediatric population. the rapporteur takes due care to ensure that the necessary studies are carried out in order to make the use of these medicinal products appropriate for paediatric use without, however, prejudicing or delaying the development of the same product for adults. at the same time, it allows, in certain cases, a request for a postponement of the submission of the 'paediatric research plan' without delaying the placing on the market of the adult version. i therefore support the commission's proposal and the report by mrs grossetête.
in writing. i voted in favour of the françoise grossetête report on paediatric medicines at second reading because i believe that the design of medicines specifically designed for children should be promoted, taking into account the specificities of their metabolism. the establishment of a paediatric committee within the european medicines agency should ensure the monitoring of scientific research in this field, in particular by seeking to restrict the conduct of scientific tests to the minimum necessary.
in writing. in labour market matters, it is regrettable to note the glaring inequalities between men and women in various aspects such as pay, access to employment, vocational training, working conditions and career development. i voted in favour of this report because it clearly points in the direction of applying the principle of equal opportunities and equal treatment for men and women in areas related to employment and occupation. i also supported this report, which arises out of the need for more initiatives to improve the balance between private and professional life. by bringing together the various initiatives on equal treatment in a single document, the existing legal framework is not only simplified, but the level of protection is also modernised by integrating the evolution of the case law of the court of justice. i cannot but regret that, despite being enshrined in the eu treaty and in various directives, equal treatment is a dream that has yet to be realised, since it is only a vague political principle with a very poor implementation.
in writing. it is never too late to stress, especially today, when we commemorate world children's day, the responsibility of the law, the states and the union to make the defence of the rights of children, who are our future and make up about one fifth of the union's population, one of their priorities. i support the creation of this framework decision on the recognition and enforcement in the eu of prohibitions resulting from convictions for sexual offences against children, as well as the amendments proposed by the rapporteur. it is a fundamental step towards improving cooperation between member states in the protection of children. in addition, it has a dual purpose:- to improve access to information on prohibitions (with their mandatory entry in the criminal record); and- to make their enforcement mandatory. this prevents an individual who has been convicted of paedophilia in one member state from being prohibited from engaging in activities involving contact with children from circumventing that prohibition by taking up residence in another member state. such an injunction in one member state should produce legal effects in the other member states, thus extending the application of the principle of mutual recognition to injunctions and prohibitions.
in writing. while it is true that the latest developments in israel show positive signs, in particular the results achieved by a party with a clear desire for dialogue and the search for agreement, the same cannot be said of the palestinian authority's electoral results. the victory there, although legitimate from the point of view of electoral legality, is doubly worrying. first of all, because it has allowed a political group to come to power which, by not recognising israel's right to exist, does not accept the minimum indispensable to a peace process. it also shows that the people under the jurisdiction of the palestinian authority did not give priority to a negotiated solution to this longstanding conflict in that election. in this context, it is essential that the european union, and the quartet as a whole, agree on the next steps. firmness towards the pa government, but openness and availability towards president mahmoud abbas and his initiatives to seek a general agreement on the only acceptable solution: the peaceful coexistence of two states. given the importance of the european union's donor role, it is hoped and expected that on this external front 'europe' will show the capacity to influence the situation positively.
in writing. we have no doubt that a tough and ruthless fight against terrorism is needed. however, it cannot and must not under any circumstances call into question or even betray the values and principles on which our civilization is founded. i am in solidarity with the concerns expressed about the situation at guantanamo and i support the call here for an end to such situations and for the immediate closure of these detention centres. the capture and continued detention, in the circumstances in which the prisoners are held, is contrary to the geneva conventions and other international humanitarian instruments. whatever measures are taken in relation to these prisoners, they must be taken in full respect of human rights and the rule of law. every prisoner shall be formally charged with the crimes with which he is charged and shall have a fair trial before a competent, impartial and independent tribunal. if convicted, he should, of course, be subject to a sentence that reflects the gravity and inhumanity of the terrible acts he has committed. i hope that at the next transatlantic summit in vienna you will take the opportunity to press the united states to close guantanamo and to find the fairest and quickest solution to the situation of its approximately 500 prisoners.
in writing. i reaffirm what i said in october 2004 on this matter. we are totally outraged by terrorism and remember with full solidarity the terrible suffering of its victims and their families. we have no hesitation in saying that this is the greatest struggle of democracies today, faced with this terrible barbaric attack on fundamental rights - as the tragedies of 11 september and the 11 march are a terrible and unforgivable example. but at the same time we say, and we say this without any hesitation, that the west must maintain the highest moral standing in this fight, by giving unconditional demonstrations of the values it defends. we therefore want to see clarification of cases where allegations are made of violations of human rights, fundamental guarantees and universal conventions. and we advocate that the values of civilization that we affirm and believe in be respected. i therefore supported the postponement of the vote in order to allow us to take a more mature and informed decision in two weeks' time in strasbourg.
in writing. the united states of america is europe's greatest and best ally. any discussion of relations between the two sides of the atlantic must start from this premise, to which two key ideas must be added: the fact that we are potentially competitors in many areas does not make us less of an ally, the fact that we are the best ally does not confuse us. we are distinct actors, with projects, purposes and interests that do not always coincide, but we are partners in the same project of society, in the same concept of human community. the last few years have revealed difficulties which, in most cases, are solvable. the idea that the united states has created an internal division in europe is false. the truth is that the eu is not itself a single entity with a singular view of the realities of foreign policy. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. there is a wider reality underlying transatlantic economic relations to which we must be attentive when we approach this issue. the european union and the united states of america play a unique role in world trade. for this reason, there are three aspects which i consider to be fundamental in a debate on this subject. first of all, loyalty. trade relations between the two must be based on good faith and effective implementation of the agreements, as well as effective protection of the rights of american and european economic operators (including both producers and consumers). secondly, cooperation in the international context. although the factors of disagreement and competition are obvious and obvious, it should be possible to reach an understanding useful for the promotion of a fairer, more transparent, more development-friendly world trade on a global scale. finally, it shares the concerns and solutions of the two sides on the main challenges facing them on a global scale. whether it is directly in the economic area (think, for example, of the energy question, the growth of economic powers such as china or india, world poverty), or in the field of security, among others.
in writing. no one doubts that any member state wishing to join the eurozone must meet the maastricht convergence criteria laid down in the ec treaty. the european parliament has always in the past been in favour of these criteria being met strictly and without exception. although the econ committee in its report chose not to focus on recommendations on the degree of preparedness of individual countries, the truth is that this vote was mainly about the negative recommendation on lithuania which, although meeting all the convergence criteria, showed a slight divergence in the inflation criterion. in fact, in the last 12 months this country has exceeded, if only very slightly, the limit value. this has led me to consider amendment no 2 reasonable and to vote in favour of it, which calls for a clear and comprehensive explanation of the calculations made to assess the criteria relating to inflation and for the commission to update its report on this country with a view to its rapid accession to the euro area.
in writing. while trade is an important instrument for development and poverty reduction, there is no doubt that real progress towards these objectives cannot be achieved without fair rules at the international level. however, finding solutions to guide the contribution of trade policy to solving the poverty problem does not seem to be an easy task. the opening of frontiers to international trade thus brings enormous benefits for the development of societies. however, we have seen that poor countries are not always prepared to protect themselves against adverse effects or to take advantage of the opportunities offered. i therefore believe that small adjustments to the wto trade negotiations on the environment, agriculture, raw materials, public services and health, as well as industrialisation, could provide greater benefit to these populations from the benefits of trade. finally, our role must continue to be to promote development and democracy support in developing countries as a way of anchoring their populations to their countries by providing them with decent and fair conditions for work and growth.
in writing. the green paper on energy efficiency forms the basis for the european commission's energy efficiency action plan, which is of great importance as it is a key document for issues such as combating climate change, environmental pollution, the misuse of natural resources and the security of energy supply. the rapporteur points to strategic and very important points in order to achieve the 20% reduction in energy consumption in the european union by 2020 proposed by the european commission. raising awareness, educating and motivating people to change their behaviour and consumption habits, encouraging the use of cogeneration technologies, the exemplary role of the public sector in using cleaner transport and efficient lighting and the use of energy-saving contracts are simple measures that can translate into large energy savings. the rapporteur also paid particular attention to the instability of the energy market and the recent oil price rises, which make the current framework different from that which existed when the commission drafted the green paper. i therefore agree with the report by mr alejo vidal-quadras.
in writing. i voted in favour of the véronique de keyser report because it makes a good diagnosis of the situation, in the triple sense: women victims, women instruments of peace and women instruments of war. the report also complains that, despite all the resolutions and recommendations of various european and international institutions, women do not participate in conflict prevention and resolution, nor in peacekeeping operations, etc. the recommendation to draw up a practical action programme to identify the constraints is therefore justified.
in writing. i have had the opportunity to address the issues of post-conflict rehabilitation as rapporteur on this subject in the acp-eu parliamentary assembly. the introduction of the gender dimension in conflict prevention and resolution was considered urgent, as was the participation of women in the political decision-making process and their association with the framework for defining conflict resolution strategies. i reiterate the need to give particularly strong support to women fighters and refugees who are victims of physical violence, rape and sexual abuse. these shocking cases cannot but challenge us and call for our most resolute action and solidarity. i regret that the rapporteur insists on exploiting the suffering of women in conflict situations in order to impose and export her conception of 'sexual and reproductive health', including the promotion of abortion, which is not even supported by all member states. as i have said before, i will not vote for any text which does not clarify this concept and extend its scope beyond the prevention of sexually transmitted diseases, including hiv/aids, and ensuring women have the necessary conditions for pregnancy, childbirth and the postpartum period.

the recommendation for second reading of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety on the common position adopted by the council with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council establishing an infrastructure for spatial information in the european community (inspire) (12064/2/2005 - c6-0054/2006 - 2004/0175 (cod)) (rapporteur: frieda brepoels) (a6-0081/2006) is hereby adopted.
on behalf of the pse group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on this excellent report and i would like to congratulate the commission on the presentation of this directive. together with my colleague seeber and other colleagues, i visited some of the countries most affected by the floods and we were able to observe the damage caused by the 2005 floods on the ground. during our visit to germany and austria, we listened to the concerns of the people, collected suggestions from the regional authorities and observed examples of good practice in flood risk prevention and management. this contact with reality was a very useful experience for the preparation of our reports. natural disasters tend to occur more frequently and with greater frequency. these are no longer events that happen once in a century, but every four years, every two years, and their consequences are increasingly dramatic. in central europe, for example, in bavaria, there were major floods in 1999, 2002 and 2005. this year, not only in germany but also in other countries such as the czech republic, slovakia, hungary and austria, thousands of people have had to leave their homes and several factories have had to shut down. the governments of some member states have even declared a state of emergency in several regions and there are already casualties. cyclically, natural disasters leave a trail of destruction and death. flooded cities, destroyed houses, millions upon millions of euros of damage and serious social and environmental problems are some of the visible consequences of floods. according to the world health organization, natural disasters kill hundreds of people every year. commissioner dimas said we should be ambitious. so let's be ambitious in disaster prevention and creative in finding answers to questions like: what can we do to prevent a natural phenomenon from turning into a disaster? what can be done to prevent so many human casualties, ecological disasters, and social and economic problems resulting from natural disasters? the un secretary-general, kofi annan, said that we must move from a culture of reaction to a culture of prevention and there is evidence that prevention works. comparing the 2002 and 2005 floods in bavaria, we find that in 2002 there were hundreds of victims and high losses and that in 2005, despite the intensity being five times higher, the damage was 30% lower.
author: mr verheugen, the presentation last march of the commission communication entitled 'a renewed european tourism policy towards a strengthened partnership for tourism in europe' could and should be an opportunity to discuss the next steps to be taken by the community institutions with the aim of boosting the tourism industry in europe. unfortunately, that is not the case. the world today is not the world we were in 15 or 20 years ago, when the economy was growing fast and vigorously, distributing wealth among the citizens of europe. in today's world, the global economy presents new challenges, but also new attractions. there is a different reality that requires different answers. our development model is outdated and will be ineffective if we don't fix it. europe therefore needs to meet development challenges where it can be competitive and sustainable, where it has comparative advantages with economic potential. that is the case with tourism. we certainly cannot compete with exotic destinations, but we have a history, a heritage and an attractive potential that is unmatched and of enormous diversity. we all know that the european tourism industry is one of the sectors best placed to respond to the challenges of the global economy. difficult to move and easily adaptable, it is able to meet quality and environmental protection requirements, it is able to meet the needs of further training, it can combat seasonality if it is able to adapt to new audiences and it has growth potential. it would therefore be expected that the commission, in presenting a new communication on the subject, would bring something new and respond to the challenges set out by this parliament in the resolution on the future of sustainable tourism in europe, which was adopted in september last year. on the contrary, the commission has produced a document which is not very innovative and in which it very rarely takes advantage of the initiatives which this parliament has put saying, and i quote, 'that it will take the opportunity to raise awareness of these good practices, possibly by means of a prize for european destinations of excellence'. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, greater involvement of the european institutions is essential to strengthening the sustainable development of tourism. i therefore share the concerns which justified mr queiroz's question. first of all, because i come from a country, portugal, and more specifically from an ultraperipheral region, madeira, where tourism is one of the most important instruments for its economic and social development. secondly, although tourism is an area of competence of the member states, the union has an important role to play in this area through policy guidelines and actions at european level. the union's action to support, coordinate and complement the actions of the member states - as provided for in the treaty, which has not yet been ratified - represents an important added value for national policies and actions for the sustainable development of the tourism sector. in support of action at european level, i would like to mention two facts: the high economic and social importance of tourism, together with the importance of new information and communication technologies and the innovation it promotes, will make this sector one of the most important contributors to competitiveness and job creation in line with the lisbon strategy. secondly, the union is the world's leading tourist destination and union citizens are the best users of tourist services and the most sought-after tourist destinations in the union. finally, given the nature of the union's and the member states' powers in the field of tourism, to take account of the need for greater integration and cohesion between the actions of the union and those of the states and regions, i would advocate close cooperation, coordination and information not only between the union and the member states and regions, but also between the institutions themselves, parliament, the commission and the council. this is why this moral issue is so important in order to inspire the necessary commitment on the part of the commission and the council to follow up the relevant initiatives proposed by parliament for sustainable development, in particular by creating the europe destination, the european union brand, the guarantee of safety and the safeguarding of tourists' rights.
mr president, i would like to stress just a few points. firstly, the importance of research for the success of the lisbon strategy. secondly, that there is a need to develop and deepen research on climate change and its relationship with natural disasters. research is also needed to solve the energy problem. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. i therefore welcome the consensus proposal put forward by some members, in particular mrs gutiérrez and mr busquin, and i call on members to support this proposal.
in writing. we voted in favour of this report, which supports the conclusion of the protocol on mountain farming. the protocol was initialled by the community at the ministerial conference of the alpine convention held in chambéry on 20 december 1994. subordinated to the overall objective of sustainable development, the protocol on mountain agriculture aims, as stated in article 1, to ensure and promote appropriate and environmentally compatible agriculture in the alpine region as an essential contribution to the maintenance of populated areas and sustainable economic activities. this includes high quality typical products, the safeguarding of the natural environment, protection against natural hazards and the preservation of the beauty and value of the landscape. the contracting parties shall optimise the multifunctional role of mountain farming. support for disadvantaged areas such as the alpine region, characterised by its wealth of natural resources, including water, agricultural potential, historical and cultural heritage, quality of life and economic and recreational activities, is essential not only for local populations but also for other populations. however, it is also characterised by difficult living and agricultural production conditions due to geomorphological and climatic conditions.
in writing. we are now facing a second reading of the directive on the protection of groundwater against pollution. this is to safeguard a natural resource essential to life, since its reserves are the main source of drinking water supply. the main problems at this stage are, on the one hand, reconciling the extension of the scope of the directive with the principle of subsidiarity and, on the other hand, the implications of some measures for agricultural practices and the need to introduce some amendments, which should imply, as the rapporteur argues, the provision of community aid within the framework of the cap. the rapporteur also stresses that agreement must be reached on the methods of measuring groundwater pollution, arguing that this should be done on the basis of comparable thresholds. the council, in its common position, refers to the exclusive responsibility of the member states to establish quality standards for groundwater. this is why we insist on proposals which allow some comparison and studies of the impact and effectiveness of this regulatory framework so that a new assessment can be made some time after its application.
in writing. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of groundwater was put to the vote at first reading to follow up article 17 of the water framework directive (2000/60/ec) which provides for the adoption by the council and parliament of measures promoting the protection and improvement of groundwater quality. the council's common position after the first reading has certain technical gaps, lack of clarity and ambition which are made up by the amendments introduced by the rapporteur, who is also trying to achieve the best possible framework with the framework directive. the reintroduction of the 'emissions principle' (as set out in the groundwater directive 80/68/ec) to achieve the objective of article 4 of the framework directive, 'protecting groundwater from pollution and deterioration', the highest restriction applied to substances listed in annex viii of the framework directive, in order to avoid long-term contamination and therefore also the need for recovery measures, are important changes introduced. amendment no 36 also, which eliminates the exemption of agricultural soils from the limits for compliance with the values laid down for nitrates, is of particular importance, since it ensures consistency between the protection and quality objectives to be achieved.
in writing. it is good that there is an assessment and management of flood risks. although it is a natural phenomenon, human intervention can increase the risks or lessen their effects. the sharp reduction in the natural capacity of watersheds to retain floods, the mismanagement of human activities (such as the increase in human settlements and economic assets in floodplains and the erosion and reduction of natural water retention by land through deforestation in watersheds) and other phenomena, in particular drought, contribute to the increase and likelihood of the adverse effects of floods. to date, there is no legal instrument at european level to protect against flood risk. in order to protect the principle of solidarity and without prejudice to the principle of subsidiarity, the management of flood risks and mitigation measures should therefore not be limited to the support provided for in the european union solidarity fund. it is particularly important in cases of river basin management that cross two or more countries, which implies the coordination and implementation of other relevant policies of the member states and the community, in particular as regards water transport policy, agricultural policy and cohesion policy. although not all the proposals have our support, the report is overall positive.
in writing. the european parliament, following previous softening of its position on the unacceptable us detention at guantanamo, adopted a resolution four years later, in which it 'reiterates its call on the us administration to close the detention centre'. the ep also condemns torture, including what are euphemistically called 'special interrogation techniques', such as sexual humiliation, asphyxiation by immersion in water, the application of electric shocks, and other cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment. this is in line with the demand of all those who have always denounced this unacceptable, brutal and inhuman situation. the european parliament has also called for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu's security is not compromised. the ep also fails to point out that the detention at guantanamo is not an isolated situation, but rather part of a us-led offensive against international law, conventions and the un charter, an offensive which must be denounced and with which we cannot agree.
in writing. the issue of prisoners in the 'war on terror' is the place where we must respond to the greatest challenge that terrorism poses to us: fully guarantee the security of our citizens without losing our values. in this struggle, in which we must be associated, the paradigms we have known are not proving to be sufficient. the geneva convention combatants (properly uniformed and identified) do not exist in this war. on the other hand, to treat soldiers of a war as common criminals would be a legal error and a folly in terms of security. i therefore believe that first of all it is urgent to find a new legal framework for the situation underlying the detentions at guantánamo. that said, and recognizing the exceptional nature of this moment, it is nevertheless desirable and defensible that the fundamental principles of international law be adopted and adapted. but we must defend it without the hypocrisy of those who delegate the hard work to others. guantánamo is an evil, and an evil we wish to see ended. but, while recognizing that the international legal system lacks an adequate response to the new reality of the terrorist threat, i believe that it is up to the states to seek a new solution that is humane, just and safe. in short, we must review the law.

the following are statements by the council and the commission on the 17th eu-russia summit (26 may 2006).
on behalf of the ppe-de group. this ambitious europe is still in the prehistory of its criminal law. vague consensus and timid progress show how states resist the future, show the unbearable contradiction of a political community which asserts itself on common fundamental values, but which leaves to the taste of each state precisely the right which guarantees these values. the irony is that the constitutional treaty tried to erase it and that the court intuited the best of interpretations. as long as the european political institutions say that european criminal law is based on the simple principle of mutual recognition, europe will not have a criminal project, it will not have an area of freedom, security and justice in the true sense of the word, because europe is a global project of justice, it is not a project of preferential areas of justice. but what europe is showing is the absence of a common space, with a common project in the criminal field, a patchwork of borders, inconsistent harmonization of minimum sentences without following a political or criminal programme, harmonization of the minimum limit of maximum penalties, showing our lack of audacity. apparent harmonisation only by the sanction, without covering the elements of the crime, alternative penalties, forms of execution. a europe which proclaims the dignity of all and the values which guarantee it, the rule of law, proportionality and equality, calls for a criminal justice programme, but what it shows is a criminal law which is absurdly separate from the values it guarantees in the framework of the powers of the pillars, a criminal law which is affirmed almost only as a security within the walls of the council, without an effective democratic sharing of the parliaments. what it shows is the mutual recognition of particular penal systems without an essential basis of harmonization, a true chancel of iniquity. that is what we do not want and what europe is showing, because this area of criminal law is the area par excellence of values. we are waiting for the treaty to open up the field and, even before that, for a strong political will which is slow to arrive.
mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, the european parliament has long been calling for a new legal framework for data protection under the third pillar, comparable to the rules in force in community law. we want to ensure the same level of protection, while taking into account the specific nature of police and judicial work. we must recognize that there is insufficient protection at the moment. the recent adoption of the proposal for a directive on data retention was already accompanied by a clear call for the appropriate safeguards to be adopted rapidly under this framework decision. as rapporteur for the three legislative measures on the establishment of the schengen ii information system, i have sought to make the necessary changes to take account of the adoption of this framework decision and i have sent a letter to vice-president frattini asking the commission to update the data protection rules in the sis ii decision with a view to ensuring consistency, as it is of the utmost importance that the new rules apply to sis ii as they do to the vis. the resolution created by the court of justice's judgment of 30 may, which annulled the decisions on the transfer of pnr data to the united states of america, will pass through third pillar solutions, as commissioner frattini said last monday. all this reinforces the idea that it is urgent and fundamental to adopt a legal instrument to ensure the protection of personal data outside the first pillar. for all these reasons, the adoption of this framework decision is of the utmost urgency and importance. i congratulate mrs roure on her work and support the amendments she has tabled which were adopted in the libe committee. these proposals make clear what principles and safeguards we want to see ensured. i also support the rapporteur's request that we postpone the vote on the final resolution until the next plenary session.
mr president, mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, we want to improve the standards of quality and efficiency of justice. we know that this is a very sensitive area and one characterized by enormous diversity between the member states. this is why mutual trust needs to be strengthened so as to allow for the mutual recognition of judicial decisions. confidence in the quality and efficiency of the judicial system of the other partners of the union contributes to the progressive development of a european judicial culture. this framework decision is a further step in this direction and forms part of the reinforcement of the principle of mutual recognition of judgments in criminal matters imposing custodial sentences or measures. simplifying the transfer of sentenced persons to another member state of which they are nationals or with which they have close links can optimise the possibilities for rehabilitation and social reintegration. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr varvitsiotis, on his report and on the excellent proposals he has put forward, which i fully support and which have been unanimously supported by the libe committee. the appropriate guarantees must be given to the sentenced person, by ensuring that he is heard before the execution order is issued, as mrs cederschiöld has stressed. the principle of specialisation should also be safeguarded in order to ensure that he is not heard or judged in relation to acts other than those for which he has been convicted. it is also important that victims of convicted persons can be informed both of the existence of a request for recognition and transfer of the execution of the sentence and of the outcome of the proceedings and the transfer order. i also agree that in no case can the possibility of converting the penalty into a financial penalty or of aggravating the penalty imposed by the issuing state be accepted.
mr president, there is a growing problem of the use of stimulant drugs, particularly cocaine, and more and more young people are experimenting with drugs in europe, which clearly shows that there is still a lot to be done in the fight against drugs. the european monitoring centre for drugs and drug addiction has played an important role in compiling and disseminating information on drugs and drug use and has promoted the exchange of best practices and organisations in the member states. as mr pirker has already pointed out, it is important, however, that there are common criteria and standardised methods of data collection, because only then can these data be comparable, reliable and objective. the existing problem of data from some member states being poorly available or difficult to compare, which makes it very difficult to analyse the situation in the union, must be tackled quickly. i would like to congratulate my colleague frieda brepoels on this report and on the excellent result achieved by our adoption today of this proposal for a revision of the regulation after three years of negotiations, which is primarily concerned with changing the legal basis originally envisaged, placing the european parliament in a position of co-legislator. i would like to stress as a very positive development the strengthening of the role of the centre in order to take account of new trends in drug use, such as the use of a number of substances, which combine legal and illegal psychoactive substances, and the fact that the centre has adapted to the new post-enlargement reality, with the corresponding adaptation of the functioning of its bodies. finally, i would like to draw attention to the global nature of the problem of drug use, which means that we need to place the analysis in the european context in a broader context. it is also important to intensify cooperation with non-community countries, especially since most drugs entering the european union come from non-community countries.
the statements by the commission and the council prove that the next european council will continue to leave out the measures needed to change what president barroso has called european "christophilia", revealing that they do not want to understand the causes of the criticisms of the citizens of the various member states. the main reason for the discontent is the social crisis, which the council's proposal for conclusions only deals with marginally, referring to a report to be submitted by march 2007. it is in the interests of the community to make progress on liberalization, the directive on the establishment of the internal market in services and the common energy policy. the priority of the priorities, which is still omitted in the conclusions, but which was the main and practically exclusive subject of the president of the commission's speech, is the constitutional question. he stressed what the commission considers to be lost by not having advanced the process, forgetting that it was the functioning of democracy that led to the rejection of the european constitution by the people of france and the netherlands, which should be respected by the community institutions. by announcing new forms of propaganda, including the proposal for a declaration on political europe to be submitted next year for signature by all the community institutions, it is only pursuing a course which does not address the existing problems.
in writing. the european monitoring centre for drugs and drug addiction (emcdda), set up in 1993 and based in lisbon, has the task of collecting, analysing and disseminating objective, reliable and comparable information, thus providing a true picture of the phenomenon at european level. knowledge of the scale and nature of the drug problem is an indispensable condition for effective policy and action to combat it. although much progress has been made, much remains to be done to improve monitoring instruments and develop a genuine 'common language'. i voted in favour of this report on the new proposal on the emcdda put forward by the european commission. the main changes include the involvement of the european parliament in the co-decision process, the extension of the emcdda's role and the adaptation of the functioning of the emcdda bodies to take account of enlargement. the emcdda should obtain more objective and comparable data and engage in systematic evaluation of drug policies and drug use trends. the importance of better dissemination and the exchange of information on best practices in tackling the drug problem should also be stressed.
in writing. as the rapporteur, who is a well-known cypriot doctor in our group, points out, there is a lot of confusion in people's minds about avian influenza and the flu pandemic. many authorities and many people, he says, 'seem to equate the arrival of a/h5n1 in europe with the emergence of a flu pandemic. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the public authorities. it stresses, as i did in a previous report, the need for the european union to provide technical, scientific and economic assistance to the countries already affected and, in particular, to contribute to raising global awareness and to a coordinated master plan at international, regional, subregional and national level, with an appropriate roadmap and timetables. the rapporteur is therefore trying to improve the european commission's proposal and clarify a number of aspects, which is why we voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i'd like to start by reminding you that the confusion in people's minds about avian influenza and pandemic influenza is massive. there is therefore clearly a lot to be done in the field of communication. as policy makers we cannot neglect our duty to protect citizens by helping to ensure that the necessary means are in place to give a decisive response to any public health threat posed to our societies. as is well known, the threat of a flu pandemic is a european public health issue of concern to everyone. however, there are many questions as to the accuracy of this possibility. since the risk to human health is considered to be very low by the competent authorities, it seems to me essential to establish an optimized mechanism for prevention and rapid response in cases of public health crises, which, as called for in this report, includes an optimized plan for coordinating actions at all decision-making levels and includes accurate and accessible communication to all citizens so that they are prepared in the event of a need. in this context, i voted in favour of mr amadou's report.
in writing. this agreement recognised that the european commission, supported by parliament, was right to challenge the framework decision on the protection of the environment through criminal law, recognising that the protection of the environment in the eu requires concerted action by criminalising the most serious offences. its purpose and substance therefore fall within the community's powers in environmental matters (ec treaty) and not within the provisions of the teu on police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. recognising that the community does not have jurisdiction in criminal matters in general, it sets a useful precedent for the communityisation of matters falling within the third pillar and strengthens parliamentary control over such a sensitive area as criminal law. the consequences will be enormous both for the adoption of future legal instruments and for those already in force, which will have to be based on a new legal basis, the first pillar, which implies the involvement of parliament as a co-legislator. a framework decision in the field of the environment has been annulled, but its consequences should be felt beyond this area, affecting the whole of community policies as well as fundamental freedoms, when it is necessary to resort to criminal law measures to ensure their effectiveness.
in writing. i congratulate my colleague tatjana zdanoka on her important report on a framework strategy for combating discrimination and equal opportunities for all, which i support, particularly as regards the request to the member states to take due account in their legislative practice of the various grounds of discrimination, in order to give the latter a credibility which has so far been weakened by its non-legally binding nature. the fight against discrimination must necessarily be based on education, the promotion of best practices and campaigns targeted at the general public and at areas and sectors where discrimination exists. awareness of the social effects of this phenomenon is probably the most effective way of combating discrimination.
in writing. the successive enlargements of the european union are a success story unparalleled in the history of our continent. now, this is due, in short, to two orders of factors. on the one hand, the willingness, availability and constant ability of the member states to bring new partners into this project at any time, with all the benefits and also the burdens that any enlargement entails. on the other hand, this process has been successful because of the positive effect of the prospect of accession. the history of europe over the last fifty years is largely the history of a continent which has been gradually adhering to the values of western democracies by virtue of the expectations of accession. for these reasons, we must draw two conclusions at this stage with regard to the prospects for accession for bulgaria and romania. on the one hand, the eu's will and desire to pursue this enlargement must be unequivocal and the final timetable must be set at the next european council. on the other hand, it must be clear that accession will only take place when the real conditions are met. our demand is justified and has been fruitful - as the progress made by romania over the past year shows.
in writing. we voted against this motion for a resolution because it insists on support for the treaty establishing a constitution for europe. the aim of continuing to commit ourselves to the treaty as a whole, in defiance of the position taken by the people of france and the netherlands in last year's referendums, is unacceptable. how can we continue to talk about the need to deepen democracy when the decisions freely taken by the people in democratic referendums are not respected? it is a hypocrisy which demonstrates the deep estrangement which exists today between the people and the elites of the community institutions. we also disagree with the propaganda campaign that is being announced, with the multiplication of parliamentary forums to meet the dates that they insist, in particular, as they refer to in the resolution, that there be a 'constitutional solution' when the elections to the european parliament are called in 2009. what was needed was more attention to social problems and a full response to the aspirations of the people for improved welfare, development and economic and social cohesion.
in writing. firstly, the debate on the future of europe is not limited to the constitutional debate, nor does the debate on the constitutional treaty exhaust the debate on the future of europe. as for the latter, i do not think it is the most glamorous and appealing to the citizens, although it is necessary - even if i doubt its urgency. and it must certainly be carried out in full view of the citizens. in my view, however, what is really needed is to update and consolidate the eu's structural and decision-making model in a democratic framework that respects national identity and diversity, since the eu as designed can hardly withstand a life of 25 and even less of 27, 28 or 29. i therefore believe that the solution may be to discuss it again at a time when the societies that are most hostile to this proposal are showing a new willingness, or it may be to delimit the 'constitutional' aspiration to a more modest and realistic institutional reform indispensable to the new life in the eu. but above all, we must respond to what really concerns the citizens, particularly in the economic sphere. lack of policy, lack of results, lack of growth and jobs in an economy that is hopelessly changing. the truth is that these challenges are, for our fellow citizens, priorities over the constitution.
on behalf of the pse group. – mr president, small arms and light weapons are weapons of mass destruction in the developing world. it is estimated that they kill half a million people each year. their long-term impact on sustainable development is undeniable. fighting them means finding creative ways to bridge the gap between security sector reform and development assistance. the latest reports by the un institute for disarmament research on european action on small arms and light weapons stresses that the eu should create more synergies between the relevant cfsp and community instruments. also, fighting the scourge of illegal brokering should be a priority. this parliament has repeatedly expressed its disappointment at the lack of specific legislation in many eu countries, despite the adoption of the 2003 common position. finally, the eu can play a decisive role in making sure that the review conference on the un programme of action on small arms and light weapons is successful, and a follow-up conference must therefore be organised. we are counting on the austrian presidency to steer that process. success would mean agreement on a global set of principles on arms transfers which, as a minimum, should ensure that all transfers are authorised through a permit or licence, that existing obligations and relevant international law are respected, that arms embargoes imposed by the un security council are respected and enforced, and that the issuing of permits or licences should take into account the risk of exported arms being used in serious violations of human rights or international humanitarian law, including the risk that such arms might be diverted into the wrong hands such as those of terrorists and that this may affect regional or internal security and stability. the un review conference should, of course, start work on a legally-binding international arms trade treaty as soon as its work is complete. i am very honoured to be a member of parliament’s delegation to that review conference.

on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, coastal fishing, in particular small-scale coastal fishing and artisanal fishing, makes a considerable contribution to the socioeconomic well-being of coastal communities, not only in portugal but also in other coastal states. as we have said, coastal fishing contributes to local development, the maintenance and creation of jobs upstream and downstream, the supply of fresh fish and the maintenance of local cultural traditions. the economic and social crisis in the fisheries sector, which is being exacerbated by the increase in fuel prices, is affecting the least competitive segments of the fleet, in particular coastal fishing. in our view, this crisis is also linked to the guidelines and implementation of the common fisheries policy and its failure to specifically recognise the needs of coastal fisheries. this fleet segment therefore needs to be supported not only at national but also at community level. we consider this report to be generally positive and stress the need to recognise the specific features of small-scale coastal fishing and artisanal fishing in the common fisheries policy and to adapt the present instruments to meet the needs of this sector, as well as the need to maintain in the future the european fisheries fund for aid to modernise and renew coastal and artisanal fishing. however, the report falls short of the immediate response to the problems of the current crisis and of the new instruments that must be created to bring about a real recognition of the specificity of this fleet segment. in this connection, we tabled two amendments, the first on the need to establish a community programme for small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing, which would not only support specific projects but also help to concentrate instruments and channel funds to coastal fishing; the second, taking into account the need for emergency measures to respond to the serious socioeconomic situation in the sector, proposes the creation of a temporary emergency transitional compensation to combat the effects of the sharp increase in fuel prices. we hope that these proposals can be supported by the house.
first of all, i would like to join all those who have had the opportunity to congratulate our colleague mr ó neachtain on the excellent work he has done and on his continued commitment to this issue which is so dear to us. i would like to say that coastal fishing is a concept which must be defined in economic, social and environmental terms, also in terms of its techniques, but which must be seen geographically in the light of the reality to which it applies. i would like to draw the attention of the commission and our colleagues to the outermost regions such as the azores and madeira, where there are no continental shelves and where the equivalent of the coast is actually the coastal banks, which are sometimes located at great distances from the islands but which are, for all intents and purposes, exactly the same as the coast close to the land is for other continental regions. this is extremely important for us because without this adaptation we will not be able to understand the reality of these regions and i would therefore strongly urge the commission to take this into account.
i too would like to congratulate our rapporteur on the excellent work he has done and to join in the general comments made by our colleagues from various political groups, including my colleague bart staes, who very timely raised the problem of agriculture, which is a burning issue in community funds. but above all, i would like to say to the commission, face to face, that what my colleague ayala sender has told us here about the conviction of olaf by the court of first instance of the european communities in case 309/2003 cannot, under any circumstances, be without consequences. it is not just a question of ordering the commission to pay compensation to an official of the european commission. it is a matter of condemning a whole series of investigative procedures developed by olaf which have not respected any of the rules which are essential to respect in a state governed by the rule of law, have not respected the principles of immunity and impartiality, have not given the accused any chance of defence and, finally, have made an investigation, and this is the fundamental scandal, instead of being directed against its real authors, be directed against those who had absolutely nothing to point to in this process. this cannot go on like this and if it does, i must say very clearly that i do not understand where the commission's transparency policy is going. there must be consequences. there is no rule of law that can see a decision like this from the court without all the consequences being drawn.
in writing. i voted in favour of the jerzy buzek report on the seventh framework programme of the european community for research, technological development and demonstration activities (2007-2013) because i believe that investment in research and technological development is key to the success of the lisbon strategy. investment in research on climate change and its relationship to natural disasters and on alternative energy sources to fossil fuels needs to be reinforced. i believe that research on embryonic stem cells from surplus embryos - a very promising area of research - which has been producing very encouraging results in the treatment of diseases such as parkinson's and alzheimer's, should be funded by this framework programme, after rigorous and case-by-case assessment by the ethics committees.
in writing. i consider this document to be one of the most important of this legislature, since it deals with the fundamental question of funding for research projects relating to technological development associated with different areas of intervention. in the fisheries chapter, i think the amendments tabled to ensure greater independence in the approach to the sector are entirely desirable and make perfect sense in the face of the crisis the sector is going through. only with more and better technology will it be possible to bring profitability and competitiveness back to the european fisheries sector. the creation of a specific chapter on fisheries and sustainable exploitation of the oceans in the seventh framework programme therefore deserves my unconditional support, as do all the other measures contained in the report.
in writing. in the european parliament's position on the seventh framework programme for 2007-13, we note a contradiction in some of the rhetoric surrounding it and its level of funding. while advocating a society geared towards 'knowledge, innovation and technology' at eu level, the eu budget allocation for these objectives has been reduced by some eur 21 million compared to the european commission's initial proposal. it should also be stressed that, in view of the priorities of this seventh framework programme, we see the attempt to regard research as just another 'product' to be marketed, and by the way, very profitable. in other words, we are faced in the seventh framework programme with the attempt to commercialise research at the expense of public research. despite the positive aspects of the proposal voted today, we believe that the priorities of such an important instrument should also include public research in the social and environmental fields, education and health. we therefore regret the rejection of some proposals that included, for example, safety at work and the prevention of occupational diseases, or the use of icts for sustainable development and social and economic inclusion. hence our vote.
in writing. the community framework programme for research and development is already of particular importance as it is one of the programmes with the largest financial allocation in the eu. divided into four specific programmes - cooperation, people, ideas and capacities - this framework programme acts as a driver for competitiveness and innovation in europe. of these specific programmes, i would highlight the 'cooperation' component, which also has the largest budget and aims to involve industry in research and development of new projects and to promote cooperation with research centres and universities. the importance of smes is also recognised, and their participation in this new framework programme is facilitated by the supporting role of technology platforms. finally, this programme reveals its importance in the context of regional development, since it provides for interconnection with the structural funds and recalls the need to take account of the regions of the convergence objective, which cover almost the whole of portuguese territory, in the allocation of financing, safeguarding the involvement of local and regional authorities in the decision on the allocation of funds for the construction of new infrastructure.
in writing. we insist that environmental policy can represent an important economic opportunity for direct and indirect job creation on a large scale, if innovation and industrial policies focus on promoting sustainable development. a macroeconomic framework is therefore needed to support the sustainable development of each country by strengthening employment, social cohesion and the environment. however, the current neoliberal policies are contrary to these objectives. the 'lisbon strategy' and the eu's monetary and fiscal policies have had negative consequences for economic growth and employment, as well as for the environment. we call attention to the fact that high levels of unemployment, poverty, social exclusion and income inequality continue to exist in the eu, and we therefore believe that the fight against income inequalities and the promotion of real convergence should be among the priorities of the economic and social agenda.
in writing. i did not vote in favour of the resolution against racism and homophobia, although i regard the substance of its content as very positive and consider it politically opportune. the objections - i abstained - are solely to the introduction of a reference to a portuguese 'case' which allegedly indicates the existence of a strong homophobic culture in portugal. the so-called gisberta case - which took place in porto - is only a juvenile delinquency act judged as such by portuguese society and handled correctly by the judicial authorities. there is therefore no reason why this case should be the subject of a resolution of this magnitude and importance.
in writing. we are in favour of technological solutions, including digital solutions, which help to improve train signalling and control systems, with a view to improving safety and eliminating congestion in rail transport. safety is all the more important when traffic speeds and capacity are substantially increased. but we already have doubts about claims that the proposed system, ertms, is superior to existing national systems. what it does is ensure greater cross-border interoperability, while never forgetting that this proposal is also part of the strategy for liberalising rail transport and the logic of an internal market. however, the central question is how the additional costs to railway undertakings will be financed. who will bear these costs and how will they be distributed among the member states in a context of constraints on the community budget? the same is true of the transeuropean networks and the european transport policy programmes, which have seen their funding cut in the next financial framework. we also have doubts about the conditionality of the use of the structural funds for transport to the implementation of this system alone. that is why we abstained.
in writing. coastal and artisanal fishing plays a key role in the local economy of several fishing communities. the lack of a regulatory framework applicable to the coastal sector has, however, affected this fishery segment and the whole industry associated with it. at a time when fleets need to be modernised and the workforce linked to the sector rejuvenated, solutions are urgently needed to reverse the aforementioned trend. i believe that the adoption of this report is a step forward in defending the interests of community fisheries and portuguese fisheries, and of the azores in particular. for all these reasons, i shall vote in favour of this report.
in writing. we regret that the proposals we put forward were rejected - despite the support of some 200 members - namely the creation of:- a community programme for small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing;- a temporary emergency transitional compensation to combat the effects of the increase in fuel prices. however, other proposals were approved and included in the original report and have now been confirmed. the following are highlighted:- recognition of the specific nature of small-scale coastal fishing and artisanal fishing in the common fisheries policy and adaptation of its instruments to the needs of this sector;- financing from the eff the renewal of vessels in this defunct segment;- creation of education and training programmes aimed at the entry of young fishermen in this sector;- financing of projects and actions of sector organisations and local authorities;- ensuring the participation of fishermen in the commercial process, revising the common customs tariff (cmo) for fishery products, ensuring fairer prices at first sale and a better distribution of value added;- ensuring the participation of fishermen and their representative organisations in the decision-making process of the common fisheries policy, in the protection of the marine environment and in the recovery of fisheries resources, applying the principle of co-management and decentralisation to the cfp.

uncompromisingly the sovereignty of the people of east timor, while fully respecting their free choice in the choice of their legitimate representatives, as well as the legitimacy and democratic functioning of the timorese institutions. reject the dynamics of external interference, in particular by regional powers, australia and indonesia, which would only contribute to aggravating the situation. promote genuine solidarity and cooperation with east timor that contributes to its economic and social development and the well-being of its people. the content of the present resolution, although it contains some of the concerns described above, is characterized by its partiality in its reading of the political situation, a partiality which carries the danger of fuelling internal and external attempts to take political advantage of the situation which could lead to new situations of tension. the european parliament must now show appreciation for and support for the actions and efforts of all the timorese institutions, without exception and with strict impartiality, which is not the case with this resolution. the resolution also ignores the real dangers of external interference which, as is well known, have shaped the course of events. this position carries two dangers: it directs all responsibility for the situation to one of the timorese sovereignty bodies and fails to warn of the future dangers of stabilization that more or less direct intervention maneuvers can have in a country still marked by the indonesian occupation and the destabilization maneuvers that armed militias have been consecutively trying to carry out. finally, we do not think it appropriate to raise the question of the presence of blue helmets at this stage. the fact is that the military forces stationed in the territory should remain only until the situation is stabilized, subject to their national chains of command on the one hand and to the timorese political power on the other, in accordance with the terms of bilateral agreements with the constitutional framework of that country and the rules of international law. in conclusion, we believe that this resolution does not reflect the full complexity and evolution of the situation on the ground.
author. i recently witnessed in dili the beginning of the last period of violence among timorese, which included tragic clashes between police and military and segments of both forces. i also witnessed with regret a dramatic moment of institutional unity, when the president, the prime minister and the president of parliament were forced to ask for the help of foreign forces to restore order and political stability to the country. i would like to highlight the enthusiastic welcome given by the timorese people to the arrival of the gnr, a portuguese police force and therefore also a european one. the timorese authorities also showed unity and convergence on the requests they presented to the un security council two days ago, namely for the reinforcement and extension of unotil with a police mission under un supervision and possibly, if necessary, a peacekeeping mission under un mandate and leadership. this resolution of the european parliament supports these calls and shows the concern of this parliament and the european union for the situation, but also the confidence that, with the help of friends, east timor will be able to overcome this serious crisis. we european socialists remain convinced that the timorese people will overcome this crisis of democratic growth, as they have overcome other crises that are much more serious and even existential. but we also know that much depends on us as europeans and on the international community as a whole. in fact, the international community has a particular responsibility to ensure that the state of east timor has the future it deserves, the timorese people, who have fought so hard against oppression and for the independence and sovereignty of their country. as kofi annan said this week, what is happening in east timor is particularly painful because the country, and i quote, "is a child of the international community". the fragile foundations of timor's young democracy have been exposed in this crisis. kofi annan has stressed: "not only timorese but the entire international community should learn important lessons from this case". certain permanent members of the security council will have to put their hands on the conscience. nations with strong democratic institutions are not built in a few years and in a hurry. declaring mission accomplished early to save money ends up costing you dearly and the people pay the most. the situation is however amenable to correction and no one should call into question the viability of the independent and sovereign state of east timor, particularly with regard to the country's important natural resources. ian martin, head of unamed, who helped deliver the baby in 1999 and was recently the un secretary-general's envoy to dili, explained to the un security council that it was not a question of debating whether east timor was a failed state, but rather how a country with four years of existence is learning to cope with the weight of responsibilities that come with independence and the challenges that the democratic system imposes. this is where we, the european union, can make all the difference. and that is the direction in which the recommendations in this resolution to the commission and the council are aimed, namely to strengthen european assistance to the consolidation of democratic institutions, respect for human rights and reconciliation in east timor. in this connection, parliament welcomed the unanimous decision of the timorese authorities to call for an international commission of inquiry into the recent incidents which have resulted in a high number of fatalities and which have left thousands of timorese displaced from their homes. the european parliament will continue to follow developments closely and is planning to send an ad hoc mission as early as next autumn. we hope that the efforts of president xanana gusmão and minister ramos horta, nobel peace prize winner, will allow the political crisis to be resolved quickly so that the mission can concentrate on european aid for the development of east timor.
we have in fact an oral amendment which is consensual between the groups and which is intended to reflect the request made yesterday by the east timorese authorities in the united nations security council for a peacekeeping mission, mandated by the united nations if necessary. the amendment is intended to clarify the request made by the timorese authorities. the paragraph would then read as follows: stresses that the process of gradual reduction of the un mission in east timor over the last four years must be reversed and calls for the urgent deployment of a un-led police force to help restore stability, and the un-mandated peacekeeping force as requested by the east timorese authorities on 13 june 2006;
the workers of opel general motors in azambuja, portugal, whom i welcome to this house, are at this moment fighting for the preservation of their jobs and the future of this company, following the threat of transfer of production from this factory to another country, which, if it were to come to fruition, would lead to the destruction of thousands of jobs and would have serious social and economic repercussions. the european parliament has adopted a number of resolutions containing a set of recommendations on the relocation of companies, and i therefore consider it of the utmost importance that parliament should be able to check with the european commission what initiatives it has taken to make community aid conditional on long-term agreements on employment and local development, as proposed by parliament, on the record of breaches of contract by companies which have relocated and which have benefited directly or indirectly from public incentives, on the refusal to grant or require the reimbursement of community funding to companies which have not fully complied with contracts concluded - as often as this has been applied - on the concrete measures which the commission has adopted to support workers and the economic recovery of regions affected by relocations, and on the drawing up of the code of conduct to prevent the relocation of companies.
