the process which will lead to the adoption of the new regulation on the european social fund dignifies this parliament. at first reading we tabled 84 amendments to the commission's original proposal. i would like to emphasize one point in particular in these amendments: the original version of the european commission set out a set of measures which were eligible for funding, but whose actions varied according to the type of region receiving funding, whether they were regions under the convergence objective or regions for regional competitiveness and employment. i have opposed this regional differentiation from the outset on the grounds that it would lead to the creation of a two-speed european social fund, which would constitute a kind of indirect discrimination against workers who benefit from the fund according to the region in which they work. both the commission and the council have finally accepted my argument. other significant changes in which the council and the commission finally accepted our proposals concerned the use of european social fund funds to finance the activities of the social partners. i have always also opposed the commission's initial proposal and suggested as an alternative a more flexible but at the same time more rigorous solution, which would allocate an appropriate amount of european social fund resources to measures to strengthen the capacity of the social partners, but which would specify that these activities should relate to training, networking measures and the strengthening of social dialogue. both the council and the commission have finally accepted our view. if the normal procedure for a second reading of this new regulation were followed, we would run the serious risk of not having the necessary legal bases in time for member states to be able to use the funds allocated to the european social fund from 1 january 2007. the austrian presidency, recognizing the importance of this, contacted me to begin negotiations to shorten the usual time limits for the legislative procedure. with the excellent cooperation of the shadow rapporteurs i was able to examine the amendments which had not been considered by the council and to put forward five points which the council had not accepted at first reading but which we found to be very important. these were: strengthening the role of social inclusion, linking member states to support actions on the priority list, commitment by member states to promote action in the area of innovation, linking member states to transnational and interregional cooperation actions and the provision of an appropriate amount for training and networking of the social partners. i am very pleased to note that the council has also agreed to all our proposals. i therefore recommend, mr president, and in keeping with the commitment made to the austrian presidency, that the common position be adopted without amendment. mr president, the great changes under way, political point of view in this process is to know how to decide on the direction of these changes, and in this respect i must confess that much of what has just been contained in this report is not only the fruit of hard work but also the result of a heated reflection on values which express, to a large extent, my view of politics as a public service. i am of the opinion that the free functioning of the market will never be able to promote the essence of the european project which i enthusiastically defend, based on the values of peace, social justice, freedom, democracy and respect for human rights. i would therefore like you to know that the new regulation on the european social fund has also been inspired by this source. finally, i would like to thank the austrian presidency for its excellent cooperation throughout this process and commissioner špidla, who is present here. i should like to express my sincere thanks to the commission services for the openness on behalf of the gue/ngl group, since the start of the negotiations on the structural funds for the period 2007-13, we have been stressing that the existence of a coherent community regional policy, properly financed, is a prerequisite for promoting an effective reduction of regional disparities at european union level, as well as real convergence between the different countries. at the level of the community budget, regional policy should be a necessary and fair redistributive instrument which, at the very least, minimises the negative consequences of the internal market for the economically less developed countries and regions. we therefore take a critical view of this general regulation on the structural funds, which translates into legislative terms the interinstitutional agreement on the amounts, objectives and rules for implementing the structural funds for 2007-13. this represents a reduction in the structural funds from 0.41% of community gdp in 2000-2006 to 0.37% of community gdp in the period 2007-2013, when the increased needs for cohesion in the face of enlargement and the increase in economic and social disparities require the opposite trend. this is also the reason why, for example, the so-called statistical effect regions, such as the algarve in portugal, are not fully compensated, which we consider unacceptable. we also find it unfavourable that cohesion policy is subordinated to the objectives of the so-called lisbon strategy, in particular by including the objective of allocating at least 60% of the funds in convergence regions and 75% in the other regions to the financing of projects in the lisbon strategy, making cohesion subordinate to competition. finally, i would like to support the speech by mr jacky henin on certain crossborder regions, such as the hainaut region in france and belgium, which have differentiated access to the structural funds, a situation which also needs to be corrected in order to ensure their harmonious development.
in writing. human trafficking has been taking on disturbing proportions, with an estimated 700,000 people a year being trafficked worldwide. this is a transnational phenomenon requiring a joint response by the international community and coordinated action by the various actors. more effective cooperation in the fight against organised crime is urgently needed, through the harmonisation of definitions of offences in the different national legal systems, mutual legal assistance, joint investigations, etc. the international community has taken a major step forward with the adoption of the united nations convention against organised crime, signed by 121 states plus the european community, which is the first global and legally binding instrument to combat criminal networks in this field. i am glad that portugal is among them and i hope that the other seven member states which have not yet ratified will do so as soon as possible. i support the conclusion of this protocol, which complements the convention by providing for strict measures to combat illicit trafficking in human beings, especially women and children, in order to protect them against slavery, sexual exploitation and illegal work, as well as measures to provide legal, material and physical and psychological rehabilitation assistance to victims.
in writing. the report voted on today endorses the council's common position of 12 june 2006 on the european social fund for 2007-13. it is noted that there are some positive aspects to this position, but insufficient, and others with which we disagree. among the positive aspects we highlight social inclusion and gender equality, but it falls short of the desired, notably in terms of promoting quality of work, and a stronger contribution to reducing income disparities and social inequalities with the aim of real economic and social cohesion. on the other hand, it is a position which continues to narrow the scope of application to policies closely related to the guidelines and recommendations in the framework of the european employment strategy and the lisbon strategy, which, as is well known, have contributed to accentuating inequalities and promoting deregulation of the labour market. however, it is up to the member states to define their priorities and the areas to be financed, so there is some room for manoeuvre that countries can apply correctly. that is why we abstained.
in writing. the adoption today of the cohesion legislative package, in particular the proposal for a regulation on the general provisions of the funds, is of the utmost importance in order to enable the member states and regions of the european union to finalise the national reference frameworks and operational programmes and to start using the european funds as from 1 january 2007. as a result of fruitful negotiations with the council, the text of the proposal for a regulation takes up almost all the main points raised by the european parliament in its interim report adopted in 2005. it regretted that the amount initially proposed by the commission had not been committed and that it would have deserved the european parliament's firm support for specific funding for the outermost regions, designed to facilitate their integration into the internal market and to compensate for their specific constraints. however, in addition to the additional funding for the ors, a maximum co-financing rate of 85% of eligible expenditure was provided for. in particular, a special, more advantageous transitional scheme for the autonomous region of madeira has been reserved for the new objective 'regional competitiveness and employment'. i therefore vote in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. the common position adopted today reflects the interinstitutional agreement which gives substance to the financial framework for 2007-13, where the structural funds are reduced by eur 28 billion compared to the commission's initial proposal and their weight is reduced from 0.41% of community gni to 0.37% compared to the previous financial framework, thus undermining effective economic and social cohesion, real convergence and the redistributive effect of the community budget. there is a major shift in the objectives of the structural funds, putting cohesion at the service of competitiveness and business interests, in line with the neoliberal lisbon agenda, by making public-private partnerships, the commercialisation of knowledge and research, and the adaptability and mobility of workers central objectives of the funds. the n+2 rule is maintained and there is no guarantee, at least on the council's part, that the cut and unused structural fund funds will continue to be used exclusively for this purpose. it should also be noted that the concessions made by the council in december 2005 in terms of the eligibility criteria for cohesion countries in exchange for the cuts in funding are now extended to the other member states. for these reasons we voted against.
in writing. the council's common position on the new cohesion fund regulation maintains, as in the previous financial framework, the conditionality of the fund transfers to compliance with the stability pact and the maastricht nominal convergence criteria. in other words, a cohesion country with a lower level of economic development is doubly penalized: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the budgetary discipline is maintained. which would work as unacceptable blackmail. we also reject the extension of the n+2 (n+3) rule to the cohesion fund, given the specificities and objectives of the fund. it should be recalled that this rule, imposed by germany in the previous financial framework 2000-2006 on the other structural funds, implies the cutting of the unused appropriations within 2 years (3 years), clearly calling into question the purpose of the expenditure of the structural funds. this new conditionality may have an even greater impact on the cohesion fund, given the financing of large projects, which leads to greater difficulties in implementation and financing.
in writing. as regards the system of own resources for 2007-13, the council decided to maintain the uk cheque (except for enlargement expenditure) and to extend similar privileges to the remaining net contributors - germany, austria, the netherlands and sweden - through reductions in the rate of vat and direct gni contributions, as well as an increase in the rate of retention of traditional own resources, in addition to cheques under the structural funds and rural development. these reductions will be paid by the other member states, including those of cohesion, which are thus doubly penalised: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject. this is an unfair and unacceptable situation, and in itself justifies our vote against it. however, there are those who insist on the creation of a new system of own resources based on european taxes, which we reject. we believe that a fair system of own resources must be based on the gni and relative prosperity of each member state, with the aim of making the effort in budgetary contribution similar for all citizens in the different eu member states. solidarity and redistribution would then be carried out on the expenditure side, taking into account the objective of real convergence and economic and social cohesion.
in writing. the current method of financing the community budget is outdated and has in recent years increasingly revealed its limitations. the last budgetary debates have become a humiliating exercise in which, almost line by line, it is argued who is or is not a net contributor. the current system with so many exceptions and derogations has become a complex and opaque system. in this context, the european union urgently needs to reform its financing system. i therefore welcome the fact that the european parliament has succeeded in imposing, in the negotiations on the latest financial perspective (2007-2013), a mid-term review for 2008/2009, a unique opportunity to thoroughly reassess the own resources system. like the rapporteur, mr lamassoure, i am in favour of a system of financing the community budget which is transparent, fair and equitable, and which provides the eu with a financial framework which is in line with its current priorities and legitimate ambitions. any future reform should be guided by the strengthening of the eu's financial independence from current transfers from the member states, as well as by the strengthening of the european character of the budget, avoiding that future debates are again the scene of clashes over the national claims of some member states.
in writing. the five largest non-financial multinationals that have remained in the top 7 since 1990 had assets of about usd 1280 billion in 2003, or more than 3% of world gdp. the largest financial multinational, citibank, alone held the same number of assets, which shows the weight the financial sector has on the real economy. when we talk about consolidating the financial services sector, we are talking about consolidating the internal market in financial services and integrating the financial markets, with a view to removing the remaining barriers to the movement of capital and encouraging mergers and acquisitions, particularly in the banking sector, so that they can compete in the globalised market. we have spoken out against this option, which is expressed in the european parliament's resolution, of which the euro is an instrument and the objectives of which are set out in the action plan for financial services. the progressive financialization of the real economy has not only led to significant job losses but has also contributed to the parasitism of the real economy, in particular by diverting productive investment, and to the fomenting of financial (and subsequently economic) crises, due in particular to the high volatility of financial markets and the speculative bubbles it creates. this casino economy has not only boosted the profits of the big brokerage firms, but above all the banking industry. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. with the implementation of air transport as the most widely used means of travelling long distances, emissions from aviation are counteracting the overall objective of reducing emissions. the measures proposed in this report, in particular the charging of fees for emissions and the trading of emission allowances, seem to me to be an appropriate way of tackling the problem of aviation influence. it is also very important that all internal flights and all flights departing from or arriving in the eu should be included in this proposal so as not to create market imbalances, and that a single european airspace should be created, which would allow savings on air routes, since more direct flights would result in lower emissions. there is, however, a detail to be taken into account which is the unique context of the outermost and isolated regions. i therefore support this report, since the amendment was adopted which provides for special attention to the outermost regions and the outlying regions, which could be greatly affected if new aviation taxes were applied uniformly throughout the european area. these regions, because of their difficult and time-consuming access, are in great need of air transport.

in writing. a european knowledge-based economy, the most dynamic and competitive in the world by 2010, were the objectives set by the lisbon european council in march 2000. however, in 2006, the european union is far from achieving these objectives. i agree with the rapporteur's proposals for europe to improve its performance in particular in knowledge creation, knowledge sharing and funding. the lack of investment in r&d and the promotion of an entrepreneurial spirit that values innovation, as well as the lack of political and financial support for lifelong learning and ict training, are to be highlighted. secondly, europe is not sharing its knowledge. there are still significant obstacles to the ability of operators in the sector to cooperate with each other within and across national borders. finally, europe is not funding knowledge. in this context, community policies should reinforce programmes such as the financial instruments of the competitiveness and innovation framework programme or the jeremie initiative (joint european resources for micro and medium-sized enterprises).
in writing. although this is an own-initiative report with no legislative impact, the considerations and concerns expressed here deserve my agreement. the idea that research and innovation will have to be central to the new economic paradigm, which europe lacks, is fundamental. but it must be noted that there is a huge and regrettable distance between the lisbon objective and reality. europe has not responded adequately to the evidence that the mastery of technology and investment in material and human resources in research and innovation are fundamental to development and growth, especially in the current context of the world economy. this observation, expressed in this resolution, together with several of the measures advocated in it - particularly with regard to the redefinition of research and innovation strategies - justifies my vote in favour. it is important, however, that we move from words to deeds. there will be no europe of results without a europe of investment.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the innovation and research sectors are essential elements for creating more and better jobs in the european union. in this context, smes play a key role as a transmission belt between universities and the business sector. the main reasons for the failure to implement the lisbon strategy are well known: poor performance by member states, fragmentation of labour markets, inefficient and inadequate use of human resources and reduced mobility of the european workforce. i regret that the member states are not providing the necessary political and financial support for the creation of a flexible workforce capable of adapting to the new realities of the labour markets, nor are they valuing their researchers. i therefore call for the abolition of the administrative and legal barriers which prevent researchers from being more mobile, the creation of better working conditions, in other words the creation of a genuine 'single market' for researchers, attractive and prestigious in order to stop the flight of european brains. i also advocate the promotion of entrepreneurship from the earliest stages of education and the strengthening of lifelong learning by actively encouraging training in new technologies for workers and the unemployed.
in writing. the report contains a number of contradictions. on the one hand, it gives prominence to negative aspects, of which the emphasis on competitiveness and competition issues is outstanding, and it insists on industrial restructuring and modernisation measures in the face of 'fierce international competition', which we already know has negative results. but it also includes proposals which we have tabled in the committee on employment and social affairs, such as the proposal to ask the commission to refuse community aid to undertakings which, after having benefited from it in one member state, transfer their production activities to another country without fully complying with the contracts concluded with the member state in question. the inclusion of the proposal to give equal priority to the working environment and the health and safety of workers with a view to ensuring the creation of more and better jobs and also to protecting the rights of workers whenever manufacturing companies are restructured and, therefore, to fully guaranteeing the availability of information for workers' representative bodies is also emphasized. that is why we abstained.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i agree that a dynamic and highly competitive industry is a necessary precondition for achieving better social standards. the study presented by the commission gives a detailed picture of the 27 sectors of manufacturing industries and wisely combines a set of sectoral actions with horizontal initiatives. i agree with the rapporteur that a coherent industrial policy at european level should be developed to meet the challenges of globalisation. although the eu is an economy based mainly on the service sector, it is also a world industrial power. it therefore makes perfect sense to develop european industrial competitiveness strategies, to promote european entrepreneurship and corporate social responsibility. i am convinced that the future of european manufacturing industries lies in increasing the added value and quality of products, as well as a skilled and flexible workforce. i also support this report because it stresses the importance of the high regional concentration of manufacturing industries. i am in favour of the regional and national authorities working closely with local economic and social actors to draw up local strategic plans for better exploitation of primary sector production and any other comparative advantage of each region.

i too am suffering at the moment from the game between portugal and france, which, contrary to mr colbert's predictions, is exactly that and not between france and england. the subject of democratic control of regulatory acts which is being discussed here today is a sign of the new times of european democracy. europe is no longer an intergovernmental area and a mere negotiating area. europe is a united and integrated area. it wants to be a democracy and it wants its own legitimacy, which is much more than the sum of the legitimacies of the states. the decision-making and implementation procedures are involved in this journey into a new era. after all, it is in these procedures that the challenge to the legitimacy and legitimacy of all political orders is concentrated. the challenge of transparency, the challenge of accountability, the challenge of effectiveness, the challenge of acceptance and trust of the recipients. parliamentary control of legislative acts, which is already well advanced in a constitution which is still pending, is more than matching the democratic power to legislate with the democratic power to control. the european institutions are assuming here that europe must have the profile of a true european democracy and that a true european democracy is not compatible with executive acts, bureaucratically alienated from public opinion and its representative institutions. this is only a small step, a small step in the unstoppable construction of a strong and democratic european centre, with decision-making chains open to a permanent scrutiny of legitimacy. it would be desirable to involve national parliaments in the appointment of national experts to the committees. in a european democracy, which has as its ideal and project the concept of comitology, the reality of networking will strengthen rather than weaken the legitimacy of political union.
madam president, mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, this is not the first time that i have spoken in this house about the need for a european policy on legal immigration - for humanitarian and economic reasons - and the urgent need for measures to strengthen the fight against illegal immigration and human trafficking. the two proposals before us are important and useful. i would like to refer first to that of mr lambrinidis and say to commissioner frattini that the commission's proposal is very positive and quite balanced, but i fear that the rapporteur has gone a little too far on some points, particularly from the point of view of political rights. the integration of immigrants must be pursued, but we must not forget that it is a two-way street: the host countries have to make an effort to integrate them, but immigrants have to do their part in this integration effort. i agree with mr lambrinidis that it is regrettable that the consultation procedure and the unanimity requirement are still maintained throughout the whole area of legal immigration and i agree with the recommendation to use the bridge clause provided for in the treaty in order to give the european parliament co-decision powers. i would also like to stress the importance of mr gaubert's report, which seeks to establish a web-based information system on these matters. although the implementation of integration initiatives is done at the local level, it is global in its implications. difficulties in one member state in defining and implementing its integration policies have social and economic consequences in other member states. it is therefore in the union's interest that member states implement effective integration strategies, the results of which serve the common interests. it can and should be the responsibility of the union to monitor and compare the results of integration efforts in order to contribute to the rapid adoption of best practices.

in writing. the last decade has seen a dramatic increase in terrorist acts worldwide, which has made the fight against this scourge one of the main political priorities at european and world level. this proposal is part of a series of measures being taken by the union to reduce access to financial and other economic resources for terrorists. it intends to transpose into community law the special recommendation 7 on electronic transfers of the financial action task force. it aims to facilitate the work of authorities responsible for combating money laundering and terrorism by laying down rules on the obligation to provide information on the payer at the time of the transfer of funds. it will be a useful and effective step towards the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorists or other criminals and the tracing of their assets. i agree with the derogations provided for, which are intended to take account of the specificities of the payment systems of the different member states. i support the position expressed by mr brejc that it is unthinkable to accept a sunset clause, whereby this regulation should expire within five years if it does not prove its usefulness, and i support the compromise reached between him and the rapporteur.
in writing. the amendment to the financial regulation would aim to simplify and make more transparent its rules - as regards external contracts and grants - which, due to their lack of clarity and poor structuring, are difficult for potential users to understand. moreover, this bureaucratic set of rules, which is only the domain of a few within the european commission's dgs, entails high costs - due to the processing of applications - for suppliers and organisations applying for these grants, which excludes many micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, as well as smaller associations, institutes and ngos. the commission also has a discretion in this process, with only a few companies and associations - always the same ones - mastering these 'mechanisms'. this will ultimately serve to make clear political choices about who to support and who not to support. however, as the court of auditors itself has stated, the revision presented is not sufficient to reduce the burden and simplify the procedures for both the commission and potential users. the european parliament's proposals improve this situation, but they still fall short of the urgently needed overall revision of the financial regulation in these areas.
in writing. we voted against this resolution for several reasons:- the failure to include any mention of solidarity with the workers of opel/gm, in particular the more than 1700 workers (and their families) at the opel azambuja plant in portugal, whose jobs are threatened by gm management, regardless of the economic, social and regional consequences that would follow. it was the position imposed by the right wing, with the consent of the european socialist party, which signed this joint resolution; - the defence of the right of companies to take management decisions designed to ensure their economic growth, regardless of the social consequences that would follow; - the disregard for the economic and social consequences of restructuring, which is generally carried out in a logic of merely reducing costs and maximising profits, without regard to factors of economic viability or productivity, often without respecting contractual obligations and taking advantage, in a mercenary way, of local, national and community public aid, leaving behind a trail of unemployment and jeopardising local economies. last year alone, restructuring resulted in more than half a million unemployed in the european union;- the resolution falls far short of the results achieved in the resolutions of march this year on the effects of relocations and restructuring on employment and regional development.
in writing. it is true that the entrepreneurial spirit and the role of enterprises are indispensable for economic growth and development, and it is also true that the substantial economic changes we are going through require the restructuring of many enterprises. of course, corporate social responsibility. but also the duty to comply with agreements and to respect contracts, particularly where there have been grants and subsidies awarded in the context of a given action. the considerations, concerns and proposals in this resolution deserve my agreement. i believe, however, that the wise establishment of the european globalisation adjustment fund should alert us in good time to the scale of the problem at hand and require us to look for profound solutions. the process of restructuring the european business fabric, particularly the industrial one, is under way and will have positive consequences, which we hope, but also negative effects in the social field, especially at first. europe, the various governments and the community institutions have the duty to prepare for this very near future today. in addition to this fund, other solutions need to be discussed and investments made in other mechanisms.
in writing. the report contains positive elements that confirm what has long been known and denounced: that the cia, or other us agencies, were 'directly responsible for the abduction, removal, kidnapping and illegal detention' of citizens - euphemistically referred to as 'extraordinary rendition' - as well as for the transfer of citizens to third countries for interrogation and torture, in brutal violation of international law and human rights. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu's citizens are protected from the threat of terrorism. the report should help to demystify the real meaning of the so-called 'preventive war' and 'war on terrorism' with which the us and its allies seek to cover up their aggression against peoples and the sovereignty of states, in violation of international law and human rights. the report should also help to establish the truth and accountability, in particular to clarify the content of the agreements concluded within nato and between the eu and the us in this context, and to enable each national parliament to carry out its own inquiries.
in writing. what is at stake in this report cannot be taken lightly. both human rights and the fight against terrorism, as well as relations with our main ally, deserve special attention and consideration. what emerges from this interim report is that there is a set of unresolved doubts and suspicions, along with contradictory statements from various entities. it is therefore understandable that the commission's work should continue, but it is not reasonable to draw conclusions which are not proved. more seriously, the refusal of several amendments which were intended to include in the report what is relevant contradicts some of the accusations and insinuations, reveals a desire to antagonize an allied country which is superior to the desire to establish the truth. i will not contribute to that understanding of the role of the european parliament or of the eu's external relations. i believe it is possible that both european countries and our allies make mistakes and commit acts contrary to the law, which should be known and punished, but i am not prepared to accuse without investigating or condemn without proof.
in writing. although it includes aspects with which we disagree, we believe that this resolution should help to highlight the real nature of the so-called 'fight against terrorism' and the security drift which also characterizes it. through the terrorist finance surveillance program, the u.s. has, through a secret agreement, accessed all financial data stored by swift (society for worldwide interbank financial telecommunications), which is a cooperative of over 8000 banks and institutions in 200 countries, including the european central bank. the us thus had access to millions of information on the transfers and banking transactions of citizens and businesses worldwide. access to this information was carried out in breach of legal procedures relating to data protection and without any legal basis, violating rights, freedoms and guarantees, as well as the sovereign competence of states to protect their citizens. the truth must be clarified and responsibility for this unacceptable situation must be established, particularly as regards the role and the action of the european central bank. this is not an isolated case. this is just the tip of the iceberg of the real meaning of the security drift which is putting the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens in question.
in writing. i congratulate my colleague, mr stavros lambrinidis, on his excellent report on the strategies and means of integrating immigrants in the european union, which i support. i would stress in this context the need to ensure the effective application of the community directives on the integration of immigrants. the european union needs to monitor the transposition of the integration-related directives and the effectiveness of administrative practices that apply the relevant legislation to the daily lives of immigrants.
in writing. while i share the rapporteur's concerns, i cannot agree with all the proposals he has put forward to solve one of the central problems raised by immigration: integration. first of all, and to cite just a few examples, the confusion between immigration from candidate countries (particularly in the past) and from other countries is an error of analysis which is revealed in the conclusions; there is an error in the assumptions that the more than 40 million third-country nationals make immigrants the '26th (and fifth largest) eu member state'; and finally, the idea - which was taken up by the gue group in particular - that the states which grant citizenship to immigrants should be imposed, without recalling that this matter has different regulations and various reasons for being, is to be simplistic with what is not simple. there is currently a problem of integration of some immigrant communities into the european union, and no european model seems to be working fully and effectively. integration is a two-way process. it must be facilitated by the country of arrival (by the public authorities and citizens) and desired and practiced by immigrants. failure to recognize this reality is to give space to extremist movements on both sides.
in writing. although the report contains aspects which we regard as positive, and which we therefore support, it does not criticise the immigration policy pursued at european union level or denounce the root causes of the migration of millions of men and women throughout the world. the report omits criticism of the eu's immigration policy, which has as its primary objective the exploitation of cheap and unrighteous labour, while implementing repressive measures, seeking to criminalize immigrants, men and women, who simply aspire to the right to live - access to food, health, water, housing, education or culture - the right to a job and an income. the report also ignores the root causes of migration, which are rooted in deep inequalities, which are also becoming more pronounced. inequalities that are generated by neoliberal and militarist policies, which are, in fact, at the heart of capitalist globalization. policies of liberalization and privatization which aim to promote the concentration of wealth and property in the large economic and financial groups, seeking to use the states to pursue their interests, even if this does not require the use of interference and war to impose their dictates.
in writing. this report, even if it is originally drafted with the best of intentions, does not go to the bottom of the problem. it is of course essential to ensure a fair income for the producer - covering production costs and ensuring a sustainable life for him - as well as his involvement in the marketing process, among many other positive points which are written in this report. however, it should not be hidden that the general lines which characterize so-called fair trade are in flagrant contradiction with the policies of liberalization of world trade, promoted, in particular, at the level of the wto (not to mention the bilateral free trade agreements, so encouraged by the us and the eu), which seek to shape the production systems of the economically less developed countries to the needs of expansion of the large economic and financial groups of the countries of the "north". what is needed is a policy which respects the right of peoples to use natural resources and to develop the productive and economic potential of their countries in order to improve their living conditions; which encourages mutually beneficial cooperation and guarantees food sovereignty; which ensures control and public ownership of natural resources and strategic sectors of the economy.

in portugal, i will also give the portuguese example, anyone who buys a new car pays an extraordinarily high registration tax to the state. sometimes it comes to almost half the final cost of the car and on top of that tax you still pay vat and then over the years you pay a traffic tax that is minimal. i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this. but that is how it has been and will continue to be because the state, the portuguese state in this case, likes to charge in advance, like everyone else, by the way. if i disclose these facts, as other colleagues have done, it is because they have to do with what we are discussing here. this proposal for a directive, which is precisely intended to abolish the so-called registration tax in the countries of the european union and replace it with an annual traffic tax, the amount of which will take account of carbon dioxide emissions, is fairer, more logical and more environmentally and economically friendly. this is the right system, because it makes the price of vehicles more affordable, especially for the middle and lower classes, and allows the renewal of the car fleet, both from the environmental and road safety points of view. contrary to what some may think, raising the price of cars through taxation is not always environmentally friendly. in my country, for example, because new, more environmentally efficient cars are expensive, people buy used cars from other countries that are less safe and more polluting. on the contrary, with a road tax defined as the proposal for a directive advocates, the tax burden on motor vehicles would not only be compulsory to follow the useful life of vehicles, but would also prevent citizens who settle in more than one country of the union from having to pay a double tax, and would contribute to more transparent rules of the internal market by allowing a true comparison of vehicle prices in the various member states. in conclusion, ladies and gentlemen, i would say that increasing the cost of cars does not reduce the number of vehicles on the road, it only makes the quality of the cars we drive worse. a fair and balanced road tax is always better than an exaggerated tuition tax, for the environment, for the economy and for the citizens. i only hope that the governments of the member states will see it that way in due course.

the following is the commission statement on forest fires and floods.
the tragedy of forest fires, which year after year is affecting the countries of southern europe, particularly portugal and spain, cannot continue. it is time to replace lamentation with concrete measures to prevent the summer from turning into a hell of destruction of forests and protected landscapes, of the lives and property of thousands of people who courageously persist in living in rural areas. the situation in portugal in august was particularly serious, with many tens of thousands of hectares of forest burned, several people killed and the destruction of an important environmental heritage, notably in the peneda-gerês national park and the serras d'aire and candeeiros natural park, as well as enormous material damage. in early september the scourge of fires continues. so, in addition to solidarity with the affected populations, the need for urgent support for herders and farmers who have lost their pastures for livestock, as in the serra de soajo, and the immediate removal of burnt wood as fair payment to farmers, small forest owners and shared plots, it is essential to insist on prevention by strengthening financial, technical and human resources, including support for those involved in firefighting operations and reforestation of burnt areas, in particular protected areas, for which extraordinary support should be granted to portugal from the european solidarity fund to all the most affected areas and populations. the adoption of effective public policies to strengthen the prevention of reforestation and forestry management must not be delayed any longer, and the cap must be changed so that family farming is supported in such a way as to guarantee farmers a decent living, in particular through guaranteed production prices, and that the abandonment of rural areas, which will be aggravated by the withdrawal of production aid, does not continue.
at the moment i am speaking to you, the fire in the far north of portugal has not yet been completely extinguished, and it has struck my country's largest natural park for the second time this year, while eight other large fires are still burning in other regions. the drama of fires continues to affect several member states this year, with spain seemingly the hardest hit at the moment, with countless human tragedies, including loss of life and economic and environmental damage that is impossible to account for. i therefore express my solidarity and my sorrow to all colleagues in all the affected states, and in particular to my spanish colleagues, remembering those who have lost their lives in this hell that is currently afflicting us and paying tribute to all those, professional and non-professional, who have made their effort to the limits of human resistance to minimize the effects of the fires. we all know that the problem of forest fires and other disasters cannot be solved overnight, especially when they are often due to complex combinations of causes, from climate to human, from negligence to crime, but we also know that their scale and their effects can be reduced if we give them the political priority they deserve. as you will recall, parliament has recently devoted a great deal of attention, resources and will to better understanding these phenomena, identifying the causes and proposing short, medium and long-term solutions to reverse this absolutely unacceptable situation. several committees heard researchers and technicians, contacted public authorities and the public and made proposals and recommendations to the commission and the council, which were widely welcomed by the political groups in this parliament last may. i myself was rapporteur for the committee on agriculture, which had the opportunity to formulate some three dozen proposals for the adoption of a european strategy which, by creating new measures and their coherent articulation with various existing policy and financial instruments, could lead to the intended objectives of reducing to a minimum the consequences of natural disasters. it would be demagogic to demand that all of them have been implemented since may, but it is urgent - and it is becoming increasingly urgent - that we move from reports to concrete action. the political debate is over and the necessary political solutions are known and agreed. the tragedy of this summer has only served as a dramatic reminder that we must act even more quickly so that next year we do not simply express mutual wishes of solidarity in the wake of a new tragedy.
every year fires consume a significant part of europe's forests. this year, unfortunately, was no exception. with climate change and global warming, the future doesn't look any better. natural disasters cannot be avoided, but they must be prevented at an early stage by complying with the kyoto protocol and by defining an appropriate forestry policy. in portugal, 420,000 hectares were burned in 2003 and 320,000 in 2005. this year, by the end of august, 59,000 hectares had burned, which is a lot, even because there were protected areas burned and victims to mourn. but it is also fair to acknowledge that a great deal of effort and investment has been made in prevention and immediate action, a permanent surveillance system has been set up involving the security forces, the armed forces and many young people, firefighting helicopter brigades have been set up in the first minutes after the ignition, and there have been days when more than 500 fires have been identified. the commission has also made a major investment in training firefighters and in the creation of professional firefighting units, whose dedication and efforts i would like to commend. in portugal and other countries great efforts have been made, but more needs to be done and the european commission must also adopt the proposals which have been put forward by the european parliament.
on behalf of the pse group. other i participated in the european parliament's election observation mission to the democratic republic of congo. i visited more than forty polling stations in different districts of kinshasa and had the privilege of observing the counting of votes and the work of one of these polling stations in dima, just one of the more than 250,000 spread throughout the country. i have admired the patient dedication of the congolese men and women, members of the polling stations and voters. they all told me, with poignant seriousness, that their commitment and vigilance in carrying out the electoral tasks would depend on the authenticity of the people's choice, of the more than 25 million voters who were registered in a logistical operation of epic proportions, and that the european union. the elections should thus be a source of pride for the congolese people, but also for europe, which financed 80% of the presidential and legislative elections, with the european commission contributing €165 million. the european union's involvement in the democratic republic of the congo since the end of the terrible war that devastated the country has been the best example of the application of the european security doctrine on the ground: humanitarian and development aid, technical support for the demobilization and disarmament of militias, support for the political process: the inability to forge a unified national army. according to the international crisis group, only 50% of the work on integrating the armed forces has been done. it is not only azarias ruberwa and jean-pierre bemba who still maintain private armies. president kabila himself has resisted subjecting his presidential guard to the brassage process and it was his forces that sparked the armed above all on congolese men and women, such as the independent candidate for parliament, eve bazaiba masudi, a member of the ngo kafko, which is made up of women who are courageously fighting for peace, democracy and human rights, in close coordination with manuc. eve bazaiba masudi and other women representatives of congolese civil society are trying to mediate and hold warlords to account. they deserve the support of the european union and i trust that the delegation of the european commission and the committee headed by general morillon, whom i commend for the excellent work they have done so far, will be able to support these bearers of peace and dialogue.

in writing. although respect for the official languages of each member state is enshrined in the treaties, attempts are increasing to restrict the number of working languages at eu level, always favouring the languages of the most populous countries. the recent example is the 'european language proficiency indicator' which includes only english, french, german, spanish and italian. although it considers 'multilingualism' to be a 'key component' of the eu, this report is imbued with a budgetary constraint which, through administrative arguments, could call into question this right enshrined in the treaties. we therefore reiterate our firm rejection of any attempt to limit the use of any official (and working) language in the eu on the grounds that interpretation costs are high. we also criticise the criteria for determining the languages used during eu-acp parliamentary assemblies, which make the use of portuguese unfeasible in a discriminatory way. we are also opposed to the reduction in the number of interpreters in parliament, the commission and the european council, the creation of a single interpreting service and the attack on the rights of these professionals in terms of contractual obligations, working hours and working conditions, all under the pretext of budget cuts.
in writing. this report provides an overview of the work of the european maritime safety agency, based in lisbon, in developing actions to improve maritime safety and prevent pollution caused by ships in the waters of the various eu countries. this action is defined as supplementary to and in support of the action taken by the various coastal countries in combating and preventing marine pollution, in particular by contributing to improving its early detection, including the identification of those responsible. the prevention and combating of marine pollution will be all the more effective if the various coastal countries are better equipped with the means - particularly public ones - to allow appropriate, rapid and effective action. apart from other important aspects which should be assessed, this report proposes to extend the scope of the regulation to include not only situations of marine pollution caused by hydrocarbons but also all types of pollution caused by ships, including harmful liquid substances, which we consider to be positive. the report also points to what it calls the 'minimum funding' of the agency, which, if not respected, would jeopardise - we add, even more so - the achievement of the objectives for which it was set up.
in writing. the proposal now voted on is particularly important in view of the recent ecological disasters caused by spills from ships. the measures proposed in the report seem to me to be an appropriate way of improving the functioning of the european maritime safety agency by introducing a new long-term vision enabled by the budget set for a seven-year period (2007-2013) and providing for the hiring of vessels immediately available for the fight against spills. the creation of a new imaging centre, proposed by the european parliament, is also very important in order to support actions to identify illegal spills and discharges, allowing for faster and more efficient intervention. this proposal is of particular importance for portugal, which has a large exclusive economic zone, crossed by hundreds of ships every day, and a history of accidental spills and ecological disasters.
in writing. i voted in favour of the lissy gröner report on the fight against violence (daphne) (2007/2013), as it is necessary to continue this successful project in the fight against violence which continues to affect children, young people and women in europe and the world, and in the defence of the fundamental rights guaranteed by the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. the prevention and combating of violence against children, young people and women, and the protection of victims and groups at risk (daphne iii) deserve a separate programme. it is necessary to inform and raise awareness among citizens about the problem of violence by providing this programme with the necessary mechanisms, in close cooperation with the various ngos which have a major role in society in this area, in particular through the promotion of the european year against violence against women in 2007.
in writing. we welcome the adoption of our amendment to strengthen the daphne programme. with the approval of this proposal by our group, which i support, the budget for the implementation of this instrument will be increased to eur 125 million for the period 2007-2013, instead of the eur 116.85 million provided for in the gröner report, which the rapporteur proposed to be increased to eur 120 million, although she also voted in favour of our proposal, which allowed it to be adopted. the conditions are thus better for daphne iii to contribute to the prevention and combating of violence against children, young people and women and to the protection of victims. zero tolerance for violence must involve increased political commitment, continued effort and persistent intervention in all member states.
in writing. the commission's strategy to harmonise motor vehicle taxes dates from 2002. the main idea is to abolish the car registration tax the ia in portugal - and to gradually replace it with an increase in the traffic tax the stamp duty, with a differentiation of value based on co2 emissions. the aim is to penalise the use of cars and to promote free movement within the internal market by promoting the sale and replacement of used cars. we agree on the need to create special measures for citizens who move between member states of the european union, but we disagree on the proposed tax harmonization. first, the federal question. this harmonization calls into question the fiscal sovereignty of the member states and their transport policy options. on the other hand, the co2 differentiation does not take account of the engine capacity and the value of the car, which, together with the penalty for driving, has a regressive and penalising effect on commercial cars. finally, this strategy penalizes the value of used cars and increased competition could have economic and social consequences. we cannot therefore accept the objectives of this directive.
the european union as we know it today was born on the basis of an ideal, the main aim of which was to achieve and preserve peace. in half a century europe has become a world reference for peace, democracy, freedom, solidarity, prosperity and development. peace, the first great objective of european integration, has been largely achieved to the extent that today, because we have lived in peace for more than six decades, we have become so accustomed to living in peace that we do not realise the real value of this great achievement. we are talking about a peace based on freedom, democracy, respect for human rights and the rule of law, and when we compare the european social model with other situations, we cannot ignore, for example, the great deception of the communist totalitarian experiments that for decades deprived many europeans of the right to freedom, which today has been happily regained for a large number of them. the brutal reality of islamic fundamentalism today is another example of the clear departure from the essential values on which the european social model is based. this report deals mainly with values. the way in which these values are applied varies from country to country, and that is why we have said that the european social model, being a unity based on values, is different in its ways of application. globalisation, technological development and demographic change are the main factors that have put the social protection systems of the different european states in difficulty, although to a different degree from one state to another. the european social model will survive if we act in time or it will die if we do not. we know that a scenario of weak economic growth makes any structural reforms unworkable from the outset. that is why we have placed great emphasis in the report on the implementation by the member states of the lisbon strategy and the need to complete the internal market. greater labour market flexibility, lifelong learning, longer working life, work-life balance, changing sources of funding, combating poverty and social exclusion are all considered as priorities in the reforms to be undertaken. in the area of competitiveness, we recommend that a great deal of attention be paid to small and mediumsized enterprises and innovation. the general outlines of the reforms which need to be carried out and which are outlined in the report we are presenting reflect a reformist thinking which is firmly rooted in the values which were at the basis of the creation of the european social model, values which, as framing elements of all political action, are today more precise than ever. it is therefore important for us that this parliament should state that the reforms which need to be carried out in the various social protection systems must in no way affect the essential values on which the european social model is based. the european parliament's decision on the content of this report goes beyond the union itself because it is a political statement in defence of values which, while important for europe, are also important for the world. in this connection, i would simply like to quote the international labour organisation, which explicitly referred to the european social model as a possible source of inspiration for the new emerging powers. i would like to dedicate a final word to my colleague and co-rapporteur, mr proinsias de rossa, for the great cooperation with which he distinguished me and which has enabled me to develop a work which has been both stimulating and enjoyable to me.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, what we are discussing here today is of the utmost importance given the seriousness of what is at stake, the so-called 'european social model', that is to say, the set of economic, social and labour rights which have been the conquest of workers and the population for decades and which the european commission and this report do not take into account. on the contrary, i did. underlying this is the idea that social security systems undermine economic performance and are not sustainable in the face of the demographic challenges of globalisation and global competition, insisting on deep structural reforms that in practice involve the dismantling of public social security systems, neglecting what has been the main instrument in defending social inclusion, combating poverty, inequalities in income distribution and sharing, job insecurity and unemployment, as well as promoting the dignity of those who work. the epp and pse rapporteurs therefore intend to continue the policy of making concessions to the big european employers, to the interests of economic and financial groups, opening up new business areas and placing a large amount of money in pension systems in the interests of private profitability, following the increasingly neoliberal path of the so-called 'lisbon strategy' and the 'stability pact'. but that is not what the more than 72 million people living in poverty and the more than 18 million unemployed expect. therefore, a change in these policies is necessary. that is what we are aiming at with the proposals we have put forward, which we hope will be adopted.
it must be recognized that the european social model was a key instrument in the reconstruction of democratic europe in the post-war period and that its success has benefited many millions of people. but it must also be recognised that, having been established in a context of overpopulation and relative commercial and industrial stagnation, it lacks adjustment to a time of sharp population decline, a highly competitive global economy and constant demand for adaptability of resources. this need for reform is all the more necessary as relatively new factors of social unrest such as the unsustainability of pension schemes, longterm unemployment, youth unemployment and skilled unemployment are increasing. the main challenge in this area is to reduce the role of the state and redefine its role, to open up the economy more and to encourage private initiative, creativity, competitiveness and investment. despite the need to be flexible and to consider the reduction for the future of some rights which previous generations took for granted, i also think it is essential to be cautious and to defend the situations of the most fragile and vulnerable.

in writing. this report on the conclusion of the partnership agreement between the union of the comoros and the european community deserves my vote in favour. this agreement is part of the new partnership approach that the eu intends to implement in the external dimension of its common fisheries policy, thus providing for the development and improvement of fishing conditions in the union of the comoros, which should use part of the eu budget to secure new infrastructure and better technologies capable of ensuring a sustainable management of its fisheries resources. the eu, for its part, guarantees fishing opportunities in one more third country that ensure the maintenance and operability of its long-distance fishing fleet. the european parliament is only now being asked to give its opinion on the legislative proposal for this agreement, the protocol to which it is attached having already been approved by the same parliament in october 2005 under a separate procedure.
in writing. in the light of the council conclusions of july 2004 on the new approach to international fisheries agreements, it is necessary to recover formulas that have become obsolete, such as the inexplicable disappearance of the regime of joint ventures that had been so successful in developing the fisheries economies of several countries. it is therefore essential to adapt the current agreements to the philosophy adopted and embodied in the 2004 fisheries council conclusions. greater involvement of the authorities of third countries in procedures for monitoring their resources with increased environmental concerns is one of the points i consider to be fundamental to the success of these new agreements. i therefore believe that this report should be voted in favour of in order to ensure that the principles enshrined in the cfp are respected.
in writing. we regret that once again those who talk so much about a decent european social model have in fact adopted a report which in reality paves the way for and covers the dismantling, already under way in several member states, of high social standards and of the right of workers and the population to a public, universal and high-quality social security system, as well as universal access to high-quality public services, particularly in the fields of health, education and housing. we regret the rejection of our amendments, particularly those expressing our deep conviction that a state with a sound social protection system, based on high environmental, social and labour standards, with progressive taxation and redistribution of income and wealth generated is not detrimental to good economic performance. we also find it unfortunate that the proposal in which we advocated a macroeconomic framework which supports sustainable development, with stronger and environmentally compatible domestic demand and full employment, in conditions which ensure economic and social cohesion, has been rejected. that is why we voted against the report.

in writing. i fully support the objectives set by the commission, in particular the action plan in priority areas such as conservation policy and the control of fishing activities. points such as the frontloading (prior and timely consultation) of institutions directly or indirectly involved in fisheries resource assessments, namely consultation of the regional advisory councils and the advisory committee on fisheries and aquaculture; the use of more frequent impact assessments of potential measures to be implemented and the revision of the legal structure of existing provisions in order to better clarify the legislative texts, enhance their readability, coherence and comprehensibility by removing obsolete provisions are some of the key points of this proposal which i consider to be fundamental to adapting the cfp to the current reality of fisheries in the eu. i would also like to reiterate the need for the commission to extend its process of improving procedures to the partnership agreements, in particular the process of monitoring, monitoring and enforcing them. this proposal deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. improvement and simplification of legislation is necessary in view of the multiplicity and legibility of community legislation on the common fisheries policy. simplification of procedures, precise wording that is understandable to all parties involved, sufficient time between the adoption and implementation of legislation and the assessment of its economic, social and environmental impacts are issues that need to be clearly defined in the interests of transparency and fairness in the implementation of legislation. however, this procedure cannot be used as a pretext for attempting to subvert what is regulated, and it must be ensured that not only national parliaments and the european parliament but also the sector and its representative organisations, in particular the workers, are monitored. acceptance of the simplification process does not imply agreement on the content of the common fisheries policy, to which we have deep objections. for example, the rapporteur's defence of a community inspection system, which we oppose, because we consider that this is a competence of the member states, arising from the sovereignty over their exclusive economic zone. the rapporteur's caution in extending the principle that member states may adopt conservation and resource management measures in their waters beyond 12 nautical miles is also not understood.
in writing. the importance of simplifying the rules governing the common fisheries policy is undeniable and the measures set out in this proposal, which aim to deal with the lack of clarity of the existing texts by concentrating efforts on a simpler wording, allowing the parties concerned to come closer together and to identify the fisheries sector more closely with the legislation, are to be welcomed. despite the numerous appeals made, the difficulties experienced by fishermen in knowing and understanding the common fisheries policy are still evident. it must be made not only perceptible but also feasible. i therefore think it is useful to gradually adapt to new technologies on board fishing vessels and to commit community aid to specific development and training in this area. these measures could create benefits for the fishing community and consumers. i also think that the procedures for managing fishing licences outside community waters need to be clarified.

i would also like to thank the rapporteur for her work. a first question raised by this report is whether there is really a need for eco-labelling of fishery products and whether it can actually contribute to adding value to the product and to the consumer. the rapporteur stresses that, according to regulation (ec) no 2371/2002, all fishing activities in the european union must by definition be sustainable insofar as they must comply with community standards, and therefore all fish caught on the basis of these standards will naturally be eco-labelled. that said, any ecological labelling of fish caught based on any other criteria going beyond what is provided for in the existing legislation in the catch sector could lead to a discriminatory situation between producers, and we believe that ecological labelling would make sense, as it does for agriculture, in the case of aquaculture and processed products, where environmental and food safety problems can be put in the right place, as well as in relation to imported products in general, which would have to comply with the general community regulation on fishery products. another question is whether such a label at community level would have advantages over the diversity of labels on the market, as has already been pointed out, since they are confusing to consumers and are often the result of a mere marketing strategy of companies without any public certification. in this respect, we believe that a community-wide label would be complex, bureaucratic and too restrictive for fisheries organisations and member states. the need is to create a public certification framework with direct involvement of the member states' authorities. this is the most appropriate way of defining rules where there is a legislative vacuum in this area. as regards the added value that may result from this type of labelling, we feel that it is necessary to ensure that it is distributed throughout the value chain in such a way as to benefit the efforts and investments of producers without penalising consumers.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i would first of all like to congratulate our colleague, mrs carmen fraga estévez, on her excellent report and say that the growing interest in safe, quality food products and the need to preserve marine ecosystems, as well as the recent proliferation of products with an eco-label, require an urgent community approach to the so-called eco-labelling. the fact that a number of high-quality eco-labelling programmes are emerging worldwide, and i will give an example of one in my country, the popa, which certifies tuna caught in the autonomous region of the azores, means that not all eco-labelling schemes are primarily aimed at protecting the biological heritage of our oceans, and that there are therefore diffuse economic interests which sometimes hide behind this type of labelling, which is why, in order to protect the environment and consumers, we must be extremely careful and assume our responsibilities as policy-makers. of the various proposals put forward by the commission in this communication, i believe that the one which could serve the interests concerned is the one concerning the establishment of minimum requirements for optional eco-labelling programmes. in this way, and on the basis of these minimum requirements, which have been established in advance, eco-labelling programmes can be developed freely in a flexible and optional way through public or private initiatives, but within a generic regulatory framework. the european union, as a public body, should define these minimum requirements, because only then will it be possible to defend the general interest and the prerogatives enshrined in the common fisheries policy. finally, i would like to emphasize that this is a task which we must carry out both within the union and in our trade relations with the rest of the world, so that transparency, credibility and fairness are guaranteed, especially since eco-labelling will increasingly be a way of differentiating products, which will also have an impact on competitiveness.

in writing. the report adopted today in the european parliament has positive aspects which we support, such as the more widespread use of environmentally friendly transport, the encouragement of the use of public transport, the reduction of building density, more green space in urban areas, the rehabilitation of degraded buildings and in particular of historic centres, and a higher environmental performance of buildings in terms of insulation and the use of renewable energy. it is also important, as the report states, to promote the exchange of best practice at community level on sustainable urban management strategy and plans and to increase citizen participation in public debates during their development. however, all this also presupposes greater community support in terms of the means of financing, which unfortunately does not happen. on the contrary, the european union is introducing more obligations and taxes without creating the appropriate financial means, which may exacerbate the asymmetries between the richer regions and countries and other deprived areas.
in writing. accessibility is central to sustainable development. transport is thus at the heart of any discussion of urban policy. as there are many ideas that try to solve the environmental and congestion problems that our cities suffer from, i think it is the consequences for public health and quality of life, in terms of socioeconomic dynamism, that we should be concerned about. the idea of sustainable urban transport plans is undoubtedly important, but we cannot forget the need to use this instrument in a flexible way and adapted to the specificities of each city. the use of environmentally friendly modes of transport and technologies is also a key factor in achieving a cleaner urban environment. but its dissemination will only be effective through the exchange of experience and good practice between local and national authorities. it seems clear to me that in order to promote an integrated approach to urban policy it is of the utmost importance to promote public-private partnerships and to manage effectively the existing community instruments in support of urban policies. only by taking measures appropriate to the specific situations of each member state can we ensure the sustainable future of our cities and the harmonious growth of our societies.
in writing. it is true that the recognition of qualifications between the different member states of the european union is important for people who want to move to other countries, so the existence of a european qualifications framework can bring advantages. it is also good that the idea of imposing criteria on the branch, duration and location of studies and training courses, as is done in the report, is rejected. we also welcome the fact that it is stated that the organisation and validation of lifelong learning is a matter for the member states and that the eqf can hardly intervene in this matter. but it is essential to pay close attention to the way in which this european qualifications framework is being constructed, to the framework from which it is being built and to the objectives which are being pursued. the report is full of contradictions in this field. the attempts to frame this whole construction within the framework of the so-called bologna process and the lisbon strategy, which, as we know, is primarily intended to protect the interests of economic and financial groups, are examples of this. that is why we abstained.
in writing. i support this report because i am convinced that the creation of the european qualifications framework (eqf) will contribute to greater employability and geographical mobility of the labour force in the european union. i support this european approach because it addresses the new challenges of the knowledge society and aims to respond to the new demands of the european labour market, since the underlying philosophy of the eqf is precisely based on promoting the competitiveness of the european economy and social cohesion, in line with the objectives of the lisbon strategy. i cannot but support initiatives which help to give greater prominence to the ability of citizens to get work by encouraging professional mobility through the recognition, comparability and transferability of professional qualifications within the community. i regret, however, that this initiative is not sufficiently linked to the realities of the labour market and that it obscures the importance of vocational training by focusing predominantly on academic training.
i am able to inform you that commissioner rehn had other commitments and could not be present at this meeting. i give the floor to commissioner louis michel again.
