we agree that the euro must be properly protected by joint, uniform and effective measures, which must be achieved through close cooperation at both european and international level. that is why we applaud the creation of the pericles programme. we welcome the detailed report to this parliament on the implementation and results of this programme and we stress that the results are frankly positive. in the last half of 2003, the number of counterfeit euro banknotes in circulation stabilised at a level below both the levels recorded before the introduction of the euro and the counterfeiting levels of the us dollar. while the number of counterfeit euro coins continues to increase, it remains low in comparison with the counterfeiting of old coins. we can therefore say that there is a minimum rate of counterfeiting, to which the high degree of cooperation of the competent services contributes greatly. the commission has also been involved in the dismantling and confiscation of large volumes of counterfeit banknotes and coins before they were put into circulation. the programme thus largely achieved its objectives and identified the geographical areas which have the most significant impact on the production of counterfeit notes, both at community and international level. it has also made it possible to achieve considerable structural improvements, such as the creation in several countries of central bodies responsible for combating counterfeiting of the euro. i therefore support the excellent proposal by the rapporteur, mr agustín díaz de mera, to approve the extension of the programme until the end of 2013 in order to align its duration with the financial perspective and, and i would like to stress its importance, to extend its application to the non-participating member states.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal for a decision on the strategic guidelines for cohesion, which we have been asked to give our assent to and which will serve as the basis for the elaboration of the national strategic reference frameworks, seems to me to be an excellent process of intentions for the council and we should thank it for the enormous effort of our colleague, mrs constanze krehl. these strategic guidelines clearly state that europe needs to focus on meeting the objectives set out in the lisbon strategy, which are of course very dear to me, both in terms of jobs and growth, and in terms of encouraging innovation and a knowledge-based economy. in seeking to respond to the challenges of the european union on a global scale and in emphasising the new dimension and scale we have today, particular care must be taken to ensure that everyone is involved, whether they are the social partners, ngos, municipalities or regions. today we are a huge giant with great ambitions and we cannot afford to neglect this or that part of the territory so that together we can achieve the objectives we set ourselves. we have to prove that the typical multi-level model of our society is sufficiently robust. full employment, a skilled workforce, lifelong learning or increased productivity are essential factors if the union's economic, social and territorial cohesion is to be a successful reality. to do that, they have to reach everyone in the spirit of networking. the focus on innovation and researchers, through incentives to keep these talents in europe, together with the creation of centres of excellence, is in my view very well considered in this document as a key element for the economic development of the regions and the member states. there is a growing awareness of the need to decentralize knowledge spots from large population centres to less populated areas, which could offer excellent conditions for the radiation of these centres.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would also like to congratulate my colleague, mrs constanze krehl, on the excellent work she has done on the proposal for a council decision on the community's strategic guidelines. the rapporteur's work was essential in ensuring that several european parliament positions on issues such as sustainable development, the urban dimension, equal opportunities, renewable energy, etc., were welcomed by the council, which is one of the reasons why this recommendation for a favourable opinion of the european parliament is being made. after the adoption of the council decision, member states will have very little time to present to the european commission their strategies for implementing the structural funds, which will already incorporate the community guidelines. it regrets that this tight timetable could jeopardise the implementation of the new cohesion policy as early as january 2007. i would also like to express my agreement with the guidelines and priorities proposed, in particular the idea of cohesion policy as a crucial instrument for achieving the objectives of the lisbon strategy. but let us not forget that the lisbon strategy is based above all on a logic of promoting european competitiveness, as opposed to a logic of solidarity on which cohesion policy is based. it will not always be easy to reconcile these two different logics, but a balance must be found. in the light of the above, i think it is very questionable whether the old member states should commit a high percentage of the funds to the achievement of the objectives of the lisbon strategy and at the same time promote an effective cohesion policy, particularly in the area of territorial cohesion. i am, however, confident that the national strategies to be presented will strike the best balance between competitiveness and solidarity.

in a two-minute speech on the important issue of immigration - which would require a broad approach given the many aspects it covers - i would like to reiterate that: - an end must be put to the security and repressive policies which criminalize immigrants, men and women who only aspire to work and a decent life; - the closure of immigration detention centres and the end of the inhumane policy of deportation; - the fight against traffickers in human beings and those who are in league with them must be undertaken; - the fight against xenophobia and racism and all the policies and distortions which fuel them must be fought; - the need to regularize immigrant workers, ensuring their labour and social rights, a necessary condition for the end of unacceptable situations of over-exploitation; - an effective integration policy is required, including family reunification; - a policy must be adopted to reverse the current concentration of wealth in the hands of a few at the expense of the exploitation and poverty of millions and millions of human beings. some data from the united nations: the 691 richest people in the world have a net worth of 2.2 trillion dollars, or the combined wealth of 145 of the poorest countries. put another way, the 500 richest people have a combined income greater than the 416 million poorest people. the richest 8 million people have a net worth equal to 80% of the gdp of all the countries in the world; - i know . in other words, a policy is needed that uses mankind's ample resources, means and scientific and technical advances to effectively solve the problems facing the peoples of the world. a policy opposed to neoliberalism, militarism and disregard for the sovereignty of peoples and states.
in writing. the extension of this fisheries agreement should allow for better preparation of the new eu-guinea-bissau partnership agreement. the main difficulty facing the community fleet at the moment is the apparent lack of means of controlling and monitoring the guinean eez, particularly outside the 12 miles, which translates into illegal practices that put the sustainability of the fishing activity of the community fleet at risk. this extension maintains the fishing opportunities of the european fleet and is intended to enable the government of guinea-bissau to guarantee the eu conditions for good fishing practices, taking into account the sustainability of the resources exploited. this report deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. the adoption of the progress programme brings together all the community measures which were previously divided into several programmes: the fight against discrimination, the community strategy for equality between men and women, employment incentives, activities relating to working conditions and measures to combat social exclusion. although during the debate and negotiation phase it was possible to improve several aspects of the commission's initial proposal on progress, including now several of our own proposals, in particular the opinion that i was rapporteur on in the committee on women's rights, the truth is that the important point of sharing has not been changed. this means a step backwards for associations working in the area of poverty and social exclusion, because in 2001 it was possible to negotiate a 90% participation and now there is a retreat to 80% which covers all equally, although there may be exceptions, of very difficult approval. that is the fundamental reason why we abstained in this report approving the progress programme.
in writing. the general objective of the community programme for employment and social solidarity (progress) is to provide financial support for the implementation of the european union's objectives in the field of employment and social affairs and to contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the social agenda in the context of the lisbon strategy. the partial political agreement on a common position already incorporates the vast majority of parliament's amendments into the text of the proposal. the positions of the european parliament, the council and the european commission on this programme are broadly in line. i therefore give my full support to the text of the common position which creates the conditions for a rapid adoption of the proposal for a decision establishing the programme. the text does not alter the substance of the commission's initial proposal, but it does bring more clarity and transparency to the implementation of the programme and, in particular, to budgetary matters.
in writing. as europe ages and the economy becomes more global, special attention needs to be paid to social policies in order to strengthen regional and social cohesion in the european area. more than an important social policy instrument, the progress programme is the recognition by this parliament that public policies remain decisive when it comes to promoting employment, social protection and inclusion, working conditions, combating discrimination and diversity and equality between men and women. it is of course very important that europe should see the indicators of economic growth improve. but for that to happen it is essential that member states understand that there is much to be done in fundamental areas, such as moving more decisively towards the completion of the internal market. this vision of more europe and less selfishness is also essential for the success of regional and social cohesion policies. i welcome the simplification that progress provides, continuing the development of activities launched by four previous programmes, in line with the european commission's intention to consolidate and rationalise the eu's financial instruments.
in writing. the swift adoption of the community strategic guidelines (csg) on cohesion is of the utmost importance to advance the ongoing process of programming the intervention of european funds in the member states in the context of the reform of cohesion policy for 2007-2013, so that the new financial programmes are operational as from 1 january 2007. the european parliament had already had the opportunity to express its opinion on the guidelines at its sitting on 18 may in a resolution adopted on the basis of the report by mrs constanze krehl on the preparation of the procedure for giving a favourable opinion on the community's strategic guidelines for the period 2007-2013 (cohesion policy to support growth and employment), which i supported and which was then voted in favour of. the recommendation for a favourable opinion on the proposal for a council decision on cohesion policy objectives put forward by mrs constanze krehl is based on the above-mentioned ep resolution of 18 may. i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. the european parliament has given its majority agreement to the community strategic guidelines on cohesion for 2007-2013, and the national reference frameworks for the different member states are now being submitted. however, we cannot agree with the change that these strategic guidelines advocate by subordinating cohesion to competitiveness, i.e. by subordinating the objective of economic and social cohesion to the objectives of the 'lisbon strategy' and its neoliberal agenda of liberalising markets and public services, encouraging deregulation and precariousness of work, privatising social security and commodifying education and research. in other words, an agenda that calls economic and social cohesion into question and promotes territorial disparities and social inequalities. the introduction of a minimum share of funds for these purposes - defined as at least 60% for the convergence regions - is therefore unacceptable, putting contradictory objectives in competition, especially in a context in which the weight of the funds is reduced to 0.37% of community gni compared to 0.41% in the previous framework. on the other hand, we cannot agree - for the time being - with the extension of the use of public-private partnerships. that is why we voted against it.
in writing. as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on transport and tourism on the commission white paper on services of general interest (sgis), i argued for:- the clear exclusion of both non-economic (signe) and economic gis: the so-called 'services of general economic interest (sgei) ' from the scope of the services in the internal market directive (the 'services directive');- the adoption for gis (including for sgeis, subject to their being subject to sector-specific regulation), instead of a framework directive, framework legislation or a general legal framework, as you prefer to call it; the commission has also proposed that the definition and description of gis and the distinction between signs and sgeis be clarified, in the interests of legal certainty. in general, i think that these ideas are reflected in this report. that is why i supported it and voted in favour of it. however, i regret that the report does not take up another of the main ideas i advocated in that opinion, for which i was responsible: the consideration, within the gis, of the particular situation of the outermost regions, taking into account their specific, structural and permanent constraints.
in writing. we voted against this report because its general thrust is to subordinate public services to competition and to a future internal market in services, taking into account the compromise reached by the council on the infamous bolkenstein directive. at the same time, it whitewashes the effects of the sectoral liberalisations carried out to date, such as in transport, energy and communications, when, contrary to what is claimed and demonstrated by many user and consumer protection associations, liberalisation has led to greater difficulties in access and quality of services provided, to price increases and to the destruction of thousands of jobs under the pretext of sectoral restructuring. the attempt to divide services of general interest into economic and non-economic services, in a commercial logic, aims to place almost all public services under the logic of the market. we, on the other hand, defend the exclusive and sovereign competence of the member states to define the type, organisation and forms of financing of public services, while being certain that public ownership is fundamental in the defence of a quality public service to ensure universal access throughout the territory, supply at socially fair prices, and the democratic sharing of users in the definition, management and quality of these services.
in writing. whatever model of capitalism and market economy we profess, there will always be a need for the provision of services by public entities, directly or indirectly. the commission's proposal is therefore not a mere technical amendment to the directive, but a step in the right direction. however, in view of future developments, three reservations should be made. firstly, the eu is not designed to provide gis, and in the case of gis it tends to be (any exceptions should preferably be cooperation solutions between member states); the legislation on these services should tend to be national, although it should of course respect the rules of the internal market and the principles of freedom of establishment and the provision of services. finally, i regret that a resolution on this subject calls on the commission to make an exhaustive assessment of the effects of liberalization to date, particularly on the situation of the consumers and workers concerned. the term "affected" indicated an ideological choice in a space that should be impartial.
in writing. the eu's internal market has already shown clear evidence of success in liberalising vast sectors of its services, ultimately benefiting european consumers and workers. however, to revive the european economy, the eu needs to take another qualitative leap to complete its internal market and thus take full advantage of its advantages. this leap can be made through initiatives in the field of services of general interest (sigs), non-commercial public services financed mainly from public funds. i believe that the precise definition, formulation, organisation and financing of gis should be the sole responsibility of the member states, in accordance with national realities and with respect for regional and local autonomy. however, the exercise of gis at local, regional or national level has been in conflict with community standards. at european level, such services are in a legal fog, as it is not clear which rules apply to gis in matters such as competition, public procurement or the internal market. the case law of the ecj has also not helped to clarify matters. i support this report because it advocates a complete clarification between the application of community law on the one hand and the pursuit of public interest objectives in the provision of gis on the other.
in writing. one year after the start of the eu accession negotiations with turkey, the turkish authorities have not yet taken any steps towards recognising cyprus - an eu member state - and continue to occupy the north of the island in the mediterranean and disregard the implementation of un resolutions for decades. after a year of negotiations, we are receiving reports and information about the deterioration of the economic situation of the kurdish people and the disregard for their legitimate political and cultural rights, as well as the increased repression by the turkish police and military forces in this region. these two aspects alone would illustrate the multiplicity of issues that accompany the negotiation of the country's accession to the eu. accession by the eu's major powers in view of the ambition of its major economic and financial groups to exploit the country's economy and resources, as well as to use its geostrategic position for its plans of interference and domination in the middle east, the caucasus and central asia. the accession process also brings out contradictions as regards the sharing of the hegemony of the great powers in the eu decision-making process, and exacerbates the contradictions between the ambitions of the great european powers and the us for subordination/sharing in the face of us imperialism.
in writing. the debate on turkey's possible accession to the european union should be conducted in a transparent and clear manner and without any blackmail on either side. this means that the first point, which should be absolutely clear, is that this has to be an open process where the final outcome is not decided. moreover, it must be recognised from the outset that it is not just a question of turkey meeting a set of criteria without which accession would be impossible, but also of the european union being in a position to welcome turkey, to absorb it. on the other hand, as i had the opportunity to say at the beginning of this negotiating phase, i believe that a negotiation in which one party does not recognise the other in its entirety - as is the case with turkey in relation to cyprus and therefore the european union - is a negotiation which starts off on one side and with serious shortcomings. finally, this process has enormous potential for promoting economic openness, development, democracy and respect for human rights in turkey, and this potential cannot be squandered. the worst possible outcome of this process would be a divergence between turkey and europe.

madam president, commissioner, every day thousands of people die because of poverty, mostly children and women. the numbers are staggering: there are 2.5 billion people in the world who live on less than two dollars a day. like i said, most of them are women. poverty is at the root of trafficking in women and children, sexual slavery and gender-based violence. poverty leads to school dropouts, child labour, an increase in children at risk, illegal immigration, fundamentalism and terrorism. without economic autonomy there is no freedom and no equality. women, especially younger ones, are easily lured by international criminal organizations that promise them well-paying jobs in rich countries and then throw them into forced prostitution. women are generally not benefiting from the advantages of globalisation, which favours highly skilled workers, but are instead suffering the negative consequences of trade liberalisation. this report is very timely and i congratulate mrs breyer on the work she has done, which contains important proposals, of which i would highlight the use of micro-credit as a means of reducing poverty. in fact, microfinance instruments have proved effective in combating poverty and it has been women who have taken advantage of them most and best, improving the economic situation of their families. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. there are studies that show that women have the capacity to participate in decision-making at the economic level. there are studies that show that companies that have women on their boards have better results. let us also follow the example of norway, which has already been mentioned.
i would also like to thank all the organisations in the sector which, by their firm action in defence of fishermen and their workers, have contributed to this report summing up a set of proposals which we believe will help to find the solutions required by the serious socioeconomic crisis facing the sector. we hope that the european parliament will support the result achieved in the vote tomorrow. the situation was described by representatives of the sector a few days ago in a meeting with a delegation from the european parliament's committee on fisheries in the algarve, which could be summed up as follows: the fisheries sector is facing a serious economic and social crisis which has deepened over the years. this difficult situation has been aggravated by the increase in production costs, particularly the impact of the increase in fuel prices, combined with the stagnation of prices at first sale, which has put the financial viability of many companies at risk and seriously affected the salaries of crew members, whose salaries depend on the yield of catches and, to a large extent, on the cost of fuel. the common fisheries policy has been inadequate, promoting a steady and significant loss of vessels and the abandonment of thousands of fishermen in a sector considered strategic in some member states. the common fisheries policy pursued to date must be reversed so that it recognises the specific characteristics of each country's fisheries and its right to develop fishing activities in a sustainable way by recovering fisheries resources, with a primary focus on feeding the population, full employment and improving the social conditions of workers, as well as the sustainability of businesses. the sector is moving forward with concrete measures. emergency measures to deal with the sharp rise in fuel costs, such as the creation of the guarantee fund, transitional direct support for the price of fuel, diesel and petrol, and de minimis aid, increasing their value. a set of measures to ensure the income of fishermen, in particular by setting the first selling prices, revising the current rules on the common organization of the market in fishery products and promoting studies to identify measures to improve the value of fish, with a view to channelling added value to the productive sector without penalising the consumer. support for the modernisation and renewal of national fishing fleets, with the consequent definitive abandonment of the indiscriminate culling policy. the promotion of a specific support programme for small-scale coastal and artisanal fisheries. this is the set of measures put forward by the sector during the visit of the european parliament. the european commission, while describing the situation in the sector as serious, has pointed to measures which are far from providing an answer. the difficulties facing the fisheries sector today are mainly rooted in the problem of the cost structure, which is exaggerated in relation to the income obtained. these costs have been suddenly aggravated by the skyrocketing fuel prices, and the solution of reducing fishing effort and fleet adequacy, i.e. reducing the fleet, is not the solution to the problem of improving the economic situation of the sector, which is mainly related to the problem of balancing declining incomes and rising operating costs in the sector. similarly, if we assume that successive fishing restrictions have contributed, though not the only reason, to the worsening of the economic situation of the sector, it is not to be understood that they are accepted or considered as measures to improve the economic situation of the sector. as the sector has stressed, extraordinary situations require extraordinary measures, in particular the use of all the possibilities and financial margins of the community budget for the current year, all the more so since it is a matter of a common community policy - the common fisheries policy - which, in a coherent way, should bear the financing of its costs, in particular within the framework of the european fisheries fund. i would like to conclude by reiterating that the fisheries sector has potential and a future and that it should not be set in opposition to aquaculture. new priorities require more and new means.
on behalf of the pse group. madam president, commissioner, the energy-intensive sector of fisheries is particularly affected by the rise in fuel prices, which is a problem that accentuates an economic situation that is already sometimes quite precarious. a challenge such as that facing the sector requires solutions which do not deepen the problems by attempting to respond to them with uniform regulations, detached from their practical control or from the specific conditions of their field of application, but which take account of the particular realities in their complexity. while it is true in general that we must move towards a reduction in fishing effort, the use of more selective gear, and the positive discrimination against small-scale local fishing, which is better able to preserve the freshness of fish, it is no less true that, in particular, these general objectives may have to be achieved by increasing the power of engines and the size of vessels, which provide more comfort and safety at work, as well as by diversifying the focus to activities such as tourism. the existence of a highly detailed, centralised legislative network, unconnected with the control of its practical application and its real impact on the situations it aims to serve, favours the proliferation of illegal, unreported and unregulated catches within and outside the community area, widening the gap between the virtual world depicted by the legislation and the real world of the european fish market. it is essential to achieve greater decentralisation of the cfp and to ensure greater local involvement of fishermen, their representative organisations and fishing communities in this policy and in improving fisheries management. as the fao handbook for the conservation of fishery quality points out, the first principle of a sustainable fisheries policy is to avoid the tragedy of the commons, that is, that what has no known owner, be it buffalo or fish, everyone will rush to exploit and ultimately destroy. and that is why only through the responsibility and direct commitment of fishermen can we think of improving their economic situation in a sustainable way.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i welcome the commission communication on the improvement of the economic situation in the fisheries sector, which is in itself a sign that something needs to be done for the sector, with emphasis on the weakest part of the cfp. the cfp aims to ensure and maintain a balance between the economic and social development of fishing communities and the sustainable management of fisheries resources. it must be borne in mind that in both aspects of this common policy, fishermen and their communities are in many cases in a situation as or more fragile than that of many of the threatened species. i do not mean that we should forget the sustainability of resources for the sake of the economic viability of the sector, because that would be damaging to the environmental sustainability and the future of these fishermen. the commission's communication, however, is inconsistent with the diagnosis it makes of the solutions the sector needs, which are largely contained in the report by mr pedro guerreiro, whom i congratulate. the balance between the two aspects of the cfp requires that we focus on the promotion of selective crafts, small-scale fisheries, aquaculture and scientific research, but also on socioeconomic support. this support must compensate for the permanent loss of income resulting from the disappearance of jobs and the decrease in income resulting from recovery plans or from deep changes in profitability conditions caused by external factors. this is precisely the case in the present distressing situation resulting from the increase in fuel. the commission should do more in this area. similarly, some member states should make better use of existing possibilities. the formation of fish prices also needs to be considered. it is unacceptable that fishermen should be mere price takers, whose prices are increased tenfold between the first sale and the consumer price. we must think about supporting producer organisations, but also about the legislative frameworks that exist to create more justice and protect those at the bottom of the whole sector.
madam president, commissioner, we all agree on the economic and social importance of the fisheries sector in the european union and on the commission's diagnosis of it, which confirms its critical situation. nor is there any doubt about commissioner borg's sensitivity to the problem and his willingness to seek to mitigate its consequences by the means currently available. however, the responses advocated by the commission are clearly insufficient and are considered disappointing by the sector, especially small-scale coastal fishing, which has the greatest social impact. if there were any doubts, they would have been totally dispelled by the missions which the committee on fisheries carried out this year to greece, italy, france and, in recent days, portugal. the commission communication and the report under discussion, whose rapporteur i also congratulate, have the merit of warning against an unsustainable situation which cannot continue. we cannot have a common policy to communitize restrictions and then nationalise the solution of problems 'à la carte' according to the possessions of each member state. the problem of fuel costs, to which several members have already referred today, and of the stagnation of fish prices and the renewal of the fleet without increasing capacity must be dealt with swiftly by the community. i therefore hope that parliament will approve the report and that the commission will follow up its practical implementation.
member of the commission. mr president, i would like to thank mrs miguélez ramos and the fisheries committee for the opinion on the commission report on the operation of the so-called shark finning regulation. i am pleased to note that the rapporteur praises the clarity and conciseness of the commission’s report and shares the view that this regulation is achieving its objective. let me assure you that the commission is committed to monitoring the application of this regulation to ensure its proper implementation, including of member states’ obligations regarding control and reporting. the commission will also continue to promote the prohibition of shark finning in international forums. in addition, the commission will continue in its endeavours towards the adoption of measures based on scientific information and other considerations within regional fisheries management organisations. i would also recall that the prohibition of shark finning practices is not the only way to ensure a sustainable fishery for these species. a more comprehensive set of management measures is required. we have already taken some measures in this respect. i refer, in particular, to special efforts to improve scientific knowledge and data collection, to establish catch or effort limits for certain species, including deep-sea species, to prohibit drift nets that may catch some large pelagic sharks and to control and limit fishing capacity. as rightly pointed out in parliament’s motion for a resolution, the commission has identified numerous actions to halt the loss of biodiversity by 2010 and beyond, including community plans of action for sharks and sea birds. my department is currently looking into the request for the presentation of a community plan of action by mid-2007. while it is too early to have a clear overview of the detailed work programme for 2007, it is clear that a formal, complete and detailed plan of action requires a comprehensive assessment of the situation and of the possible measures, together with an early consultation of all interested parties, which will take time and resources. the desired timeframe seems rather too ambitious, and setting too short a timeframe for preparation and consultation could even be counterproductive. i would prefer to be less prescriptive in terms of deadlines. however, i can assure honourable members that my department will undertake to complete the plan of action at the earliest possible date. returning to the report’s core concerns, i have taken good note of the proposed calls for the commission to present amendments to the shark finning regulation, especially with a view to reviewing the 5% fin weight versus live body weight ratio on the basis of a species-dependent approach, and to revise the possibilities for separate landings of fins and carcasses, as well as to report again on the operation of this regulation within two years. when deciding on this regulation, the council did not consider it appropriate to adopt a species-specific approach regarding the fin to body weight ratio. i think the reasons mentioned in the debate then are still valid now. a single 5% fin to live body weight ratio applicable to the whole shark-catch of a vessel is a realistic, feasible, controllable, simple and proportionate method of preventing shark finning practices from spreading. the commission’s report also confirms this. i am not, therefore, of the opinion that amendments to the regulation should be proposed at this stage. firstly, because the regulation was only recently adopted and is working well overall. secondly, because the commission believes it would be unwieldy to start revising the fin to body weight ratio or introducing some species-specific approach to the shark finning regulation without new measures to ensure sustainable shark fishing. the much broader exercise of preparing a community plan of action for sharks will necessarily include a reassessment of developments under the shark finning regulation and its possible need for review, especially on the basis of the national annual reports, which are available for all those interested. it is at this point, therefore, that we will be able to consider once more the situation with respect to body-fin ratio and make any recommendations accordingly. parliament’s necessary full involvement in a proposal for a plan of action will also provide another opportunity for parliament to be informed about and to play a role in developments on shark finning matters. the commission will continue to monitor the situation. you can rest assured that i am always ready to act and to present all supporting evidence if new information becomes available indicating significant changes in the situation. i am committed to advances in the area of shark conservation and other aspects of marine biodiversity, and will inform you in due time of the progress made. (applause)
i would also like to thank mrs miguélez ramos for her work and say that it is necessary to clarify and emphasise that since 2003 the practice of finning has been regulated in the european union and that sharks cannot be fished solely for the purpose of exploiting their fins. so this is a targeted fishery for a species like any other, which puts the issue of the sustainability of the resource on a par with what happens to other fish, so the question of feeding catches does not fall within the scope of this report but within the framework of quotas or even recovery plans according to the usual scientific reports. what we are discussing here is the fact that the commission's communication recognises the positive effect of the 2003 regulation and its implementation. what has been most in question in this debate, however, is the percentage of the weight of the fins in the total weight of the sharks. what the icat reports say is that the total utilisation of fins by the community fleet differs, for example, from the partial utilisation by the united states fleet, which is why it will be necessary to study the possibility of changing the percentage in the light of reports which already point to an increase of 5 to 6.5%. and that's what this is about. to ignore this reality is to confuse the full exploitation of a fishery with the preservation of a resource. we have to preserve the resource, but that's on another plane. in the plan we are discussing, the adaptation of the utilization rates to reality and to scientific reports will ensure that leaks are avoided. the compromise solution reached by the three largest political groups ensures that the european parliament understands that this is the way forward, thus responding to the studies already carried out by recognised bodies of which the european union is a part, and ensuring, on the other hand, that the conditions for compliance with the law are met, thus contributing to a truly sustainable and regulated fisheries.
in writing. the european commission intends to amend regulation (eec) no 2092/91 currently in force on the import of organic products in order to streamline the procedures for the recognition of imported organic products, but it does not go as far as necessary. the commission has also proposed a number of amendments to the proposal to protect consumers and national producers. the need to control products imported from third countries is therefore stressed, in order to ensure that the product has been produced in accordance with production standards equivalent to organic production in the european community and that there is reciprocity. it would not be fair to farmers and consumers in the european union if the same controls were not required as those required of farmers in the european community. it is also essential that, as a minimum, the competent national authorities are involved in the process of recognition of third country control bodies. however, the fight against fraud will only be effective if there is control and recognition by the national authorities of the importing countries.
in writing. the galileo programme - the european radio-navigation and satellite positioning programme - when used for non-military purposes and not integrated into the security apparatus, is in itself an important instrument which, in order to ensure the provision of a public service, can represent great opportunities for cooperation, scientific and technical progress and for the exchange and accessibility of information, while ensuring respect for the rights, guarantees and freedoms of citizens. this programme could help to end the dependence on the us-controlled gps system, which is managed by its military services, which even make it difficult to access and use it when carrying out military aggression against peoples and states. we therefore regret that the majority of the european parliament voted against the amendments tabled by our group, which rejected the use of the galileo programme for military purposes and stressed that the galileo programme should provide equal access for all users and that the public should be able to use the information available free of charge.
in writing. galileo is the community project par excellence for implementing the lisbon strategy. the european satellite radio navigation programme is a new technological challenge that will bring further growth to the european economy and business opportunities. we must therefore ensure that this is not just another project. this first european infrastructure, managed by the community, is of crucial strategic interest for the implementation of the lisbon strategy. in a europe populated by smes, this is the moment of great opportunity. the community institutions must therefore ensure their good governance. moreover, ensure transparent and effective rules for public-private partnerships and ensure that we exploit the full potential of this project. it is therefore essential to ensure that the full and timely exploitation of the project opportunities is achieved and this can only be done if we realise that this is the right way to go.
in writing. the tampere council set out an ambitious political programme for europe - to build a common european area in which the issues of freedom, security and justice are in perfect balance. the balance that was sought then is still too fragile today. what we are seeing is a security trend overtaking concern for human rights: the fight against terrorism and illegal immigration clearly dominate the agenda of justice and home affairs. the new hague programme for 2004 lacks a vision for the future. the problem of immigration calls for the community's decisionmaking method, the legitimacy that comes from the european parliament's intervention in the co-decision procedure and a binding charter of fundamental rights. immigration policy must be a humanistic, preventive union policy, geared to cooperation with the countries of origin. it requires a solidarity commitment between member states based on common duties, or it will not be a fair policy.
in writing. i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the eu's common immigration policy (rc-b6-0508/2006) because of the need for the european union to adopt a genuine common immigration policy and to remove all obstacles to the creation of a european asylum system that would make it possible to define common standards for the protection of the fundamental rights of immigrants and asylum seekers in the european union. the european union should adopt a cross-cutting approach to open up pathways for legal immigration and encourage the integration of migrants into host societies based on regular integration into the labour market, the right to education and training, access to social and health services, and effective participation of migrants in social, cultural and political life: on the other hand, it is essential to support the development of countries of origin in order to address the root causes of migration.
in writing. the resolution contains aspects which we regard as positive, such as the recognition of the current drama and the need for legal migration channels, effective integration and development plans in the countries of origin. however, we believe that it does not denounce the eu's security and repression policy, criminalising irregular immigration, promoting border buffer measures, the setting up of detention centres and the expulsion of immigrants. we are also against the creation of a common immigration policy, because it is not the appropriate answer to the questions and problems that arise, as the results of other common policies show. the reality of migration differs between the countries that are part of the eu and the decision on this policy must respect the sovereignty of each state, which obviously does not prevent cooperation in this field. what is needed is not a common policy but a policy and other measures that effectively protect the rights of immigrants - such as ratification and compliance, notably by portugal, with the un convention on the protection of the rights of all migrant workers and members of their families - and tackle the root causes of immigration.
in writing. immigration is a sign of economic vitality and a factor in the entry of active and enterprising people. illegal immigration, on the other hand, is a mafia business, a threat to the lives of applicants and an incentive to the parallel and inhuman labour market. that is why measures such as extraordinary legalisations are good intentions with bad results. they're a small prize for illegal immigrants and a huge asset for the smuggling mob. if we want immigration to have a positive effect, we have to consider the absorption capacity of the market as the fundamental concept. but this can only be achieved with clear and workable rules that facilitate legal immigration and make illegal immigration impossible, and this is a problem of a european dimension. that is why i have rightly argued that the re-equipment of the armed forces must take into account the component of the protection of the external borders, which are common borders. finally, i do not believe that the solution lies in strengthening law enforcement alone. the way forward - against uncontrolled immigration, poverty and the threat of terrorism - is through the export of wealth, economic prosperity and our liberal democratic model.
in writing. the important report on eu-india relations covers a multitude of, sometimes contradictory, aspects. although it contains points which raise concerns which we share, the report is in line with the prospect of liberalizing world trade in the framework of the wto or through the proliferation of bilateral or multilateral free trade agreements, and in the framework of competition and coordination with the usa, which we clearly reject. the report advocates the so-called 'doha development agenda' and the progress of the currently stalled negotiations for the liberalisation of trade and markets worldwide. the report again stresses the eu's demands by urging india and the g20 to 'understand' (???) that 'a european proposal in the field of agriculture must be followed by a reasonable g20 proposal in the field of market access for non-agricultural products and services', which is unacceptable. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. the initiative report in question has the important merit of reminding us of the importance for our future of a proper strategy in the relationship with india. the concept of brics is an important concept for understanding the current state of the world economy, but it cannot make us believe that brazil, russia, china or india are countries for which we should develop identical strategies. on the contrary, i did. our relationship with these countries must be reflected from a strategic point of view so that the result of globalisation, economic development and the growth of world trade are factors of prosperity for all - or for as many as possible, at least, which implies different strategies. a democratic and populous india is different from a non-democratic but populous china or our neighbour russia. if we want to be a successful project, one of our priorities must be to think about our future in the light of the development of these countries and to devise appropriate strategies for the relationship with each of them, the case of india being the most important. in geographical, political and economic terms, its situation deserves special attention, as it is expected to be an important ally in the future.
in writing. we voted in favour of this resolution because, despite some contradictions, it has a positive view of women's involvement and the fight against discrimination, particularly in the field of international trade. however, we cannot fail to point out that we should go further in criticising the liberalization of international trade and its negative consequences for the people of the least developed countries, with particular emphasis on women, and that we should criticise in particular the action of the epp, which has sought to prevent a more progressive view of the struggle for women's rights. we should also have gone further in criticising the harmful actions of multinational companies which use women's work in one country while they cannot find another where they can make higher profits, without worrying about the consequences in worsening unemployment and women's living conditions.
in writing. with this vote the european parliament has confirmed the main proposals already unanimously approved in the committee on fisheries, with a view to improving the economic situation of the fisheries sector, which we consider to be positive. these are proposals that have long been put forward by representatives of the fishing industry to deal with the economic and social crisis they are facing, a crisis now aggravated by the sharp increase in the cost of fuel. we welcome the inclusion in the final text, on our proposal, of the definition of a clear priority for marine resources and fisheries, with adequate funding, in the seventh framework programme of the community for research, technological development and demonstration. we also welcome the fact that, despite pressure from members of parliament from the main 'net contributors' such as germany, the request to increase the funds for the european fisheries fund has been maintained, in a context of insufficient resources to deal with the implementation of the instruments of the common fisheries policy, as expressed in this resolution. it is now up to the commission to take initiatives to make them a reality. however, we regret the fact that the request for the creation of public insurance for the fisheries sector to deal with unforeseeable situations has been dropped, when this same parliament is asking for it for other sectors such as agriculture.
in writing. the report calls on the commission to bring the rules for shark fishing into line with the realities of community fisheries, particularly as regards the percentage of the limit weight - currently 5% - of fins in relation to the live weight of the catch. this limit, which has been transferred from the reality of the usa, does not apply to species fished by european union countries, in particular the blue whiting, which is the species mainly caught by the national fleet in azorean waters. we agree with the rapporteur in proposing that this limit be raised to 6.5%, in accordance with the existing scientific studies and the requests of several member states whose fleets are affected by the present commission impasse. this has already been referred to in iccat itself. in the portuguese case, 11 longliners are involved in the swordfish and pelagic fisheries, where the 5% ratio applies. i take into account, even in the amendments that have been tabled, that there is some contradiction between scientific and technical opinions, and we think that a technical forum should be held, with the participation of scientists and professionals in the sector, in order to reach a scientific consensus and clarify the need to change the level of the limit set and the degree of change.

president of the commission. mr president, first of all let me welcome the broad support that was given for the agenda for innovation, for a european institute of technology, for a common energy policy and for a european immigration policy. but let me tell you that we need to deliver that message outside this room, because, as some of you said, there are still some misunderstandings. let me just mention the eit. it is interesting that everybody agrees that in europe we are not doing enough in terms of innovation; there are not enough links between the universities and the research centres and the world of the economy, business and practical projects. but when an idea comes to change that situation, immediately there is resistance. it is amazing! everybody then says, ‘but we have excellent universities!’ – of course we have excellent universities! but if we have excellent universities, why are we falling behind the americans and others? something is wrong. the status quo is not an option. we cannot go on with business as usual. i know we have excellent universities. universities were created in europe. they are a european creation, but we are not taking advantage of the full benefits or the full potential of our european dimension. let us be frank: some of our universities are still very corporatist, very closed. we need a european dimension. even the biggest member states lack the dimension to promote the global culture we need now to face the challenges of this 21st century. therefore, the idea is network-based. it is not a huge bureaucratic institution; it is network-based, building on the principles of excellence, on what all excellent universities and excellent research centres are doing, but with a view to connecting businesses with research so that we can promote innovation. at the commission i met with the leaders of the most important european companies that are driving research in the world. i got great support for the idea and i could name some of the companies. two of those leaders in european business came from the united states, and they told me at the meeting that their biggest shock when they came to europe was to discover great institutions to promote research in germany, britain, france and sweden. we have great things, but we are missing a european dimension. we are missing a european mission to give them the real tools they need to compete with the best. that is why i believe this is a great idea. i hope that, not only will it be supported in general, but that it will be supported when we come forward with practical proposals. that is why i hope to have your support when we come forward next week with a practical proposal on the eit, and i hope for your support when in january we come forward with a policies. it would not be credible, let’s face it. the first thing to do if we want to be seen from outside as credible, is to put our own house in order and to have a real joint approach to energy. the same, of course, applies to other issues. but i strongly agree that the fight against climate change is a crucial element in our energy policy and we should recall that the european union is a key player in that field. we are, in fact, leading in the world. i can tell you that when we discuss this matter with our american friends, with our russian partners, or with the chinese or indians, we always put this question at the forefront of our negotiations. it is important to do what we can, but also to involve others in those efforts. but what all these issues show – from innovation to immigration, to energy, to the fight against climate change – is a strong argument for europe. in the age of globalisation, even the biggest member states do not have the means to tackle those challenges. so if you want a strong europe, we are going in the right direction. a strong europe is not bureaucratic, but has a common approach to those issues. we should also speak with one voice on human rights, and i hope that this is the message which comes out from lahti: the european leaders may come from different political and ideological backgrounds, from different national situations, but they are ready to build a strong europe together and they are ready to speak with one voice to the outside world. that is what i am hoping for from lahti.
the next european council, in addition to important items on the international situation, includes on its agenda the so-called 'innovation policy', the proposal for a 'common energy policy' and 'illegal immigration', topics for which working documents have not yet been submitted. we'll get back to them at another opportunity. the debate on 'absorption', 'functional' or 'assimilation' capacities, i.e. enlargement (croatia and turkey) and institutional reform (composition of the commission and the ep and decision-making in the council) seems to be out of the question. that is, the debate on the definition of the rules of the game, always imposed by the great powers of the eu and in accordance with their interests. the debate on attempts to (re) impose the so-called 'european constitution', which has already been rejected, is also on the agenda. so far, and despite many attempts, contradictions persist as to what they think can be done at this time to resurrect the 'european constitution' (recauchuted or not). but they are preparing the ground, setting up think tanks, while they await the elections in france and the german presidency of the council, which will point the (pseudo-) 'way'. their hesitations are directly proportional to the consciousness of the workers and peoples as to the real meaning and class aims of the eu.
the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a very good one. the commissioner will be aware of the closure and relocation of many companies and the destruction of jobs in the footwear sector in portugal, which has increased unemployment and the risk of poverty for thousands of workers. the situation of the workers of the multinational c&j clark in castelo de paiva, who, three years after its closure and after many promises, are now without alternative employment, should be recalled. in other words, with the liberalisation of world trade, workers have been lost in numerous micro, small and mediumsized shoe companies in the european union. on the other hand, the people who have benefited from the rapid increase in footwear imports from third countries are not the so-called consumers but the large multinationals and the large importers and distributors who have accumulated fabulous profit margins, as has been acknowledged by the commission. if large international trade were really concerned about the interests of consumers, it could have long ago reflected this concern in a significant reduction in the selling price of the footwear it imports. the responsibility for this situation, commissioner, as we have been saying, should not be placed on third countries but on the european union and its policies to promote competition and to liberalise international trade, and on the maintenance of the value of the euro, which is detrimental to productive sectors such as footwear. the commission has already announced its intention last week to increase bilateral free trade agreements and to launch a new crusade for the liberalization of world trade. it is precisely this policy that must be called into question.
the european union has made a good decision, but a late one, by imposing an anti-dumping duty on imports of leather footwear from china and vietnam. but better late than never! it is not new that china and vietnam export a number of products to the world, including footwear and textiles, which benefit from strong state intervention at the source. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's financial instruments are used to the full. these products also benefit from a total or almost total absence of social and environmental regulation, which accounts for a significant part of the production costs in the countries of the european union. the european shoe manufacturers know that they have to compete with firms that produce at lower wages and cannot accept that competition is distorted by this kind of intervention by exporting countries that sell the goods below the price of production itself. in my country, we call this a "battle". the european union has made a good decision, albeit belatedly, but it has also made a complacent decision because what we see is a lack of will on the part of the authorities of these countries to change their behaviour and given their repeated insistence on unfair practices, i preferred the initial version of the sanctions which envisaged anti-dumping tariffs for a period of five years, rather than two years, as was finally decided. in conclusion, i would like to ask: given that the majority of the council that supported these measures was weak, only 13 of the 25 member states, will this split within the two continue? and if it does not, what will the european union do? commissioner, let me be very clear: i am not in favour of protectionist policies. i want everyone to play by the rules!
the advocate of free trade considers that only in absolutely exceptional circumstances, duly verified, should recourse be had to the adoption of a trade defence instrument such as 'anti-dumping' duties. but that is unfortunately the case here. china and vietnam have been engaging in particularly unacceptable trade practices in the footwear sector, in part because they add to the already numerous competitive advantages that these countries have. in doing so, these two states are violating a fundamental principle of free trade: the principle of loyalty. and that is why these measures cannot be seen as being against free trade but, on the contrary, must be seen as measures which are indispensable to safeguard free trade in the long term. we must therefore welcome the work that the commission has done in this area. it is important to stress, however, that european industry cannot rest on its laurels of modernisation by focusing on innovation and quality enhancement in order to increase its international competitiveness in the sector. this effort must be supported by the public authorities, while respecting the rules of free, fair and equitable trade. the adoption of the present measures cannot therefore be seen as an attempt to reopen the door to undesirable protectionism, but as an indispensable instrument for ensuring the fair and correct regulation of international trade.
the defence of production and employment with rights requires that the commission and the council pay more attention to the productive sectors, in particular industry, in each of the member states and not only take account of the interests of economic groups based on international trade. sectors such as footwear, textiles and clothing have been particularly affected by this disastrous policy of liberalizing international trade, particularly in the context of the wto. thousands of jobs were lost. in portugal alone, the shoe industry is characterised by the c&j clarks factories in arouca, castelo de paiva and vila nova de gaia, the rodhe factory in trancoso, ara in avintes, the reductions in the number of jobs at ecco and rodhe in santa maria da feira, and many others, particularly in the felgueiras area. but this policy has not only led to the loss of workers and numerous micro, small and mediumsized enterprises, but has also blocked the regional development of large areas, particularly in portugal. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's trade policy is not distorted by the introduction of new barriers to trade.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the budget is properly managed. mr president, commissioner, rapporteur, i would like to take this opportunity to convey the testimony of the committee on budgetary control, which, in at least two missions - one to thessaloniki and one to kosovo - was able to testify to the capacity, efficiency and innovation which it has represented in the framework of the community's external action to the european agency for reconstruction. it is unparalleled by anything we have seen in community action. it is a very good example of what can be done on the ground in conjunction with the local forces, and i think it would be a grave mistake to let it go and not use it in other circumstances. the european commission and european funds cannot simply be a gateway to the united nations or to ngos or to any other institution without any real capacity to administer community funds on the ground. this experience has been very valuable from this point of view and i would appeal to the european commission not to let it go to waste because it would be very bad for the whole of the european union.
mr president, i would like to take this opportunity to welcome the day of struggle of the portuguese workers and their trade union centre cgt-in, who are holding a general protest against the right-wing policies in portugal tomorrow, 12 october. among other things, portuguese workers are fighting against the government's proposals for social security to raise the retirement age and reduce pensions, they are fighting for the defence and increase of national production, for the creation of jobs with rights, for the defence of public services and a public administration at the service of citizens, for the right to collective bargaining, for the increase of wages and for a fair distribution of wealth. a final note, mr president, on the recent decision of the european court of justice in the cadman case concerning maternity/paternity leave and the calculation of wages, to state that it is totally unacceptable that this means and can be used to call into question the principle of 'equal pay for equal work', a principle which is enshrined in article 59 of the constitution of the portuguese republic.

in writing. i support the conclusion of these bilateral agreements for the participation in the european monitoring centre for drugs and drug addiction of romania, bulgaria and turkey. these three countries are included in the list of the 13 candidate countries covered by the accession process and this type of agreement is intended to reinforce the pre-accession strategy, which allows them to be given authorisation to participate in community programmes and agencies. they are thus one of the main ways of strengthening the capacity of the applicant countries to apply the acquis communautaire, since they serve as a kind of preparation for these countries and their citizens to become familiar with the union's policies and working methods. these agreements stipulate conditions of participation in the emcdda similar to those governing the participation of norway. the advantages of these agreements will undoubtedly be numerous, but i see no problems with the arrangements for participation, either at technical level (they will have a link to reitox, they will share data, in full respect of community and national data protection rules) or at financial level (they will have to contribute to cover the costs of their participation), participating in the management board but without voting rights.
in writing. the ep has consistently rejected all initiatives put before it when consulted on detailed matters relating to europol. we find ourselves in that situation once again. i therefore support the rapporteur's position, mr claude moraes, that we should reject both the initiative on the amendment of the staff regulations for europol and the initiative on the adjustment of their basic salaries. i fully understand the need for europol to make internal adjustments, but there is no point in parliament having a say since, as an intergovernmental institution, parliament plays no relevant role in the administrative decision-making of this institution. we have supported numerous initiatives to extend europol's mandate and give it operational powers, helping to make europol an effective instrument in the fight against organised crime. but we have also been insisting on the need for this process to be accompanied by measures to ensure democratic and judicial control. i therefore hope that the commission will soon present a proposal to integrate europol into the eu institutional system, and that the europol convention should be replaced by a council decision, in which the structure, working methods, areas of activity and tasks should be defined in co-decision.
in writing. although the council's common position on a proposal for a directive on the patentability of inventions involving computer programs was rejected by a large majority (648 votes) in the european parliament in july 2005, the european commission relaunched the debate on the future of the patent system in the european union in january this year, thereby circumventing the outcome of that vote, which in turn resulted in a large mobilisation and popular opposition. the central issue is the attempt to create a european organization for patent litigation and a european patent court whose decisions would supersede those of the national courts of each member state. this court would be under the authority of the national representatives who sit on the board of the european patent office and who would be responsible for appointing judges. in recent years, the institute has granted hundreds of patents, for example on software, which some countries consider invalid. with the loss of sovereignty, national courts could not rule against patents. the resolution adopted today, which we voted against, reaffirms that patenting ideas and knowledge and hindering intellectual freedom, technological innovation and the competitiveness of the european economy itself is unacceptable.
in writing. i voted in favour of the first part of paragraph 71 of the jeggle report for the following reasons: 1. bullfighting is a centuries-old tradition, rooted in different regions of different eu member states, with different characteristics, and in the portuguese case, the killing of the bull was for the first time prohibited in 1836; 2. bullfights are responsible for the existence of the bullfighting. without them, this species would have long since become extinct, since its rearing is of no economic interest for meat or milk production; 3. this does not mean that the bullfighting spectacle and the tradition associated with it should not evolve and adapt to the moral values of each historical moment, in this case aiming, as soon as possible, at the elimination of any physical suffering of animals. there are now forms of sport with a high sporting status that have evolved from violent traditions, such as fencing, for example, which does not require the practitioners to be physically harassed to be practiced today. the iron bar may well be replaced by an electronic stick whose contact with the animal produces the same spectacular effect. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. since animal protection and welfare are important, and since the quality of human life is also linked to food safety and the quality of animal products, account must be taken of specific traditions and cultures. we support a number of ideas in the report, including: the protection of animals is a sign of humanity; extending the scope of european animal welfare policy beyond farm animals; taking account of the regional and environmental specificities of the european union; advocating a cross-cutting animal welfare policy that includes legislation, vocational training, financial support and scientific research. we welcome the reference to the need to take account of the size of farms and the additional costs of animal protection, and to compensate farmers, especially small and mediumsized farmers and family farmers, for the financial losses incurred in implementing animal welfare measures. as regards bullfighting, we disagree with the rapporteur's position, since it is not right to include everything in the same plan. for example, it is not correct to consider rope bullfighting in the azores on the same level as death bullfighting, although these also have to be understood in the context of local cultures and traditions that may evolve into new practices.
in writing. i voted in favour of the epp amendment which provided for the deletion of the word 'bull' from paragraph 71 of the jeggle report. i voted this way because it is important to ensure the survival of the bullfighting bull, which is guaranteed by the bullfighting institution. however, i am disgusted by the spectacle of bullfighting as it is practised at the moment in portugal and other eu countries. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the animal welfare system is properly managed. as with other aspects of the daily life of our societies, bullfighting will have to evolve in such a way as to lose the barbaric characteristics that have inherited and still distinguish it. no aspect of collective life should be immune to the progress and evolution of sensibilities. in this respect, this resolution should serve as a warning to those who reject any change in the bullfighting system: it is imperative that this activity evolves rapidly to a situation where it is no longer dependent on the suffering of animals. otherwise, my country, portugal and the eu must take drastic measures. the way a society treats animals reveals more than just its attitude toward them. it reveals the degree of civilization, humanity and progress at which it stands.
in writing. this owninitiative report is flawed for two reasons. the commission has not yet adopted the proposal for a directive on the protection of animals during transport. since the minimum requirements for membership of the european union are not at issue, i do not think that the community institutions should comment on this matter. moreover, the temptation to try to impose on one member state, by means of community 'legislation', the cultural traditions and values of another member state, or the particular view that any of them has of the cultural traditions or values of others - which, moreover, involves an arrogant and totally unacceptable attitude - is an undesirable method and practice. regardless of what opinion we have of the traditions in question. let us leave to the european union what should be community, and let us leave to the member states what should be their responsibility by nature.
in writing. the report has one objective: to assess and promote reforms in the professional services sector by deregulating and eliminating all obstacles to competition. moreover, the objectives of total deregulation and strengthening competition set out in the kok report of november 2004 and included in the 2005 review of the lisbon strategy were met. it is also part of the process of liberalising the services sector and creating an internal market for services, as proposed in the so-called bolkenstein directive. in this sense, there is a tendency to regard self-regulating organizations of the liberal professions as obstacles to the free provision of services. we agree that some of these services are in the public interest and should be considered as public goods, and that there should be rules to ensure the quality of the service and to ensure the protection of users/consumers. but this cannot call into question the right of the states to regulate these activities at national level or to allow self-regulation by professional organisations. the legitimacy of their drawing up regulations, based on traditional, geographical and demographic particularities, or other special regulations (for example on advertising) must be guaranteed.
in writing. the proposal to conclude an association agreement and a free trade area between the eu and mercosur is part of the current drive to open up markets to competition at world level, particularly in the context of the current impasse in the wto. the report makes explicit the eu's ambition to dominate latin america - particularly the mercosur countries - in relation to the ftaa, while at the same time not calling it into question. what are the contradictions? the ep also calls for the introduction of a single currency for all sectors, including the so-called 'singapore issues' (investment, competition, public markets and trade facilitation). moreover, this majority is proud to point to the eu as a model of integration for latin america. we believe that the liberalization of markets calls into question the sovereignty of peoples and (some) states over their resources and over the definition of the path to their development. with the liberalisation of world trade, workers are under pressure on wages and labour rights, the vast majority of small and mediumsized farmers and smes are being challenged, the interests of large multinationals and the concentration of capital are being promoted. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. as history teaches us, trade is an effective factor in promoting good relations between peoples and economic development. that alone would be a good reason for wanting and seeking an agreement with mercosur - as i have had the opportunity to advocate both in public interventions and in political initiatives before the commission. but to the reasons given are added others, of historical and cultural proximity, which make our efforts in this area even more justified. we think in particular of brazil or the very strong portuguese community in venezuela. the recent accession of venezuela to the agreement also gives it a new dimension in foreign policy, since it is not only an oil producer but also a country to which the european union must pay particular attention. the potential for progress and economic development in this agreement is enormous, and that is why, insisting on a subject which i have followed, i join the rapporteur in the hope that the commission will do everything possible to make the creation of this enormous economic area feasible.
