to ensure its great flexibility and the reception of many innovative proposals. despite some reservations i expressed during the first reading debate, i sincerely hope that they are right. in this panorama of full interinstitutional understanding and cooperation, one negative note stands out, as is easy to see. i am referring to what cannot be overlooked, namely the very limited resources available for the culture programme 2007-13. the first reading gave me, the rapporteur and many of the other members who took part in the debate, the opportunity to draw attention to this point. we are facing a third generation programme which is intended to go further and be more effective than the previous ones, a programme which envisages a wider range of measures and a greater number of member states involved, a programme which involves more management and evaluation costs, and yet the budgetary allocation falls far short of all these ambitions, as it falls far short of what all those responsible, from the members of the commission to the ministers of culture, from the cultural agents and operators to the members of parliament, consider to be essential. i believe, however, that we should all hope that the culture 2007-2013 programme will be a great success and make a significant contribution to the construction of the europe we are all committed to.
in writing. the council's common position, which is the subject of this report, differs significantly from the commission's initial proposal of 2004, notably the inclusion of the 'nature and biodiversity' component, the objectives of which are, inter alia, to support the continued development and implementation of the natura 2000 network, including coastal and marine species and habitats, and in particular to achieve the objective of halting the loss of biodiversity in the community by 2010. the inclusion of this component in the life+ programme is in line with the position adopted by the european parliament at first reading in july 2005, which we regard as positive. however, despite our vote in favour of the programme and its objectives, we cannot but regret that the budgetary resources foreseen for the implementation of the life+ programme, covering the period from 1 january 2007 to 31 december 2013, are manifestly insufficient and are the result of the bad agreement for the 2007-2013 budgetary framework. moreover, they fall short of the commission's own estimate, which, it should be recalled, estimated the needs of the natura 2000 network at eur 6.1 billion per year, i.e. eur 3 billion for co-financing, and the amount proposed by the commission in 2004, and the guarantee of co-financing of the natura network through the structural funds will not allow all needs to be met.
in writing. the life+ programme and its predecessors are the main instrument for financing projects in the environmental field in the european union. the council, in a wrong and insensitive way, substantially reduces the budgeted amount. the european parliament reintroduces the value initially agreed, in accordance with the financial perspective, for the financing of the natura 2000 network for the conservation of nature and biodiversity. the amendment aims to ensure that european funds for the environment are not used for other purposes related to the life+ programme, such as staff costs, as it provides for delegation of project management to the member states, instead of the usual management by seconded staff. there is also an amendment to the commitment that if no agreement is reached at second reading, measures will be taken to continue funding for ongoing projects. for portugal this report is of great importance, since a significant area of the continental and outermost territory is part of the natura 2000 network, the financing of which is defined in this report. the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of national authorities responsible for the protection of the environment.
in writing. i congratulate my colleague, mrs graça moura, on her position at second reading on the common position adopted by the council with a view to adopting the european parliament and council decision establishing the 'culture 2007' programme (2007-2013). i express my support in particular for the amendment to the common position concerning financial support for the actions referred to in article 8 (2) (d) of the decision of the european parliament and of the council establishing the 'culture 2007' programme.
in writing. the civil protection mechanism was set up five years ago to facilitate the mobilisation and coordination of civil protection resources in the event of emergencies within or outside the eu. during 2005, more than 10 countries activated this mechanism to respond to emergency situations. the aim of this proposal is to strengthen the mechanism in the light of experience gained since 2001, provide a legal basis for future community action in the field of civil protection and complement the emergency preparedness and rapid response instrument. this report includes the 'public health' dimension in civil protection. it also stressed the importance of solidarity between member states and a more effective european surveillance system. it also addresses the issue of effective land use and management in disaster prevention and the use of military means to prevent and respond to emergency situations. this mechanism is of great importance for the whole of europe and in particular for portugal, which is plagued every summer by serious problems of drought and fires, which fall within the scope of the proposed mechanism. the socialist group therefore supports the report by mr papadimoulis.
in writing. the report adopted today is positive overall and makes the response to emergencies more coherent and effective on the part of the european union and the member states, although we have some differences on some aspects. we know that the fundamental objectives of civil protection are the prevention of collective risks and the occurrence of major accidents or disasters resulting from them, and therefore the need to mitigate collective risks and limit their effects in the event of occurrence, to rescue and assist people and other living beings in danger, to protect property and other cultural, environmental and public interest assets and to support the restoration of normalcy in the lives of the people affected. we therefore welcome the possibility of focusing on studies, training, prevention and monitoring, and of encouraging the exchange of experience, in order to take advantage of the lessons, both positive and negative, of the interventions and to correct them. we also support the establishment of a dedicated and appropriate emergency communications network and the conduct of broad information campaigns, as well as the adoption of education and awareness-raising initiatives aimed at the public, especially the young.
in writing. it is well known that female immigration is steadily increasing in the european union, and now accounts for about 54% of the total number of immigrants, for a variety of reasons, notably economic reasons, family reunification, and seeking refuge and asylum. in general, women face numerous difficulties and multiple discriminations, which require a strengthening of public support policies, in particular social structures and services. it is particularly important that international conventions, including those on family reunification, are applied and that migrant women, irrespective of their irregular status, are guaranteed all human rights, including access to education for their children, the right to family benefits and health. in any case, we believe that immigrant women who enter a member state of the european union under family reunification should be guaranteed the possibility of obtaining a legal status independent of their spouse as soon as possible. we also believe it is important to ensure that immigrant women and young women, particularly those who are victims of physical or psychological violence, including forced or arranged marriages, are granted a residence permit and that all the support measures they need are taken.
in writing. the recovery of community funds which have been misused - and each situation needs to be examined - requires greater attention, particularly from the member states. consider the situation of relocation of companies which have used community funding for years or situations where public health is at stake, in particular in one or more member states, where cooperation between the different states and bodies should facilitate and improve a rapid recovery of the amounts concerned and prevent the companies or organisations involved from continuing to benefit from community funding. however, we cannot agree that this need, which is valid in itself, should be used to catapult another federalist advance, as proposed in the report, by suggesting the creation of a public prosecutor's office and a public prosecutor at eu level, which would in fact cement another step that would subordinate the sovereignty of the states.
it is not surprising that the european parliament's proposal for the community budget for 2007, representing 1.04% of the community's gross national income, although it improves both the european commission's proposal, which represents 0.99%, and that of the european council, which represents 0.98% in terms of the volume of payments, falls short in the first year of the agreed level in the financial perspectives, that is 1.06% of the community gni, which we consider already insufficient in itself to promote real economic and social cohesion, particularly in the face of the needs of an enlarged european union. as this is a stage in the negotiating process, we hope that, unlike in the past, the european parliament will at least try to ensure that the minimum amounts stipulated in the financial perspective for 2007 are respected as much as possible, and that these financial resources are put at the service of an effective policy of economic and social cohesion and of a genuine policy of cooperation and development. while we welcome the adoption in the committee on budgets of specific amendments tabled by us, we regret the rejection of other important proposals, such as the creation of compensatory measures to deal with the increase in fuel prices in the fisheries sector and the creation of a community programme to support small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing to respond to the specific problems of this sector, in line with previous positions adopted by the european parliament, or the increase in the budget for convergence in the european regional development fund to fully compensate the so-called 'statistical effect regions' such as the algarve, which suffered a cut of some 20% this year.

on behalf of the pse group. mr president, the increase in international trade over the last few years, which has led, among other things, to increased competition, has led many countries to resort to trade defence instruments as a means of protecting their markets. it is therefore not surprising that we are seeing a rise in a number of situations where anti-dumping, anti-subsidy and safeguard measures are being adopted. european exports, as the report now under review clearly shows, have on several occasions been the target of such measures by third countries. these cases have been increasing in a worrying way. the traditional countries are now joined by some of the new players in international trade relations. this phenomenon, which can cause significant damage to various sectors of the european economy, must therefore be tackled seriously. a serious approach would, of course, require a correct and strict separation between cases in which the use of these instruments is strictly the result of the legitimate application of the principle of loyalty in commercial relations and cases in which their use is no more than a legal device to illegitimately conceal genuine protectionist intentions, in the worst sense of the word. that distinction can be made with complete clarity only if the emphasis is on enhancing transparency in the handling of proceedings leading to the assessment of the lawfulness or unlawfulness of the use of trade defence instruments, thus seeking to ensure full compliance with the rules and case-law of the world trade organisation. the commission should therefore endeavour to contribute to the improvement of these procedures, thus helping to discourage the misuse of these instruments. the commission's support to member states and european industry in trade defence cases brought by third countries is also important. this support is particularly important for small and mediumsized enterprises, which are naturally less prepared to deal with such situations. finally, we believe it would be useful if the commission were prepared to take an active part in joint work within the wto in order to carry out a balanced review of the provisions governing the adoption of trade defence instruments in the interests of enhancing multilateralism. however, in this debate, it should not be forgotten at any time that the european union is already the most open trading area in the world and that europeans also have legitimate interests to safeguard.
it is worrying that the european institutions are increasingly underestimating the social consequences of this acceleration of neoliberalism, which not only keeps unemployment, poverty and social exclusion high, but also increases precarious and low-paid work, trying to make the so-called 'flexi-security' mean forcing workers to give up their fundamental rights and accept increasingly precarious jobs. the measures being put into effect and those being announced, such as the liberalization and deregulation of services and the dismantling of public services, are emptying the concept of the european social model, which deserves our vehement opposition. this is why protests against these policies are growing, as happened in lisbon on 12 october, with the grand demonstration organized by the cgtp, the largest since the 1980s, with about 100,000 workers. do you not think it is time to take account of these just indignations?

against the backdrop of the summit, forces are moving in concert on how to (re) start a process, disregarding the sovereign and democratically expressed will of the french and dutch peoples, which will seek to (re) impose the unacceptable treaty, incorrectly and abusively called the 'european constitution'. these sinister intentions have been coming more and more to the fore. the portuguese presidency of the council in the second half of 2007 will have the "enormous responsibility" of "taking the first steps in the implementation of the (so-called) constitutional change programme" and "will be the launching pad for the new (so-called) european constitution", putting into practice a "programme" previously defined by the german presidency and to be completed by the french presidency in the second half of 2008. the capitalist integration of the european union, a neoliberal, federalist and militarist integration which the so-called 'european constitution' would strengthen on the legal and political level, will once again, despite all the propaganda, mystification and demagogy, be firmly rejected by all the forces fighting for a europe of sovereign and equal states, social progress, cooperation and peace.
the rapporteur. mr president, the council was not able to attend the debate on monday and has now made a statement. i think it is legitimate for parliament to react to the council's statement through your rapporteur. if i may, mr president, i would just like to say two very simple things. the first is that i congratulate the presidency on the work it has done on this dossier and i believe that parliament can count on the presidency to strengthen the external borders and help to increase the security of our citizens through the legislative act we are about to adopt. but if it is true that the presidency has done very well in this process, it is also true that the council as such has not done so well. the council has not honoured the commitments it made at the trialogue in may in this city of strasbourg. i hope that the council will not do to the finnish presidency what it did to the austrian presidency, that it will honour its commitments and approve the document as we will approve it, because only then will we have an agreement at first reading and only then will we not delay the entry into operation of the second generation schengen information system.
in writing. the resolution adopted deserves my vote against for several reasons. first of all, i think it is unacceptable to call initiatives (these or any other) aimed at putting an end to the terrorist activity of eta a 'peace process'. the choice of words is equivocal and not innocent. there's no war here. what we have here is a democratic, free state that respects autonomy and a people who have been the victims of indiscriminate violence by a terrorist group for no good reason. secondly, i cannot vote for a resolution which does not clearly recognize the impossibility of negotiating with a terrorist group which refuses to renounce violence explicitly and in advance. finally, i understand that spain and the spanish people are free to resolve the question of basque terrorism as they see fit, but i refuse to subscribe to a european parliament resolution on this subject which makes no reference to the unjustified and indefensible motives of eta. the european union must not be allowed to continue to be a victim of terrorism. in this case the very substance of the terrorists' complaints merits our condemnation, and it does not elicit any relevant support in terms of democratic voting.
in writing. the terms in which the motion for a resolution was put to the vote are offensive to a large part of the spanish people and, above all, to the victims of terrorism in spain, as was made abundantly clear by the association which represents the overwhelming majority of the members and which has been calling the process initiated by the spanish government a surrender. the title itself wrongly indicates the existence of two legitimate sides involved in a peace process when what is at stake are negotiations between a government and a terrorist group responsible for the death, persecution and extortion of hundreds of spanish citizens. it is important to remember that after the eta ceasefire declaration, there have been threats from its members, no weapons have been handed over and there are reports of attempts to rearm it. opening an unconditional dialogue with terrorists who not only do not condemn, but do not justify the armed struggle and show no remorse for the innocent lives they have taken, is an incredible concession on the part of the political power of a democratic state. there is no reason for celebration. i cannot but deplore the opportunism of the zapatero government, which has tried to win international support which it has not obtained from its own citizens.
in writing. today, the european parliament is voting on the report by mrs lissy gröner on the 'youth in action' programme for the period 2007-2013, which deserves my support, especially as it will guarantee the funding of youth activities throughout europe. this new programme provides for five types of action: youth for europe, european voluntary service, youth for the world, social and educational encouragement and support systems and support for political cooperation. europe thus continues to rely on a youth policy as a means of strengthening the sense of belonging to europe of its citizens and of contributing to the development of its young people, based on the necessary solidarity and mutual understanding between all.
in writing. even this programme is a testimony to the lack of attention the european union pays to its citizens. of course, the financial figures are very low. there were about 60% cuts over the budgeted amount. but it is also true that it is an ambiguous programme. in addition to interesting objectives such as support for twinning of cities, civic projects, surveys, various studies, artistic events and conferences, there are others which reveal unacceptable policy options, such as excluding fascist crimes from support in the new action 4 - european active memory. as regards the changes in the budgetary allocations within the programme itself, the strengthening of action linked to education is welcomed, but it is hoped that the inclusion of such educational projects will be done by ensuring the pluralism of positions on the european union and the policies practised and not by trying to turn it into another forum for propaganda. we welcome the inclusion of amateur sports organisations and hope that there will be pluralism in its application.
in writing. the 'europe for citizens' programme aims to bridge the gap between citizens and the european union by providing the union with instruments to promote active european citizenship. it encourages cooperation between citizens and their organisations from different countries, so that they can meet, act together and develop their own ideas in a european environment that transcends a purely national vision and respects their diversity. i voted in favour of this report, which, by introducing the two amendments that follow, makes it possible to improve the 'europe for citizens' programme. firstly, by reducing the budget for action 1 'active citizens for europe' from 47% to 45%, it will be possible to increase the budget for action 2 'civil society in europe', which is particularly suitable for financing projects on europe, its values and cultures. finally, as regards the overall objective of the programme, i support the rapporteur's initiative to integrate the strengthening of tolerance in order to ensure that projects financed under this programme contribute to active citizenship which promotes mutual respect and intercultural dialogue and combats racism, xenophobia and discrimination.
in writing. perfluorooctanosulfonates (pfos) are toxic, persistent and bioaccumulative products present in some applications as colourants, waterproofing agents and fire retardants. the report, in contrast to the commission's original proposal, proposes a phasing out of the placing of pfos on the market with a view to phasing out their use and removes certain initially envisaged derogations (in the case of metal chromium and fire-fighting foams for which there are already viable safer alternatives). the administrative threshold of 0,1% proposed by the commission is further amended by an amendment to the undertaking to a new threshold of 0,005%. it also provides for the drawing up of inventories of products in which pfos are used by each member state in order to prevent releases of these substances into the environment. i agree in particular with the amendment which proposes that current derogations can only be maintained if there are no safer substances or technologies that are technically and economically feasible and if the best available techniques are applied to minimise pfos emissions. the amendments seek to ensure that the commission's proposals are implemented in a way that is consistent with the objectives of the treaty.
in writing. i voted in favour of the reports by mr carlos coelho because i consider them to be of the utmost importance for the defence of the interests and security of our citizens. the sis ii system will allow the enlargement of the schengen area to new member states to take place as quickly as possible, not only by updating and increasing its capacity, but also by introducing the new possibilities that the latest technological developments allow. the key point, however, is that the operation of this system should allow for greater security in the management and control of personal data, without losing sight of the fundamental individual rights, and thus ensure our citizens that all measures are taken to effectively combat organised crime, illegal immigration and other crimes that undermine their security and interests.
in writing. the objective of the report is to extend the sis features beyond their original purpose by developing new features, extending its access to new authorities, interlinking alerts between them, adding new categories of data - such as the arrest warrant and biometric data - and a technical platform for sharing information with the visa information system. this extension from the previous system entails high risks for the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens by adding new elements to a database which is also shared by more bodies and is accessible to more people, and there is no full guarantee of confidentiality of this data. there are also other concerns in this proposal, namely that records may be 'kept for a longer period if they are necessary for control procedures already in progress' (the question here is who defines this 'need' and the vague notion of 'control procedures already in progress'). another area which is too vague is the sharing of data with third countries made possible by the proposal. the basic aim is to adapt sis to the new needs arising from enlargement and the dangerous and unacceptable objectives of the current security offensive in the eu.
in writing. the report advocates trade liberalisation and the principle of reciprocity and the imposition of retaliatory measures. the whole logic of this is competition for market shares in the name of competition. not a logic of cooperation where trade has a role to play in development, but it is not everything. anti-dumping or anti-subsidy measures are interferences in the internal decisions of each country and threats that can be imposed by the wto. the losers are the developing and the less developed countries. the report also defends the wto and the dispute settlement mechanism, seeking to alleviate whatever trade defence mechanism is more offensive (anti-dumping) or more defensive (safeguard). to lighten the dispute mechanism and give it more power is to strengthen the weight of the great powers in the wto, because they are the ones who have the capacity to impose rules. the essential point is that trade liberalization is contrary to the logic of equitable development. each state must have the right to decide its own model of economic and social development, to industrialize and to protect its industry. this right cannot be denied. it is a sovereign right, which calls into question the model of export promotion and free trade.
the aim of the report by mrs de keyser is dialogue and the future normalisation of our relations with syria. we see the association agreement as part of that political process. the political emphasis is that the agreement is much more advantageous for europe than for syria itself from an economic point of view. the freezing of relations with damascus was a political mistake. europe cannot have blacklists, nor can it subscribe to the american theses on the axis of evil. syria, regardless of its regime, is a key country for peace in the region. on the other hand, europe must learn to appreciate the complexity of syrian society and the plurality of its views. the regime is as authoritarian in politics as it is soft in economics and liberal in religion and customs. plurality is stifled and suppressed, but it exists in society and in the institutions themselves. it will be all the greater the less the western powers interfere in the region. it is a pity that the final version of the report suffers in several places from the tics inherited from the colonial age: for example, it's not our job to name who is trustworthy and who is not, because we don't accept third parties, and very well, that kind of opinion. it would also be better not to cast imaginary suspicions about damascus's relations with al-qaeda or sunni fundamentalism, which do not exist. ignorance is not good for us and we owe it to ourselves to be consistent. you can't make diplomatic relations contingent on the outcome of a criminal investigation. the proof of the crime of the horrible murder of rafik hariri must be made in court, otherwise our policy violates the principle of the presumption of innocence. the report is clear on the essential points. you want to normalize relations, and that's good. it is also good that the issue of human rights is at the heart of this normalisation - it just needed europe to make this same policy with all other countries, including israel. and finally, it supports the return of the golan heights to damascus, a guarantee that is supported in un resolutions and that syria has never sought to reclaim by violent means.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the barcelona declaration sets out the objectives of building a common area of peace, stability and prosperity by strengthening political and security dialogue, economic and financial partnership and social, cultural and human partnership. this objective has been successfully pursued over the last few years and there are already association agreements with virtually all the countries of the mediterranean basin, except, of course, syria, for various and understandable reasons. the european union has always taken account of the situation in recent months. it must seriously engage in genuine negotiations with that country in order to achieve its firm will to conclude the agreement, moving towards a democracy which respects human rights, religious freedom, the fight against terrorism and promotes dialogue and a consistent peace in the region. to this end, it is crucial that the syrian government act to ensure that the end of the state of emergency is swiftly a reality, with all possible assistance from the european union. syria has a geo-strategic situation of the utmost importance and a crucial role to play in the middle east peace process. it must be made clear once and for all that the european union considers that democratic consolidation cannot be achieved by a policy of bombing or isolation.

the report by barbara weiler, on behalf of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, on public-private partnerships and community rules on public procurement and concessions [2006/2043 (ini) ] (a6-0363/2006) follows.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, the discrimination that many workers from eu member states, such as portugal, continue to face when they go to work in other countries, also members of the eu, but where higher wages are paid, is well known. the directive on the posting of workers states that it is the sole responsibility of the host country to ensure the protection and rights of posted workers, and the country concerned is obliged to take measures to prevent the minimum standards from being circumvented, giving rise to situations of genuine discrimination, which ultimately affect all workers, both posted and those in the host country. but reality has shown us that this directive is being ignored in many quarters, despite the numerous requests, both from the european parliament and from specific cases, as we have done on several occasions. there is still a situation of non-compliance which must be resolved and we cannot accept the commission's position that it intends to limit, in important areas, the minimum requirements imposed by the member states on companies, which, moreover, follow on from the proposal for a directive on the creation of the internal market in services. in supporting the rapporteur's work, we cannot but deplore the pressure and proposals the epp is maintaining following its attempts to prevent clarification of important aspects of the implementation of the directive itself, such as the deletion amendments it has made to several points in the report under discussion. the attempts to delete paragraph 13 and parts of paragraphs 26 and 29 of the report are particularly serious. we, for our part, insist on defending the rapporteur's work and on approving a number of other proposals aimed at complying with the directive.
mr president, mr commissioner, the dynamism of the internal market has provided increased mobility of workers and has helped european companies to develop their activities in a transnational manner. the possibility for companies to second some of their workers to another member state of the european union for the temporary execution of a job has also contributed to this increased mobility. however, the experience gained so far leaves much to be desired. in the portuguese case, especially in the construction market, the posting of workers has gone badly. several cases of exploitation of portuguese workers have been detected in spain, france, the united kingdom and the netherlands. this is because there is a gap between the 1999 directive, which strikes a balance between the freedom to provide services and the safeguarding of the labour rights of posted workers, and the application of the directive on the ground. in addition to divergent interpretations of the directive by the member states, there are also practical difficulties in its implementation which have contributed to more barriers, more bureaucracy and slower procedures. the lack of control over the application of this directive is obvious. subcontracting is a striking example of situations which, although very frequent, are not covered by the directive, which leads to an unacceptable dilution of responsibilities and always to the detriment of posted workers. i support mrs schroedter's report because i believe that it is the duty of the host member state, in close cooperation with the authorities of the country of origin, to ensure that the employment conditions laid down in the directive are respected in order to increase the effectiveness of monitoring and combating illegal practices. i also support mrs schroedter's report because it is necessary to adopt corrections to better organise support, monitoring and implementation of this directive in a systematic way.
mr president, i also agree with the proposal to postpone this debate and the vote on it until november for the very reasons which have been mentioned, namely that it is too important a matter to be dealt with in 15 minutes or so.

in writing. reaffirming our criticism of the central aspects of the negotiating strategy and the priorities set by the european parliament for the 2007 community budget, we think it is important to highlight the adoption of some of our proposals, which are aimed at: - strengthening the convergence allocation of the european social fund; - promoting cooperation and associativity between micro, small and medium-sized enterprises; - protecting and preserving forests, with forest fire surveillance and prevention measures and actions; - promoting, conserving and protecting cultural heritage, such as the european cistercian route and unesco heritage sites; - promoting cooperation between agricultural organisations and other rural actors with a view to revitalising the world; - promoting rural or family farming, small and medium-sized farmers and young farmers; - carrying out studies or reports on: child labour in the eu; - unemployment and displacement; - the unemployment of workers in the eu; - the impact of new technologies and information on the prices of essential goods and services and the impact of seasonal and labour market diseases outside the country of origin; - the banking and information on the prices of goods and services; - the impact of the banking and financial services sector.
in writing. the structural, economic and social situation of the fisheries sector in the outermost regions and the adoption of the new european fisheries fund require the extension of the derogations provided for in regulation (ec) no 639/2004 as regards the criteria and conditions for structural actions relating to the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources under the cfp. the proposal for a council regulation providing for the extension of these derogations for the outermost regions until 31 december 2006 and the practical implementation of the measures adopted in the meantime until 2008 should of course be adopted as soon as possible so that it can actually have the practical effect it is intended to have. i agree in substance with the purpose and content of this document, and i regret that the implementation plan for the renewal and modernisation of the fisheries fleets of the ors cannot be implemented for the whole duration of the next financial perspective, instead of the time limit set for 2008. in spite of this, and because this derogation still represents positive discrimination against the ors, i am voting in favour of the adoption of this proposal for a regulation.
in writing. the purpose of this proposal is to extend until 31 december 2006 and then until 31 december 2007 the derogations granted to the fishing fleets of the outermost regions as regards the entry/exit capacity of fleets and the application of public aid for the renewal and modernisation of fishing fleets. it was therefore urgent to approve this proposal in view of the specific structural, social and economic situation of the fisheries sector in the outermost regions - in particular the azores and madeira - together with the permanent difficulties and constraints of these regions, such as the small size of the markets and insularity. the question is that for many of these regions the existing economic activities, in this case fishing, are of very high socioeconomic importance, in particular in ensuring the consumption of fresh fish by the population. since these derogations are necessary and given that the fleet situation is structural - not cyclical - and as is acknowledged by the european commission and the council, what is important is that these derogations become permanent and be included in the european fisheries fund for the period 2007-2013.
in writing. one of the greatest virtues of the recent enlargement of the european union is that it also involves an enlargement of our memory. for most of us the hungarian uprising of 1956 is a distant memory in time, in geography and even in politics. but the entry of countries such as poland, the baltic states, slovenia and hungary itself brings with it the active incorporation of another memory. for a year and a half, that memory is also entirely ours. from this comes a whole new geo-strategic notion of our place in the world, which we must integrate and update, while implying a different understanding of what the struggles for democracy in the 20th century were. on the other hand, and this is obvious, this moment should serve as a reminder that communism was not romantic or utopian. the history of communism is the history of repression, of violence, of inhumanity. we remember.
in writing. we are of course not calling into question the conclusion of an association agreement with syria, which is reportedly the only country in the region with which the ec has not concluded an association agreement. however, we disagree strongly with some of the important and central points in the report. the report is characterized by a line of interference and imposition on a diverse set of issues on which only the syrian people can decide sovereignly. moreover, the european parliament is blaming and accusing syria of the situation in the middle east, which it has never dared to do in relation to israel and the united states, which are the main responsible parties for the dangerous and dramatic situation in the region. the report states, among other things, that the aim of the agreement is to 'transition the political regime' in syria and to create 'an open market-based economy'. it seeks to impose on syria compliance with un security council resolutions on lebanon, but omits that israel continues to occupy part of syrian territory, attacks lebanon and maintains its policy of state terrorism against palestine. it criticises syrian policy and calls on it to review 'its foreign policy and its alignment in the region'. which we consider unacceptable.
in writing. the adoption of this report, which is essentially balanced in its version negotiated with the epp, still deserves some reservations. the european union has neither the power nor the capacity to act as a world power, both because of substantial impossibility and because of practical difficulties. it lacks the military means, the finances and, above all, the vocation. but this does not mean that the eu should be a passive member of the international community. europe as a market, europe as a financial support, europe as a land of welcome for immigrants, europe as a neighbour - all these dimensions make - or should make - the eu a partner in foreign policy. this is not the usual reference to the virtues of soft power, nor is it the discussion of the need for alternative poles. i am talking about the capacity that these dimensions should give the eu to influence and change policy in one of the most important regions: the mediterranean. the eu must be able to produce the same effect on its neighbours in the medium term as it did on the countries which joined it in succession. a different model is needed to reproduce the effects of the expectation of accession on a mediterranean scale. unfortunately, this agreement does not yet reflect that ambition.
in writing. the wortmann-kool report calls for the appropriate promotion of water transport, which has so far been little developed. this safe, environmentally friendly mode of transport, whose infrastructure is far from being fully utilised, could contribute to modal shift and thus to reducing the congestion problems affecting other modes of transport. the increase in trade after enlargement also seems to favour the development of new markets, such as this type of transport. since it is of the utmost importance for the future of a sustainable transport policy that we adopt measures to re-balance the transport modes, i consider the development of the inland waterway transport market to be significant, since it can, from its development stage, include all the strategic areas important for the optimum development of this market. therefore, taking into account the different characteristics of the european territory, it is essential to contribute to an appropriate legislative framework that allows the development of markets that can participate in the transfer of traffic to alternative types of transport. i am therefore a portuguese member of the european parliament and i support this programme, which, while not promoting national interests, i am confident will also have positive consequences on the transport market in portugal.
in writing. public-private partnerships are very popular in the member states of the european union and, of course, the united kingdom is the european champion. but in fact they are a euphemism for privatising or preparing the privatisation of public goods and services, giving, for long periods, the concession of these goods and services to private for their profitability. and this, advocates say, is to better manage risk. what is forgotten is that the private sector gets the profits, the state always ends up paying, especially when the partnership "goes wrong" or does not guarantee the profits that the private sector wants. and this applies to everything from granting motorways to running hospitals and schools to participating in investment projects under the structural funds. they are a form of outsourcing of state responsibilities, which we cannot agree with. the initiative also aims to have a legal regime at community level. we can therefore only vote against this report.
in writing. the european parliament has fulfilled its annual ritual of sanctioning the monetary policy of the european central bank (ecb). although the report advises caution in raising interest rates and the need for investment, it considers price stability and fiscal consolidation, which threatens economic growth, employment and the purchasing power of wages, as central objectives. when economic and social concerns have been imposed, changing the fundamental objective of the ecb, the recipe is more of the same - structural reforms, of course, in the labour market and social security. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a welcome one. this is in a rotating voting system in the governing council, adopted in 2003, which has excluded small countries from voting on monetary decisions. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. it won't be hard to tell who's in and who's out. for all these reasons, we could only vote against.

mr president, commissioner, first of all i would like to congratulate mr mulder and mr goepel on the excellent work they have done and to say that i support the proposals contained in their reports. the decision taken by the council last december to make voluntary modulation possible may represent a distortion of the conditions of competition between farmers in several member states, as a result of different options as to the modulation percentages to be adopted. the proximity of the 2008 cap help check, where we can discuss the increase in compulsory modulation and the cap, is another reason why we are not moving forward now with measures such as voluntary modulation, which may have irreversible consequences. if this proposal is accepted, we will clearly be taking another step towards the renationalisation of the cap and the dismantling of the community approach to agricultural policy. without diminishing the political importance of rural development, i must say that this measure will not strengthen investment in this policy, and i give the example of my country, which is the one that returns the most second pillar funds to brussels, and the one in which, in the european union of 15, there is already the greatest balance between the first and second pillars, 53% and 47% respectively. however, in my country, portugal, the minister for agriculture has already announced his intention to adopt the 20% modulation. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. with these practical risks, which are already clearly detectable in countries like portugal, as i have just mentioned, it is clear that in order to defend farmers and a common agricultural policy uncompromisingly, we must do everything possible to prevent the proposal for voluntary modulation from being put forward.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, by its contribution to employment, to doubling gdp over the next two decades, sesar will be a key priority for the union and its member states and an indispensable condition for meeting the challenges of the next few decades: ensuring the safety and fluidity of air transport at european and world level, improving the functioning of the market and competitiveness, improving the management of environmental effects, improving european cohesion. on the relevant points i would like to make, firstly, the legal basis should not be article 161 alone, but should be a double one, consisting of articles 161 and 163, in order to increase and improve the involvement of the european parliament. secondly, in the management model, private initiative, industry, operators and the scientific community must certainly be guaranteed, as the commissioner has said, but it is essential to ensure that the partners with the largest public obligations, the commission and eurocontrol, play a key role in terms of financial participation and also voting participation, with a view to efficient air traffic management and technology, and also without any impact on the taxpayer's taxation.
in writing. the united nations convention against corruption is in fact the first instrument designed at global level to prevent and combat corruption. it thus aims to create a strategy and an overall framework with a set of minimum but important standards which should be applied to all participating states. those rules should cover the prevention, investigation and prosecution of corruption, as well as the freezing, seizure, confiscation and return of proceeds of such offences. the commission negotiated this agreement, which covers those elements of the convention which fall within the community's field of competence, and concluded the negotiations in september 2005 on behalf of the community. i therefore support the conclusion of this agreement. but i regret that three member states (sweden, slovenia and estonia) have not yet signed this convention. i hope that the ratification process, which has been carried out not only by the community but also by the member states which have not yet done so, will be completed as soon as possible. stressing the crucial importance of its entry into force as soon as possible, so that more effective action can be taken to prevent and combat this type of crime.
in writing. this report could only have my vote in favour, of course. the fight against corruption at global level is an indispensable objective for good governance in the various members of the international community and, therefore, a fundamental factor for peace and development. even before the ethical considerations, the economic considerations, there is a previous point that makes the fight against corruption on a global scale a key factor in international relations. countries with corrupt governments are governed by rules, criteria and interests that are incompatible with those of sustainable development, cooperation and peace. combating them is combating one of the causes of conflict and poverty. it is not enough, however, that we sign these conventions; in international practice - particularly in the field of cooperation, in which the eu plays such a significant role - this struggle must be part of our criteria for action. that is the meaning of my vote in favour.
in writing. the commission proposal under this report aims to bring regulation no 1698/2005/ec into line with the agreement of the european council of 15/16 december 2005 on the financial perspective 2007-2013 as regards the 'cohesion support fund ceilings for transfers' and the exemption of portugal from the application of the co-financing requirement of eur 320 million. under the terms of the agreement, the amount of eur 320 million to be allocated to portugal would not be 'subject to the national co-financing requirement', 'taking into account the specific difficulties of portuguese agriculture'. for portugal, first, the provision of a 'national envelope' within the overall allocation foreseen for the new rural development instrument (the eafrd), and then the doubling of the initially proposed amount, plus such an exemption, in recognition of the difficult situation of portuguese agriculture, were one of the aspects considered most positive of the political agreement reached under the uk presidency in the arduous and long negotiations on the next financial framework for the period 2007-2013. i therefore voted in favour of the report by mr jan mulder, which proposes adopting the commission's proposal.
in writing. apart from the general considerations on the need to link agricultural policy and funds for farmers more closely to rural development objectives, my vote in favour of this report is also justified by the fact that the portuguese exceptional nature has been recognised and, for that very reason, the requirement for national co-financing has been excluded here. as is clear from my question to the commission, in the recent past portuguese farmers, national agriculture and potential rural development have been harmed by the inability or lack of will of the portuguese government, leaving large amounts of money unused. that is why this exceptional situation is fully justified.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mrs marie-nöelle lienemann (a6-0373/2006) on a proposal for a european parliament and council directive establishing a framework for community action in the field of marine environment policy, because this 'marine environment strategy' directive will make it possible to give the necessary effect to the 6th environment action programme on the promotion of the sustainable use of the seas and marine ecosystems. a significant proportion of europe's citizens live in coastal regions and depend on the sea for work or leisure. the development of national marine strategies - with the aim of achieving good environmental status and protecting and maintaining the most vulnerable marine ecosystems and biological diversity - will allow the maintenance of activities in the marine environment at sustainable levels that do not compromise the uses and activities of future generations, nor the ability of marine ecosystems to respond to natural and human-induced changes.
in writing . we consider it important to take the initiative of establishing a framework for action in the field of marine environment policy, with the appropriate financial means. because of its strategic importance, it is essential that member states define environmental assessment strategies and objectives for their marine environment, in collaboration with other member states and third countries, as this is an area where the actions of some may affect others. but there is a fundamental issue in this whole process - the ownership and management of the marine waters to which this directive applies. both the proposal for a directive and the amendments adopted today in the lienemann report start with the definition of 'european maritime waters', leaving it unclear what an eez is and what the role of each member state is. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment is a very important one, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done. in view of the lack of clarity on these issues, we abstained from the final vote.
in writing. the proposal for a 'marine environment directive' aims to establish a high level of protection for europe's seas and oceans, a greater knowledge of the same heritage about which there is still so much to discover and define a management strategy with an integrated approach and with qualitative and quantitative objectives to reduce pressures on marine resources and their ecosystems. the inclusion of the reference to the need for co-financing by the european union of the measures to be implemented to enforce the directive and its inclusion in the budgets from the year 2007 is emphasised. this measure is very important for portugal, since it is a country with a large exclusive economic zone (the largest eez in the european union) which therefore entails high costs. the approval of the change in the deadline for achieving the set objectives (from 2021 to 2017) proposed by the epp shows the ambition with which parliament is dealing with this issue and how involved it is in the pursuit of a 'good environmental status' for the marine environment. the other measures proposed by the epp to ensure the sustainable implementation of economic activities involving seas and oceans, the protection of biodiversity and the prevention of pollution are also of great importance, substantially improving the european commission's proposal... (the minutes were approved)
in writing. we welcome the initiative of a policy for the marine environment in the framework of the necessary cooperation and coordination between the different countries, safeguarding their full sovereignty over their territory and resources, and taking into account economic, social and environmental aspects. the conservation of fisheries resources is threatened, in particular, by marine pollution and intensive maritime transport, which have impacts on fishing activity. fishing is not the only element, nor will it be the most important. fisheries resources and their regeneration are indispensable to ensure the future of fisheries, without fish there is no fishery. fishermen are therefore the main stakeholders in the protection and regeneration of the marine environment. in this context, the measures to recover resources must include the necessary economic and social compensation measures for the sector and its workers, with adequate funding. the central issue is respect for the sovereignty of the member states, in particular their eezs, and their capacity to implement autonomous measures in the defence of their fisheries resources. finally, since the maritime strategy must be linked to the cfp, the latter cannot impose its structures on those of fisheries.
in writing. the proposal follows the 'community strategy on mercury' adopted in january 2005, which aims to reduce the use of products containing mercury by prohibiting the placing on the market of devices containing mercury. the adoption of this report prohibits the placing on the market of all types of measuring instruments and amends the original proposal of the european commission so that the new regulation enters into force as soon as possible. the regulation excludes products already placed on the market, appliances considered to be old and collectible, and barometers, the production of which must be duly licensed, and only the possibility of phasing out is provided for. the use of traditional barometers in europe is very low, as is the total volume of mercury they represent. their exclusion from this proposal, as well as from measuring instruments more than 50 years old, is an important measure since, it protects existing small producing industries, the mercury used is generally recycled and reused, and if they were included (and the traditional barometer production industry is extinct), unforeseen contamination and flows of mercury could result... (the minutes were approved)
in writing. i voted in favour of the maría sornosa martínez report (a6-0287/2006) on a proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending council directive 76/769/eec on the restriction of the placing on the market of certain measuring instruments containing mercury, because, given the high toxicity of this substance to humans, ecosystems and nature, it is important to define restrictions on the marketing of these products, which will prevent the entry of considerable quantities of mercury into the waste stream and contribute to a higher level of protection of the environment and human health. mercury-containing appliances should be replaced whenever safer alternatives are available on the market, but exceptions may be allowed where alternative solutions do not yet exist, as well as in rare situations related to the maintenance of traditional barometers, museum collections and industrial heritage.
in writing. we voted against the rapporteur's proposal and therefore in favour of the commission's legislative proposal because 'modulation', that is to say the possibility of transferring up to 20% of the appropriations allocated to farmers who receive more than €5 000 per year from the first to the second pillar of the cap, is an essential instrument for introducing some fairness in the distribution of agricultural aid. it should be noted that in portugal only 5% of farmers receive more than €5000 per year. we cannot understand why the current situation is preferred to the alternative of 'voluntary modulation'. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. in the portuguese case, the proposed implementation would increase support for rural development by some eur 50 million per year and benefit many farmers who are currently excluded from any support.
in writing. the central point of this report is that the commission's proposal is not a proposal for genuine modulation, i.e. a proposal to increase aid to those who receive less or receive nothing at the expense of those who receive more, in order to ensure greater equity in the distribution of aid between producers, countries and productions and to support small and mediumsized farmers and family farming. we believe that the european commission should make a new proposal to create a genuine, compulsory modulation, making it more equitable and freeing up financial resources, introducing a ceiling on aid per holding (cap) and a percentage increase in aid for farmers who receive less aid from the cap (modulation), such as proposing an increase of 15 or 20% for farmers who receive less than € 5 000 in aid and, even from this value, taking into account various situations. without this, we risk widening existing inequalities. we therefore insist that the european commission should reformulate the proposal so that a decision in this area does not end up justifying the renationalisation of the cap. that is why we voted against the report, in order to make way for a fairer proposal.
in writing. the aim of the european commission's proposal, which is confirmed in the report adopted today, is to create a public-private partnership (ppp) to develop a european air traffic management system. the setting up of this ppp sets a dangerous precedent, since it would be the first european ppp with the participation of the european community. without calling into question the continuous need to update and improve air traffic management systems to make them more reliable, accurate and, essentially, safer, given their importance for the safety of all airspace professionals and users, we believe that this objective will not be better achieved by subjecting them to the interests and pressures of the private sector. on the contrary, i did. we also regret that the amendment we support in the committee on transport and tourism (the committee responsible for drawing up an opinion) to safeguard the interests of the air traffic management staff representative bodies in the decisions to be taken by the joint undertaking's board of directors was not considered. for all these reasons, we could not support this report.
in writing. we know that the creation of the euro was a political decision which did not take into account the specific needs of the euro area members, as is shown by the differences between the euro area member countries in economic growth, unemployment rates and inflation rates compared with 2005. we have always said that with a single monetary policy, with the budgetary constraints of the stability pact, the workers would have to pay for the problems of joining the euro, in order to serve the interests of economic and financial groups. the report makes this very clear, saying that 'labour markets should be made more flexible and that those aspects of permanent employment legislation which may make adjustment in the labour market difficult should be abolished', i.e. it insists on liberalising redundancies and fixed-term contracts. it also calls for "wages to respond more rapidly to changing economic circumstances", i.e. to be reduced in line with the cycle. there can be no greater clarity of intent. the rapporteur is not satisfied with this, but he also advocates the liberalisation of services and energy, the strict application of the stability pact, and compliance with the lisbon agenda, i.e. the european liberal consensus. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. this own-initiative report aims to create a single european market for mortgage credit and to promote it across borders. the interest of banks and capital markets is high, given that in 2004 the volume of loans outstanding was eur 4.7 billion, or 45% of eu gdp, a market which is growing rapidly. the report follows the liberal line, advocating more competition in the sector, promoting european mortgages or cross-border mortgages, a secondary market for mortgage credit and the possibility of its trading on the capital market, promotion of cross-border mergers and acquisitions in the financial services sector, opening up this market to institutions other than credit institutions, guaranteeing the freedom to provide services and liberalizing these services, restrictions on the state's regulatory capacity, marketing, via the internet, of mortgage credit and access by foreign entities to databases on customer credit, including its default. it is not difficult to see the risks of all these proposals to the volatility of financial markets, putting at risk mortgaged assets, that is, the savings of many workers and others in purchasing housing. that's why i'm voting against it.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, reading the legislative programme and hearing the presentation of the commission's work for 2007, we can only conclude that we are facing more of the same. the same neoliberalism that is calling into question social and labour rights, that is increasing the precariousness of work, that is resuming old exploitation processes, that is promoting the liberalisation of services, including public services, making clear what was intended with the so-called lisbon strategy. in the name of flexibility, the creation of an internal market, globalisation, contractual ties are being destroyed, and the threat of more relocations of multinationals such as gm opel from azambuja, johnson controls from nelas and portalegre, lear from valongo, to name just a few of the most serious cases that are currently threatening thousands of portuguese workers, whose unemployment is already very high after the layoffs in the textile, clothing and footwear sectors. but it is these same unemployed workers who are now at the mercy of the exploitation of temporary work enterprises and other unscrupulous employers, such as the recent cases reported in the media of portuguese workers in the south of the netherlands who are hungry, without pay and without food. is this corporate social responsibility? but at the same time, in the name of the single currency and price stability, the european central bank is imposing constant interest rate increases and the governments are using the stability pact to undermine production, block social development, undermine micro and small enterprises and create the culture that favors this shameful exploitation of workers, whether migrants or immigrants and their families. what is needed is a break with these neoliberal policies. it is time to give priority to policies of social development and the welfare of the people and i ask for solidarity with these cases of portuguese workers who are hungry and exploited, such as those which have just been reported in the south of the netherlands.
