the following is the oral question to the commission on games of chance and sports betting in the internal market, tabled by arlene mccarthy on behalf of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection (o-0118/2006 - b6-0443/2006).
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the exclusion of gambling from the services directive, in particular lotteries, but not only, seemed to have brought some clarification in this sector, but we will have to go further. we know that certain types of gambling are complicated, and it is therefore necessary not only to ensure consumer protection but also to ensure effective supervision of the financial circuits linked to these activities in order to prevent or combat money laundering. of course, we cannot confuse adequate consumer protection with undue protectionism that some state wants or is using, but it is worth recalling in any case the right of each member state to regulate the phenomenon of gambling on its territory until another legal instrument appears at european level, and online gambling would in this case deserve special attention from the commission, as it already deserves from parliament, as has been said and shown in this debate. finally, i welcome the fact that the committee on the internal market and consumer protection has raised this matter and that we have made some progress in clarifying it tonight.
mr president, apart from some amendments, against which i shall vote tomorrow, this report, in the form in which it has reached this house, is in general a statement of correct principles which have been acquired over the years, and in particular since the year 2000, which was designated the european year of languages. but the extent to which some of these principles are put into practice is the extent to which they are possible in connection with the subsidiarity rule, and if it is true that everyone has the right to his mother tongue, it is no less true that, in practice, applying this principle to the letter and beyond the official languages would block the entire functioning of the union's institutions. on the other hand, we must avoid exploiting the question of so-called minority languages for the purpose of potentially exacerbating it in a nationalist way. the issue of extending the european language proficiency indicator is also discussed. in its current version, it is only intended to measure proficiency in english, french, german, spanish and italian. it is important to avoid that this situation actually misleads and encourages the general learning of only these five languages. not only because of the necessary balance and legitimate scope, but also because the projection of european languages outside europe is a factor of the greatest importance in an era of globalisation, beyond its historical, human and cultural dimensions. the portuguese language - and i will give this example - is the third most widely spoken language in the european union, after english and spanish and before german, french and italian, so, as in written declaration 58, which i am one of the proponents of, i welcome the principle introduced in the report under consideration, that the european indicator of linguistic competence should include all the official languages of the union and, if this proves feasible, the other languages spoken in europe.
today, it is an invaluable milestone for european languages spoken throughout the world, such as portuguese, whose role and importance are recognised by the european parliament. recitals e and f and paragraph 3, which i proposed, establish the high degree of strategic importance to be accorded, within the framework of the european policy of multilingualism, to languages which, like portuguese, have the particular ability to enable direct communication with other parts of the world. this resolution recognises that europe cannot close in on itself but must look to the rest of the world and to the ability to communicate on a global scale. and some languages are precious tools in that regard. a greater balance and strategic sense have been ensured, by giving due value to languages such as portuguese, which have a wide global distribution. the door is open to demanding greater active promotion of the teaching and learning of languages which have this potential and which should thus be promoted in the eu as second, third or fourth languages of learning. i am grateful for the support of my colleagues, the openness of the rapporteur and, in particular, the availability of our shadow rapporteur, erna hennicot-schoepges, whose help was crucial to the successful conclusion of this initiative.
for unice (the largest employer in europe), the agreement reached in the council on the bolkenstein directive represents an 'important' and 'promising' step forward, and it should therefore be 'correctly and timely transposed and implemented', to which unice and its national members - in portugal, the aip and the cip - will 'contribute actively'. this is the view of the representatives of the major economic and financial groups who see in this 'step' new opportunities for exploiting workers and economic domination, undermining the sovereignty of states in defining, protecting and financing public services and in defining the rules for how services in general should be provided, while at the same time strengthening the power of supranational entities over the member states, such as the european commission and the court of justice, by imposing the primacy of competition, with very serious consequences for the rights of workers and the services provided to the population. this is an unacceptable proposal. it must be rejected. finally, it is only necessary to underline the role of the social democrats (socialists) who, with their 'tactical' tricks, helped to whitewash the aims and scope of the proposal for a directive under vote: initially proposing the directive; (pseudo) amending it; finally (re) supporting now what they said they rejected before.
in writing. i voted in favour of the joan i marí report on a new strategic framework for multilingualism despite my reservations about some of the proposals and amendments that have been adopted. i believe that the european strategy for multilingualism should include the teaching and dissemination of 'european languages of universal communication', such as portuguese, which is the third most widely spoken eu language in the world (after english and spanish and before german, french and italian). the uniqueness of the portuguese language, which is spoken by some 200 million citizens in eight countries across five continents, requires a special place in the eu's official languages, a status that is not recognised in this report as it should be. the portuguese language is the most enduring link between the various continents. as a means of communication and the raw material of great poets and prose writers, and also because it is endowed with the dignity conferred by eight hundred years of history.
in writing. i congratulate my colleague bernat joan i marí on his important and timely report on a new strategic framework for multilingualism, which i support, particularly as regards the measures proposed to promote multilingualism in europe. the existence of several languages in europe is a specific feature of the process of european integration and a basic element of european culture. the learning of several languages, in particular the lisbon strategy's goal of 'mother tongue + 2', should be encouraged as a means of facilitating communication between peoples and acceptance of differences between peoples.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because multilingualism is a subject which is dear to me and because i believe that the european union must give a clear and strong signal in favour of linguistic diversity within its borders. more specifically, as regards the european language competence indicator, mentioned in this report and on which i have made a written statement, i repeat the same argument here. the adoption of a language competence indicator is necessary in the absence of real data on the language skills of eu citizens. however, this indicator should not be restricted to the five most widely spoken languages in the eu. the european union must take account of the importance of the other european languages outside europe, which is a major factor in its policy of openness and cooperation with the rest of the world. that is why my vote on amendment no 4 is an insistence that the commission should present a concrete timetable for the extension of the indicator to all the official languages of the european union - as the written statement i have presented advocates.
in writing. i welcome the fact that in the new strategic framework for multilingualism parliament welcomes my contribution to the recognition of the strategic importance and global relevance of the european languages of universal communication. in fact, english is the official language of 350 million people worldwide. for 280 million, the spanish. for 230 million, the portuguese. and for 125 million, the frenchman. these numbers and the geographical dispersion of speakers make clear the importance of european languages as having a global projection and, therefore, the ability to maintain and deepen direct relations and contacts, without mediation, with other parts of the world. on the other hand, i know that the critics of the european option of multilingualism often claim that its cost is one of the factors which should contribute to its elimination and replacement by one or a few working languages. it's useless to deny that the cost exists. but despite the repeated presentation of financial arguments, it should be remembered that this is one of the most typical and noble costs of modern european construction. it's probably a lot cheaper than war. it is also a powerful cultural asset.
in writing. what has just happened with the adoption of this directive is particularly serious. we regret that the proposal to reject the council's common position, which our group has tabled and which we support, has been rejected. what has happened today is a genuine capitulation by the two largest political groups - the pse and the ppe - to their position at the first reading last february. they did not even defend the agreement they had then made and voted on, after the struggles and demonstrations in strasbourg. now they are going back to some of the more negative aspects of the infamous bolkestein directive. what they want is the liberalisation of services, including public services, giving in to the pressure of the big economic and financial groups who see in this 'step' new opportunities for exploiting workers and economic dominance. while seeking to undermine the sovereignty of states in defining, protecting and financing public services, it removes the possibility of defining rules for financing and defending services in general, reinforcing the power of supranational entities such as the european commission. we believe that each country should retain the sovereign right to decide on the public services it wants, their public ownership, their financing and organisation, and the rights of workers and users.
in writing. it took 50 years for the eu to achieve the free movement of services enshrined in the treaty of rome (1957). it's now about to become a reality. with the services directive, the eu is taking another step in the right direction towards facilitating the freedom of establishment and the provision of services in the eu member states provided by the internal market. controversial from the very beginning, when the bolkestein directive was still in force, the final text finally dilutes the initial impetus. i believe, however, that this report has struck the balance between the imperative need to open up the services sector to competition while preserving the european social model. i voted in favour of this directive because i believe that portugal has everything to gain from the benefits of the directive and thus from the full potential of the internal market. the mere fact that a whole set of administrative and legal procedures imposed by national, regional and local authorities has been eliminated has made the directive worth adopting. portuguese companies, especially smes, will be the main beneficiaries. the adoption of the directive also contributes to the achievement of the lisbon strategy's objectives of more growth, more employment and more choice of services for consumers.
in recent years we have seen the erosion of the most important legal instruments for combating the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. the biological and toxic weapons convention is no exception. we are now more vulnerable than ever to devastating terrorist attacks. the main ideas of this resolution - which reflects a remarkable consensus among all the political groups in the european parliament - are decades old and also applicable to other conventions. it can be summed up in three key words: universalization, application, verification. the notorious cluster bombs must be fought like the new anti-personnel mines. these immoral weapons should also be made illegal. the fact that they spread death in a random way and have a low rate of immediate detonation means that long after the conflicts have ended, these bombs continue to kill innocent people. the recent war in lebanon, in which israel left that country mined with hundreds of thousands of cluster bombs, should force our consciences to ban once and for all, as we have already done with anti-personnel mines, the production, transfer and use of all types of cluster bombs. perhaps the mere addition of a new protocol to the existing convention against certain conventional weapons is not enough, perhaps a specific convention is already needed, it does not matter, as long as the european union is mobilized and humanity unites to eradicate these hideous weapons.

the report by mr von wogau, which i welcome, is ambitious. it is a report which recognises that, despite the progress that has been made in the area of european security and defence, there is still much to be done and i agree with what the rapporteur has said here today; the process of building a security and defence union has the potential to bring european citizens closer together again. the eurobarometer figures are clear: 77% of europeans support a european security and defence policy. even in the united kingdom, where mr van orden comes from, and where some of the most vocal eurosceptics in this house come from, support is 59%. but the ambition of this report has its limits. although it courageously advocates the creation of a european budget also for the union's military activities, although it advocates the strengthening of the role of the european parliament and national parliaments in the scrutiny of european security and defence policy and although it even urges that progress in this area proposed by the constitutional treaty not be set aside, this report merely reiterates support for the initiatives of the council and the commission in the crucial areas of industrial integration and the creation of a european defence equipment market. i regret that this report does not go any further and i am in favour of the introduction of the principle of european preference in the field of defence equipment. what is at stake in the long term is the strategic autonomy of the european union and the european parliament has never been able to present its own vision in this area. madam president, we should not be blinded by the dogma of the market. it is essential that we do not forget what none of our friends and partners around the world do, the strategic and political implications of this industrial area.
the rapporteur. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank all the political groups for their important contributions to the preparation of this report, which have made it substantially better. the presence of women in international political life has increased. it is enough to recall chancellor angela merkel, president michelle bachelet, president ellen johnson-sirleaf and prime ministers han myeong-sook of south korea and luisa diogo of mozambique. the european union itself is now presided over by a woman, tarja halonen from finland, but a close look reveals that women's political representation is still unsatisfactory, both at global and european level and in each member state, and gathering the figures to compile this report was not easy, which has a dark meaning. at the global level, despite the beijing declaration and platform for action, despite the millennium development goals, the 191 member countries of the united nations today have only 10 women as heads of state or government and only 16% of parliamentarians worldwide are women. at the un, only 9 women are among the 91 envoys or representatives of the secretary-general. despite security council resolution 1325, adopted six years ago, inequality continues to mark the composition of international bodies and missions involved in conflict prevention and resolution. three weeks ago, the security council held a debate on women, peace and security to gauge progress in the implementation of resolution 1325. all agreed that much remains to be done to turn good intentions and rhetoric into reality. the debate resulted in recommendations to integrate more women into peacekeeping missions and thus improve the effectiveness and operability of such missions. the urgent need for a cultural change in the office of the assistant secretary-general himself, who is responsible for peacekeeping operations, was also advocated. our report contains recommendations which go in the same direction. let's move to the european level. despite resolution 2025 and others in this parliament, and the lisbon strategy, we still do not have a european commission with equal composition and we have only 7 women among the current 107 heads of delegation of the european commission around the world. in the council, there is only one woman among the 14 personal representatives of the high representative of the european union for foreign affairs and security policy. however, qualified, experienced and competent women abound in the member states and in the european institutions. at virtually every level of decision-making, except at the top, there are signs that the glass ceilings are beginning to crack, but they have not yet been broken, because it is indeed only at the top of the ladder, in power, in europe that women continue to be scandalously underrepresented. at national level, the pioneering example is the government of josé luis zapatero in spain. in a world where political engineering has historically tended to obstruct women's participation in the centers of political and economic power, this is a model example. it demonstrates that peer democracy is possible and much depends on enlightened political leadership. the conclusions of this report are simple: inequalities of opportunity at the european and national level require action in all these areas. firstly, the un and its secretary-general, through a human resources policy which should set an example to the world; secondly, the european union, through support for international european women's networks and human resources policies which ensure a balanced presence of men and women in the centres of political and economic decision-making. in this respect, it is positive that the council has just sent a questionnaire to the member states to find out how they have implemented resolution 1325. thirdly, governments should encourage and put forward more female candidates for political positions at national, european and international level, they should ensure that electoral systems produce democratic institutions with balanced representation, no democratic institution should have a composition of less than 40% or more than 60% of any sex. quotas and other balancing mechanisms which are necessary for women today may be necessary for men tomorrow. without equal representation, democracy is incomplete and does not function properly. the impact of laws and measures that allow men and women to better balance and share family and professional responsibilities is also decisive in this respect. finally, political parties should promote women's participation by setting up quotas or other mechanisms to correct the imbalance, including specific training for women to pursue a political career. the momentum for change depends on the quality of party political leadership. for example, in my country, portugal, certain careers were only opened up to women after the fall of the dictatorship in 1974, such as the judiciary, diplomacy and the armed forces and security, professions which could provide many more candidates for all kinds of european and international missions and posts. since 1974, the presence of women in these careers has made extraordinary progress, but the advance is not replicated in the top positions of these careers, such as in government or party decision-making centres. the glass ceilings are evident, despite the overwhelming presence of qualified women in academia, in public administration and in the workforce in general. a parity law impacting the electoral lists of political parties has recently been passed and practical results are expected. there is indeed a way forward and on that way we need to not just focus on numbers, we need to recognise and highlight the qualitative difference that women's representation in politics makes in shaping government agendas, in resolving conflicts in transparency and accountability, in short, in strengthening the rule of law and democracy.
i would like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur on her excellent report, which deals with a very topical and relevant subject, because women are still underrepresented in national and european political life, as indeed they are in the european parliament itself. it is not understood that women are more numerous in universities, that there are more and more women with master's degrees and doctorates and that they have very little access to the decision-making bodies or to economic power. from a certain level, there's always a glass ceiling that prevents them from progressing. parity is a requirement of democracy itself. experience has shown that only a quota system has led to a more equal society, and therefore to a more just and harmonious society. member states need to adopt laws to ensure parity. i will end, madam president, with a rhetorical question: how different would the world be if it were ruled by a majority of women? and would europe be any different?
on behalf of the ppe-de group. human trafficking is the modern form of slavery. it is not a recent phenomenon, but it has been growing in recent years and is assuming alarming proportions. the ilo, for example, estimates that there are some 2.5 million forced workers worldwide. this form of trafficking is already the third most lucrative, right after drug and arms trafficking, and it translates into the sexual exploitation already mentioned here, but also for the purpose of labor under abusive conditions, forced domestic servitude, illegal adoption, forced begging and organ sales. the fight strategies should be promoted. trafficking in human beings is unacceptable and cannot be facilitated by the existence of legislative gaps. the legislation must be clear and comprehensive and implemented and correctly applied by all member states. there must be a legislative platform that provides the basis for more intensive cooperation at international level, and i cannot but regret that trafficking in human beings is a heinous crime which degrades the human condition in a particularly insidious way. unfortunately, it has become one of the most lucrative forms of international organized crime, affecting hundreds of thousands of people worldwide every year, with a particular focus on the most vulnerable, the poor, women and children. the fight against this scourge must be a top priority. for this to be successful, international cooperation in the fields of investigation, information exchange, victim identification, law enforcement and reintegration must be strengthened. in this regard, the various member states which have not yet done so should speed up the process of ratifying and implementing the many existing international conventions which can play a decisive role in the progressive eradication of this absolutely intolerable criminal practice. the european union must also strengthen its commitment to promoting initiatives to tackle the causes of such a bad trade, by providing effective support to the weaker countries where much of this trafficking originates. we are all fully aware, as we are discussing this matter here today, of the enormous difficulty of the fight we must wage together, but we are also all aware and very firmly convinced that what is at stake in this fight is a boundary between the dignity and the abjection of the human person, and there is therefore no more urgent fight than this, ladies and gentlemen.

in writing. we consider the report to be generally positive, although we regret that amendments have been adopted which do not contribute to a more consistent fight against trafficking in human beings, especially women. we find it negative that the paragraphs referring to the need to 'criminalize the purchase of another person's body for sexual use' have been removed in order to reduce trafficking for sexual purposes. as several studies indicate, the prohibition of the exploitation of prostitution substantially reduces organised crime and trafficking, in particular of women and children. the report nevertheless maintains a number of positive aspects, such as the need to apply extremely severe sanctions to companies that use cheap labour through trafficking in human beings, or the need for member states to assume their responsibilities towards the victims of trafficking in human beings, in addition to effectively combating money laundering stemming from trafficking in human beings. however, we could have gone further in combating poverty at the source by means of a policy of cooperation with the countries of origin, by supporting their own projects of economic and social development, thus reducing the main causes of poverty, unemployment and social exclusion.
in writing. human trafficking is the modern day version of the slave trade, with aggravating circumstances. here poverty makes the traffickers pay for the traffickers, and the authorities, often with the best of human intentions, enact policies that encourage trafficking and promote the traffickers' business. as is often the case, humanism is on the side of the demand. demand for those who employ, demand for those who arrive, demand for those who stay and, above all, demand and rigor in the enforcement of the law. turning a blind eye to illegal immigration is complicity in human trafficking. i therefore believe that we must unhesitatingly recognise the virtues of legal immigration and, recognising that a lack of firmness in the fight against illegal immigration is the food of human trafficking networks, we must be firm in defending legality. but it's not enough to think about immigration law. an efficient - and humane - approach requires us to seek to promote the success and economic development that we enjoy in the countries of origin of immigration. that is where we must go together.

in writing. this fisheries agreement between the european community and the republic of cape verde sets out the fishing opportunities for the fleets of community countries for the period 2006 to 2011 and is an important agreement for tuna fishing, which grants fishing licences to 7 portuguese surface longliners. that's why he deserved our vote in favour. however, this agreement, as with other fisheries agreements with third countries, raises important questions as to the economic viability of long-distance fishing fleets and the real fishing opportunities granted under it, as the commercial nature of these agreements is increasingly being modified, with a stronger partnership and development component. the cost of the agreement is therefore increased by the reduction in fishing opportunities, in particular by reducing the number of licences allocated. the costs to shipowners are also rising from eur 25 to eur 35 per tonne of tuna caught by the fence and longliners, which is exacerbating the difficulties in the use of these licences by shipowners, the supply of the industry at national level and the growing external deficit for fishery products.

mr president, i extend a special greeting to you, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen. i would naturally like to welcome this initiative and also congratulate the rapporteurs on the quality of the work they have done. i welcome this initiative, which is of the utmost importance, given that the code currently in force dates back to 1992. its modernisation was necessary to reflect the changes that had occurred in the meantime and to react to many of these changes. there are two aspects which i think are essential: firstly, this new code makes it possible to contribute to the promotion of international trade because, by simplifying processes, it can lead to an increase in the competitiveness of european companies and thus contribute to the strengthening of economic growth. in this sense, openness to new technologies, the exploitation and even the imposition of the use of new technologies is a very significant advance which can certainly contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of the european economy. however, there is a second aspect which cannot be overlooked and which has to do with the new nature of the functions assigned to customs in modern times. this aspect has to do with the need to increase safety at various levels in order to protect public health, ensure food safety and combat more effectively phenomena such as money laundering, counterfeiting and fraud. in short, to better protect consumers. in conclusion, i would like to stress the following: the commission's proposal is aimed at safeguarding the interests of europeans both as producers and as consumers, and it deserves our full support.

the report i am presenting on behalf of the committee on agriculture and rural development welcomes the european commission's proposal for the possibility of adopting multiannual programmes to be submitted by the member states and the updating of some of the instruments accompanying community animal health policy. however, it considers that some of the measures contained in the proposal to amend council decision 90/424/eec are insufficient. we therefore insist on 12 amendments aimed at achieving five essential objectives: the first, noting that there is little knowledge of the state of play of the programmes for the eradication, control and monitoring of certain animal diseases in the various member states, is to propose that the commission submit every four years to the european parliament and the council a report on the animal health situation and the cost-effectiveness of the implementation of the programmes in the various member states, including an explanation of the criteria adopted. secondly, given that there are different attitudes and behaviour towards the same diseases in several neighbouring member states, which may affect the effectiveness of the measures adopted, it is proposed to support actions to disseminate good practice and to encourage the presentation of joint programmes from two or more member states in border areas, where this is important for the control of contagious animal diseases, including zoonoses, and for their surveillance and eradication. thirdly, in the face of emergency situations requiring sudden and unpredictable expenditure of very high financial resources, insist that the respective financing proposals are always made, which should not be subject to the deadlines referred to in this decision, which, in any case, should slightly increase the deadlines provided for by the european commission. take the example of the outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in the uk in 2000. in the case of these diseases, the measures imposed are all the more effective the earlier and more radical their application. this requires a minimum financial reserve to meet these sudden, insidious and unpredictable disasters. fourthly, we propose to complete the list annexed to the decision by including the animal contagious diseases for which community financial support may be granted, contrary to the commission proposal which seeks to reduce that list. the proposal contained in this report from the committee on agriculture adds eight diseases to the existing ones and proposes a few more in order to ensure that funding is also provided for their control and eradication. the proposal is of the utmost importance, since it is known that there are several countries where eradication programmes are under way and should not be interrupted. in portugal, for example, a situation i know better, bovine leucosis is a disease which has had eradication programmes for some twenty years and is in the final stage of its final eradication. very few cases of leukaemia have been found in the last year, and it is estimated that one more year of campaigning will allow the disease to be eradicated once and for all. the fact that this disease is not eligible for funding could jeopardise all the efforts made and lead to its uncontrolled resurgence. another case is newcastle disease, endemic in wild birds, which can be transmitted to unvaccinated poultry at any time. the economic consequences of this disease for poultry farming would be devastating. the aujeszky's disease of pigs, which the commission wanted to exclude, is also covered by a programme for portugal, and its non-eradication is due to the impossibility of sending pigs to some markets. other diseases such as swine brucellosis, which are not included in the list proposed by the commission, are diseases which can cause the same type of problems to trade, the latter being endemic in the mediterranean basin. fifthly, the commission also proposes, in the name of simplifying the legislation in force, the repeal of decision 90/638/eec laying down community criteria for the eradication and monitoring of certain animal diseases, replacing them by the new technical criteria contained in the annexes to the new decision which we are considering and which the commission wants to convert later into standard criteria and requirements. in this report we propose a new opinion from the european parliament in the event of a change in the criteria in force. finally, mr president, i would just like to thank everyone who has contributed to the preparation of this report and hope that the commission will take due account of the proposals put forward to help improve animal health.

in writing. this regulation sets out how to tackle and combat diseases such as bse and scrapie which affect ruminants in general. firstly, the number of categories of risk for bse has been reduced from five to three, in accordance with the recommendations of the world organisation for animal health. the use of animal protein in the feed of ruminants is prohibited, but a limit is set for the amount of animal protein to be considered insignificant in the feed. the report also calls for a review of the rules on the use of mechanically processed meat for human consumption, including new rules for better consumer information. in order to avoid mass slaughter and the consequent loss of the producer, the use of animals until the end of their productive life is also defined, obviously subject to very strict control conditions, since there are no scientific data to say that bse is transmitted through milk or from cows to their offspring. the programmes for the prevention of transmissible spongiform encephalopathies are left on a voluntary basis and a regular evaluation of the scientific results of these programmes is foreseen. the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of national authorities responsible for the protection of the environment.
in writing. the proposal, which has been submitted for second reading, differs from the legislation in force on the subject in three fundamental respects. the proposal is to provide annual data instead of monthly data. recent studies have shown that monthly data submitted up to six months after the reference month are of little use for day-to-day market monitoring, whereas annual data can be used for medium- to long-term market analyses and reduce the workload of national entities in submitting the data. it is also intended that the reporting of data should be made by flag (or nationality) of the vessels responsible for landings. this requirement, as opposed to the current submission of data by eu, efta and other vessels, will allow for more detailed data analyses, but will not significantly increase the workload of national authorities already collecting data at this level of detail. finally, this proposal for a regulation aims to make a more flexible approach to the use of sampling techniques for estimating total landings. national authorities will be allowed to use an appropriate level of sampling techniques for data collection, provided they justify their use and analyse the quality of the resulting data in a methodological report... the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used effectively. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in an attempt to deal with social emergencies in the member states of the union. the economic scourge of unemployment caused by the phenomena of globalisation is clearly one of these emergencies. with 19 million unemployed, we have to find solutions. this fund will be financed from the unused amounts of the other headings up to a maximum of eur 500 million per year, it will not have its own financing line, nor will it be able to request the advance of the fund for the following year, as happens with the solidarity fund. this is a serious matter, because we can thus leave behind situations which are clearly eligible but for which there is no financial availability. i consider this regulation to be a positive one overall. i cannot, however, fail to express my scepticism about the strict eligibility criteria laid down in article 2. we have managed to include a flexibility clause, but i am afraid that it is not sufficient to protect the situations of smaller countries or regions where, although the quantitative criterion is not met, the impact felt is extremely serious. it is urgent to contribute to an instrument which will work to preserve the european matrix, which is the european social model. to do this we must support our own workers with the globalisation adjustment fund and support workers from the rest of the world by putting social criteria as a barrier when importing certain products into the european area. only then will we be able to defend our social model and promote the interests of millions of citizens around the world by advocating fairer trade. a final note is that it is urgent to respond in a timely manner to the serious economic and social problems caused by this phenomenon.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, the commission's proposal is merely a palliative to the serious problem of the consequences of globalisation in several member states. it is well known that restructuring and relocation of multinational companies alone are causing many thousands of unemployed and blocking the development of vast regions in several countries where there are no employment alternatives. apart from the obvious insufficiency of the proposed global amount, conditions are laid down which prevent its use in practice in countries such as portugal, which is experiencing a serious situation of relocation of factories of multinationals. by not allowing the fund to be used when there are restructuring and relocations within the european union, support is being prevented for workers in the known cases of opel-azambuja, which is going to relocate to spain, and the same could happen to others, such as johnson controls, which is threatening to go to romania, lear and so many others who are relocating to poland and other countries of the european union. so in reality this fund is a symbolic measure with no solutions. its budget is limited and the eligibility criteria are restrictive. the european commission estimates that between 35,000 and 50,000 workers could benefit from the fund, but it was not until 2005 that the number of workers made redundant as a result of restructuring exceeded 570,000, the majority of whom were restructuring within the european union. so, despite being pompously dubbed the 'global adjustment fund', it is nothing more than an attempt to hide the serious consequences for workers of the neoliberal policies pursued and implemented by the european union. the fund is not intended to prevent layoffs, factory closures, relocations, the pursuit of maximum profit at all costs, treating workers as mere numbers to be killed. the aim is simply to ease the conscience of those who promote such actions.
mr president, globalisation is the mark of our time and must be seen as a positive phenomenon, because it allows everyone to connect with everyone else, and that is good. globalization has also lifted millions out of poverty, and that is good too. in living with globalisation, europe is doing what it has always done well: opening up to other cultures. but today we must be aware that globalisation also brings with it some worrying aspects, especially for some regions of europe. the decision to create the globalisation fund, taken simultaneously by the three most important institutions of the european union, has a political connotation. for the first time, the three institutions acknowledge the existence of negative aspects of globalisation in the european area. with the closure of industrial units there are clear signs of widespread concern in layers of our societies. so we see that the concern of people today is not even to fight for more rights, but to try at least to maintain the status quo. for large sections of our society there is a feeling, which i am not afraid to call a certain fear, the fear of the future. but i think fears can only be overcome by a willingness to change. when people are restless and fearful it is very difficult to accept any kind of change. this fund, in my reading, is above all a way of helping to mobilise the most vulnerable workers for change. in my view, this instrument is not, nor does it intend to be, the miracle solution to redundancies, restructuring, closures and relocations of companies. the reason for this fund is only about people who are in a very vulnerable situation and we want them to find, as quickly as possible, a high degree of self-esteem. i congratulate the rapporteur and support this report.

in writing. i voted in favour of the sacconi report on the amendment of directive 67/548/eec on dangerous substances (reach) at second reading, because i consider the common position adopted by the council to be a good agreement, which will benefit the citizens of the european union. i think this is a moderate legislative proposal which has sought to strike a balance between safeguarding the legitimate interests of industry, particularly smes, and the necessary protection of the environment and public health. the reach regulation will ensure, as from june 2007, that substances of very high concern from an environmental and public health point of view are replaced wherever possible by safer alternative substances or technologies.
in writing. the low budgetary implementation of the structural and cohesion funds is one of the reasons for presenting this amending budget for 2006. the commission is proposing to cancel eur 2.5 billion in payment appropriations under these budget lines: eur 1.5 billion for the erdf, eur 500 million for the esf and eur 500 million for the cohesion fund. regardless of the situation underlying the commission's proposal to cancel cohesion policy appropriations for this reduction, we find that this is a common practice. it is therefore important to look seriously at the reasons for this reduced budgetary implementation and not to allow this proper assessment - for example, on the impact of the nominal criteria enshrined in the stability pact on public investment in the different member states, as well as on the reduction of member states' contributions to the community budget - to be used as an argument for reducing the funds provided annually in the community budget for the structural and cohesion funds.
in writing. the aim is to amend this directive on the grounds of the evolution of television, but the question is how to guarantee the profitability of private television stations. there are several studies that show that people see fewer and fewer ads, since they can change channels, and therefore the times when the advertisements are broadcast are increasingly coincident across the various channels. thus, advertising revenue is not as high as it used to be, since the channels cannot guarantee the audiences to those who pay, and everything on television is measured in percentage of audiences. so we have to reinvent advertising to keep it profitable, such as through product placement, split screen, telemarketing, virtual advertising and interactive advertising. the same applies to the programme time at the end of which advertising may be broadcast. there have also been several proposals concerning advertising of high-calorie food and drink when children's programmes are broadcast. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.

in writing. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) will undoubtedly be a valuable financial instrument to respond at european level to the loss of jobs resulting from the opening up of markets and the increase in international competitive pressure. one of the main adverse effects of (economic) globalisation, in addition to the recognised benefits. i regret, however, that the purpose of the establishment of the egf, as proposed by the commission, is to enable the community to provide targeted support for the reintegration into employment of workers who have lost their jobs only because of major structural changes in world trade patterns. it does not, therefore, grasp the phenomenon of globalisation. it ignores that, in addition to the liberalisation of world trade, the liberalisation of capital movements and the deregulation of markets - which are also factors driving this phenomenon - may also be at the origin of the redundancies associated with globalisation. i have therefore tabled several amendments to the proposal, as part of the opinion of the committee on regional development, which is chaired by mrs jamila madeira. the report in question, while maintaining the scope of the egf, introduces a number of amendments to the commission proposal which significantly improve, complete and clarify it. that is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. unfortunately, the proposals we have put forward to improve the eligibility criteria and, above all, the possibility of granting aid in the event of relocation outside the european union have not been adopted, which could create a feeling of injustice among workers made redundant as a result of relocation or restructuring within the european union. the rejection of our proposals has made it clearer that by creating this fund the european union wants to give the impression to workers that it is committed to combating the negative effects of globalisation, but in reality it is a symbolic measure with no solutions. its budget is limited and the eligibility criteria are restrictive. the commission itself estimates that between 35 000 and 50 000 workers could benefit from this fund, but only up to 2005 the number of workers made redundant as a result of restructuring exceeded 57 000 and the majority of these were restructuring within the european union, which, according to the fund's criteria, are not eligible. we therefore abstained from the final vote.

in writing. as we are used to, the majority in the european parliament approves a report which is based on the idea that enlargement of the eu should be made possible by ensuring and even deepening federalism, that is, by ensuring the dominance of the great powers in the eu decision-making process and, in this way, the imposition of the interests of its major economic and financial groups. the report begins by making the demagogic premise that institutional reform is necessary to ensure the 'effectiveness' and 'functioning' of the eu institutions. after a list of reforms, it is not surprising that he ends up where he wanted to be: defending the incorrectly named 'european constitution'. the report also clarifies what the real purpose of resuming the so-called constitutional process is: insisting on the content of the draft treaty which has already been rejected. this is why the usual panoply of measures aimed at centralising power in supranational bodies dominated by the great powers is introduced: a new weighting of votes and the end of the rotation of the council presidencies, the extension of the 'qualified majority', the 'minister for foreign affairs', the end of one commissioner per country in the commission or unanimity in amending the treaties. this is unacceptable!
in writing. you don't take home someone who doesn't have a home to take home. if by 'absorption capacity' is meant, then i am - as i have said many times - in complete agreement. the union, as it enlarges, must be able to absorb new entrants and accommodate the changes that follow. that is the sense in which i am voting in favour of this report. worse than disappointing the expectations of those hoping to join the community, it would be to disappoint those who are joining and those who are already there. let us look at our capacity to accept new member states before each enlargement. but they do not count on our support to twist this concept into something it is not: a euphemism to keep out. finally, i would like to reiterate what i have said: the eu's capacity to enlarge will obviously be limited; but the ability to produce the same effects would be better off not. the first is our neighbours on the mediterranean coast. if we are not able to absorb them logically, we are able to "integrate" them into our space in a new and much broader sense of the term.

it is clear that, as the social problems in the european union are growing, there is increasing pressure to move forward with the development of neoliberal policy, with the disastrous consequences that we know of, unemployment, precarious work, poverty and social inequalities. on the contrary, what is emerging is the emphasis on immigration policy, the attempt to extend the application of qualified majority voting, on the grounds that it facilitates policies in this area, but in fact to apply more security mechanisms. the same applies to institutional questions, with the aim of moving towards a revision of the european constitution. it is symptomatic that in our meetings with the representatives of the future presidencies, especially germany, the institutional question comes first, followed by the completion of the internal market and energy. the way in which they devalue social and environmental issues is also symptomatic, and there is no thought of revising the statutes and guidelines of the european central bank, despite the serious consequences of its policy on the weakest economies, households and micro and smes.

we are confident that tomorrow's vote will confirm the completion of the legislative procedure on the adoption of a european driving licence. i would like to begin by congratulating mr grosch on his excellent work. he has conducted this long process with the qualities of dialogue and efficiency that enabled him to reach a compromise which, while not reflecting the views of the various countries and the community institutions, has managed to maintain consistency on a matter which affects, as he has rightly recalled, about two thirds of europe's adult population. my main concern was that a good idea would be undermined by excessive regulation without any benefits for road safety. however, the consensus reached on the main points of the directive allows us to look to the future with optimism. the text seems to have generally achieved its objectives, while taking account of the principle of subsidiarity and respecting many of the practices which are legitimately established by the member states. this positive idea will enable european citizens to be guided by clearer and more uniform rules which favour mobility and road safety, prevent fraud by the misuse of false cards and enable more effective control of offenders. the new directive will thus reach its intended audience in a simple and easily understandable way (i hope) and we can expect citizens to adopt it without any great difficulty. it should be clear that our aim is to make life easier for citizens and the various operators in the sector and at the same time to promote safer road traffic. finally, i refer to the controversial issue of a phased and progressive access to motorcycling and the imposition of a minimum age of 24 for the most powerful motorcycles in the absence of previous experience. i recognize as a motorcyclist (i am an old motorcyclist!) that age is not the only indicator of maturity and a sense of responsibility on the road, but combined with experience it is the best indicator the law can use. the truth is that there are motorcycles on the market that can achieve performance close to that of a formula 1 car. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the directive is implemented. i, for one, would never make them available to a child of my own age. i therefore express my support for the solution found in the name of protecting the most vulnerable motorists, who are the youngest and youngest citizens.
mr president, mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, we all know that sis ii is an important instrument. commissioner frattini has just reminded us. the free movement within the community and the absence of internal borders oblige us to strengthen the security of the union's external borders, and this can only be done by sharing information between all the members of the schengen area. commissioner frattini also said, and i agree with him, that sis ii is not just a new generation of the schengen information system. we can say that it is a new schengen information system: it has new functions, it has new users, it imports new data. beyond the technical issues of building a new system there is a political issue. this political issue has to do with the legitimate ambition of the new member states to join the schengen area as soon as possible. for the new member states this is a key issue, whether or not they can offer their citizens the opportunity of free movement within the community area. to be in the schengen area you need to enter the sis. as we know, the sis is not a sufficient condition, that is, it is not enough to enter the sis to be in the schengen area. there are a number of other requirements that must be met. but it's a necessary condition. we cannot be in the schengen area without being in the schengen information system. the creation of sis ii must therefore be a priority for us, and that is why - and commissioner frattini is a privileged witness because he has always stood by parliament in this endeavour - we have endeavoured to conclude, at first reading, the adoption of the legal basis for sis ii. it was so that, because of the legal basis, we would not have a longer delay in sis ii and i would like to thank optimistic version. i was very pleased to hear vice-president frattini say that in february 2007 he will present the final timetable to parliament and that he expects only a delay of six to eight months. i must say that this forecast is much better than the information that was circulating and that we were worried about. it is still a delay, but it is a much more comfortable delay than the one we had feared. i hope you are right, although some people think we may have to face longer delays. in any event, the commissioner will know that parliament never relinquishes its powers of control. we in writing. the decision to create a fund for the union's external borders comes at a good time. while it is true that the borders of each state are within the strict limits of national sovereignty, the truth is that when these borders are also the external borders of the european union, there is a dual nature which must be recognised and treated accordingly. in a time of increased risks - whether it is the threat of terrorism, illegal immigration or economic crime - the need to strengthen borders is imperative. it is not, however, the building of walls around europe or the construction of a fortress continent. this is a matter of sharing a part of a burden whose cost is partly the result of being part of the european union. it's only fair. let us hope above all that it is effective.

in writing. we must ensure the protection of personal data and prevent their misuse. everyone has the right to privacy and to his or her identity. the increasing cooperation between judicial and police authorities in combating transnational crime is increasing the flow of personal data. we have called for these exchanges of information to respect fundamental rights such as respect for private life and the protection of personal data and to strengthen mutual trust between the competent authorities in the police and judicial fields. we want a framework decision that is close to what is established for the first pillar. it makes no sense that our union has a high level of protection of personal data in the first pillar and legislates substantially differently in relation to the third pillar. a high level of protection should be ensured, taking into account the specific nature of police and judicial work. this matter has been dragged from one presidency to another and the council has unfortunately shown itself to be unable to reach a decision. the council should be aware that this framework decision is linked to several proposals currently under consideration by the ep, such as the vis, although it believes that these should not be held hostage to the adoption of the framework decision.

in writing. the green paper on a european strategy for sustainable, competitive and secure energy is the basis for the action plan for the european energy strategy, to be presented in early 2007. this document is of great importance as it plays a key role in issues such as combating climate change, environmental pollution, the misuse of natural resources and the security of energy supply. the report sets out very clear objectives: a 20% share of energy produced in the eu from renewable sources by 2020 and 50% by 2040; a 30% reduction in european carbon emissions by 2020 and a minimum of 60% by 2050. the objective set by the green paper on energy efficiency of reducing european consumption by 20% by 2020 is also recalled. in the field of renewable energy, the focus is on marine resources (waves, tides and the enormous potential of offshore wind) and solar energy. the commission is also asked to undertake an independent analysis of the potential and the shortcomings of nuclear energy and its generating stations. in writing. despite its shortcomings and even some contradictions, there are positive aspects in this report, particularly in the area of the defence of alternative and renewable energies. however, we insist that it must be borne in mind that biofuels are not in a position to solve the serious problems of energy dependence in a lasting way, as they have a localized technical interest and a limited impact. moreover, the production of biomass and biofuels should not replace the main function of agriculture: food production. the devastating effects of the production of various oilseeds in third world countries are recalled, in particular with the destruction of vast areas of forest, oilseeds which constitute the raw material for the production of biofuels in europe. we therefore do not support the excessive emphasis on the promotion of energy crops which are the basis for obtaining biofuels, since such crops use scarce production factors such as water and soil, as well as various fertilizers. we therefore consider that the most important thing would be community support for the promotion of biomass and biofuels produced from various types of organic waste, such as forestry waste, waste from waste water treatment, solid and municipal waste and edible oils.
